title: Compact and efficient for small homes.
text: So, I ordered it, fretted over the price and it arrived late. The box was damaged. The main canister was warped. See photos below. $599 for a warped canister? German engineering and quality? I think not! To say I was very upset is an understatement. I had already been through this with regular Dysons, awful refurbished Dysons and another brand I won't even bother to mention made overseas. So, I calmed down and gave it another go. Amazon made me "less angry" in that they sent a replacement immediately without receiving the damaged one so I could vacuum ASAP and rightfully emphasized that I would be billed twice if the first vacuum did not return to Amazonland. However, due to the hype and price, it was not love at first sweep. Others have said this as well in the reviews. Perhaps I was unjustly expecting the earth to actually move underneath the Miele. Yet I must admit, it cleaned my low to medium carpets and hardwood floors quietly, beautifully and with little effort on my part.  It doesn't topple over unless you move abrubtly and tug at it. It is compact for storage which I need. I didn't need to read a thing to set it up and it took five minutes from the time I opened the box before it was up and running. The red little titan is the best vacuum I have purchased in years. It is not a life altering vacuum, but I suspect if your expectations are for a vacuuming revolution you may be a wee bit unrealistic.  Like others say, the cord is too short but I can adapt. The tools fit in it a bit awkwardly but I am happy. My house is immaculate and I look forward to vacuuming again tomorrow. Thank you Amazon and Miele, I am" in like" with my vacuum and look forward to a non dysfunctional relationship with it for years to come.

title: Decent, pretty little teapot
text: This teapot is smaller than I originally expected it to be, but this is just because the pictures have little else in them to show the scale; the description of how many ounces it holds, and the fact that it is listed as a "tea-for-one" set, are accurate. I actually find that the pot holds two very good-sized cups of tea when filled up. I have not used it on the stovetop, so I can't say how well it works for that, but I find that it is perfectly adequate for making loose-leaf tea by pouring in already-boiled water. The pot is also very pretty, pours nicely without splattering or dripping, and is not too heavy to hold in one hand, even when full. The handle is also big enough to put your fingers through and hold securely. The only minor issue with this pot is the fact that the lid sticks in the basket a bit, so it can be hard to remove without pulling the whole basket out. I think this is meant to be a feature, since you can easily lift the basket and tea leaves out when they finish steeping by picking up the lid, but I find it somewhat annoying since the mouth of the pot is far too large for the lid to go on it without the basket, and I usually prefer to keep a lid on my teapot. Instead, I end up leaving the whole basket and lid in the pot and just pouring the tea out of it when it's done steeping, which works out fine since I'm only making a cup or two at a time. Any loose-leaf drinker looking for a decent little teapot at a good price will probably like this pot a lot.

text: Well, I always wanted a mandolin slicer, but could never bring myself to spend $150+ dollars on a good stainless steel one.  Then I found this one and it had pretty good reviews on Amazon.  But alas, after 4 uses in 6 weeks, it has continued to disappoint and now I passed my window of return. title: Quality, No Brainer Timer
text:
I needed a timer. How hard can it be to find a timer, right? I chose this timer because of the description, reviews, and perceived quality through pictures. BEFORE I received the timer, I received an email with some simple tips and an easy way to reach the company IF I had issues or wasn't satisfied. One tip emailed to me was to turn the timer off on the side using black mini switch. This saves battery and was good to know. I have had no issues or need to call the company. The timer works just as expected but better.

When it arrived, I was immediately impressed with the sturdiness and the feel. It's quality for the money and let's face it, lately, products on Amazon have been subpar lately. I just had a baby shower and ordered lots off Amazon and I've had to send three things back in a week (which I hate doing so you know they were bad). Not this timer though.

I needed a it to make waffles for my waffle bar at the baby shower. I set the timer fo 5 minutes, and each time it goes off, I hit the stop button and it sets the last time automatically so I can keep cooking instead of setting the timer repeatedly.

I store mine on the fridge using the strong magnets on the back. When I use it for cooking or time-outs, I use the stand which is sturdy and doesn't feel like it will break at all (and I have heavy hands). And setting it is a no-brainer. I hate reading directions and I had no issue to figure it out. My faith is renewed in buying on Amazon for the moment based on this purchase.

title: Waste of Money!
text: I don't understand how this juicer even gets 2 stars at all!  This juicer is a waste of money and I am returning it.  The Breville510XL is not my first Breville juicer, it is actually my second.  My first Breville juicer, the 98XL was a piece of junk too because the pulp was always so wet and huge chunk of fruits and vegetables were always in the pulp bin.  I upgraded to this juicer hoping for an improvement.  What a disappointment!  The only thing good about this juicer is how it looks, but that is not my reason for buying a juicer.  From the very first use I knew I was going to return the juicer.  I am not new to juicing.  I have been juicing for a long time.  I am pretty good at estimating how much juice I will yield base on the amount of fruits and veggies that I use.  I was very surprised of the amount of juice I got, especially since all the veggies and fruits I was juicing were the types that produce a lot of juice.  I mostly juice cucumbers, celery, apple, carrots, romaine lettuce, etc.  Anyway, when I went to check the pulp bin I knew exactly where my money was going!  It was going in the trash bin.  The pulp was extremely wet with huge chunk that were never even grind.  I knew immediately that this juicer was not worth my money.  I ran the pulp back in the juicer numerous times to see if I could get more juice out.  The amount of time it took me to make so little juice was ridiculous!  Let me not even get started on the amount of foam that was in the juice.  It was foam galore!  I base my opinion on a juicer according to the amount of juice I get, how much time I spend doing the juice, how wet the pulp is, and how easy it is to clean.  I did not have any problem cleaning the juicer.  But everything else was a disappointment.  My search for a decent juicer continues.  I do not mind paying higher for a juicer as long as it works.  I have learned my lesson well with Berville juicers and will never buy another one.  I absolutely would NOT recommend this juicer.  This is a complete waste of money.

title: whatever I'm weighing only to have to take some back out because the update lag it has which is by far the most annoying fault.
text:
I bought this scale in 2012 and a few issues have made me decide to write a review on it. Overall it does the job and is decent and priced well but there are some small irritants that potential buyers may want to know.

-It is very slow to update the weight. Often times I end up adding more flour, coffee, whatever I'm weighing only to have to take some back out because the update lag it has which is by far the most annoying fault.
-It times out and shuts off rather quickly which can often leave you in the middle of an operation not knowing what your weight is at (in my experience, pouring coffee after a pre-soak).
-It does not do well with rechargeable batteries (eneloops in my case). When using rechargeables, it thinks the batteries are low very quickly (seems to not deal with the voltage drop of rechargeables very well). Which causes you to very frequently need to charge the batteries. With standard batteries it lasts quite a while though.

I would rather have spent a bit more for a scale that does not exhibit these problems.

title: Great fan, a bit short.
text:
I bought this fan after moving into a new home and certain rooms always seemed to stay 3-4 degrees higher than the rest of the house. It fit the bill perfectly. Comparing it to the last fan we had (A Lasko remote-controlled fan), it blows it away.

It moves about the same amount of air and is far quieter, while being much easier to use and clean. The remote in particular is very convenient as it even controls the oscillation. The only real complaint I have is that it's a bit short (even if the tilt makes up for that). The breeze options seem a bit gimmicky unless you're really sensitive to that sort of thing, but it's nice to have. If only you could control the tilt by remote as well, you would never have to get up!

Pros:
Metal grate that is easy to remove and clean
Easy to use and feature-packed remote control
Sturdy base that is tightened on (unlike others)
Quiet (compared to other fans, at least)

Cons:
It's a bit short
The bolt that holds the fan on is red, not black like the fan itself. (some in the family like it, so that's up to you.)

title: With proper care, the softness lives on!
text:
I LOVE this blanket! The best way to describe the softness is... if you could feel a whisper, that's what this blanket feels like. I have considered purchasing several and keeping them in storage because, as with most things, they will stop making them, and I'll kick myself for not ordering more. Then running the risk of it living on in legend only, much to the dismay of bored relatives and friends who eventually get tired of hearing about this seemingly mythical thing they can't feel for themselves.

Anyway, I have washed it once, but after reading comments here, decided to try a different approach when it came to drying it so that it wouldn't destroy the softness. After washing it in a gentle cycle, I put it in the dryer and began alternating, in 10-minute intervals, between the air-fluff setting, and the delicate setting. Even on the delicate setting, I turned down the temperature to low heat... or "less dry". It took about an hour, which seemed like a fairly normal amount of time. In the end, it was just as soft as when it was first purchased!

title: If you have neck issues, don't give up on this pillow!
text:
I've got to tell this story. I have had trouble with the discs between my cervical vertebrae, especially C7, slipping out of place on a daily basis for the last 10 years. , probably due to a lifetime of heavy shoulder bags, poor posture, because of my dental assiing job, and the wild 60s dances, I did when I was young. 😃
To avoid surgery, which has horrible consequences, I've used therapy balls to unkink the horrible knots in my shoulder, neck and upper back/shoulder blade region (right side mostly), and to gently press the discs back in place. For years, at night, I have slept with a king size pillow on each side of me to get my body in an optimal position [ I'M A SIDE SLEEPER ] . But also, I brought to bed with me each night, five different pillows : latex, memory foam, sobakawa, down and a medium firm fill. I sleep on my side, mostly the right side. Each night was filled with swapping out pillows all night long, as no pillow was perfect to keep my neck vertebrae in place.
THEN, I ordered this PILLOW, exactly one year ago. I had to remove at least half the buckwheat. So yes there was a little smell for a couple of nights.. not a big deal. But the *hardness* of the pillow made me regret having paid so much for it. So I ordered another pillow that had shredded foam, that you could remove and adjust the fill as needed and mush it around to give support. The hardness of the buckwheat pillow hurt the blood vessels in my temples and it was compressing my jugular veins. I tried the soft pillow and it was *dreamy*, but after a couple of nights, I had to bring "Mr. Buckwheat" back, because my neck was screaming for support! So I would sleep on the buckwheat and do a lot of adjusting to take the pressure off sensitive areas. During the night, when I couldn't take the hardness anymore, I'd switch to "Mr. Softee". So I kept on trying with the buckwheat and LISTEN TO THIS!... As the weeks and months went by, my head and neck veins either became used to the hardness or the buckwheat became not so hard.. or both. I used the buckwheat (pillow) more and more, until I no longer used the Softee at all... NOR ANY OTHER Pillow, EVER! Also, you become very adept at the adjusting of the pillow, you just know how thick it needs to be and how to lie on it right away, instantly. I usually like my pillow to be fairly thin, so the part I'm not lying on is thicker. However, sometimes I really need extra support on that C7 vertebra, so I flip it over and voila!.. .. instant support and relief and back to sleep I go. I now sleep soundly and solidly through the night, seldom changing position ... for the first time in decades (I'm 66)! Oh.. also the pillow is very cool and seldom heats my neck, if it does, I just flip it over. And something else, no one else might mention is, the PILLOW NEVER SMELLS!! IT NEVER gets stinky! How does that happen?! Now, I would never go off ANYwhere to stay without it. I look SO forward to going to bed every night now, knowing when I lie down on my pillow, I will have instant comfort and relief if I've had a bad neck day. I have the smallest pillow ( I'm 5' 1") and it's plenty big for me, more than enough. This little bag of seed hulls has made a HUGE, HUGE difference in my life. It is the PERFECT PILLOW! So DON'T GIVE UP on it. Keep working with it. Pretty soon you'll be a pro at maneuvering it and you will benefit greatly with how your neck stays in place and the extra sleep you get because you are not waking up at all hours of the night. ONE PILLOW!.... That's all I use now, except I still have my two king size pillows I use as body pillows, for my lower body. I almost never take the time to write a review, especially one this detailed, but this pillow has helped me soooo much, that I want others to have the same relief I've experienced. It's such a little thing and makes such a big difference. Just don't get discouraged at the initial hardness. It took about 2 months to become accustomed to it, and about 6 or 7months before it was the ONLY pillow I wanted. It is more than worth it to stick with it. You WILL get used to it, I know because I'm extra sensitive, and although it never loses its support, I do believe the hulls get a little more supple. I saved the other half of the hulls in a gallon ziploc bag, just in case these hulls ever wear down. After a year, it doesn't seem like that is going to happen. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS PILLOW! Have a wonderful Christmas and SWEET DREAMS! 💕
ps. Poor Mr. Softee pillow now just takes up space in my closet. ;D

title: Great Little Vacuum and a Great Price
text:
I was originally looking for that really expensive brand stick vacuum but just couldn't see paying so much money and ended up landing on this one based upon the reviews of others. I am quite pleased with it. I will say that I am a single person living with one non-shedding dog and one shedding cat so the amount of dirt and dust tracked in is smaller than it would be for a family. Even though I have listed a couple of cons below, I still gave it 5 stars because it meets what I was looking for, does the job and is a great price.
PROS: I love that it is rechargeable. It stays charged long enough for me to vacuum my living and bedroom carpet and the hall, dining room and kitchen hardwood and has some charge to spare. (I keep forgetting to actually time it) The carpet head is very maneuverable, has a very low profile and lays out flat to get under most furniture items. It is narrow so isn't going to sweep a wide path with each pass but that also allows it to fit in tight spaces. Although the motor doesn't sound like it's very strong (it is quiet) I have been surprised each time I've used it how much it picks up. The dirt cup is full after doing the above mentioned areas. When the handheld section is detached from the upright section, it has two attachments, the crevice tool that is conveniently located in the back of the housing and the small carpet type brush roller head for use on furniture, steps, car interiors etc. It works well and again picked up a lot of dirt and cat hair.
CONS: This unit feels top heavy to me and feels heavy when using it, either attached to the carpet head or detached for the handheld.I am 65 and do not have the upper body strength that I once had and I find myself switching hands often because it makes my shoulders tired. (But I chose to count this as upper body exercise and am getting used to it!) The unit also will not stand up on it's own so you have to find a place in a corner to lean it when not in use and charging. It would be nice if it came with a bracket. Also, there is no dusting brush attachment nor a non-roller type head that you could use on drapes or other vertical surfaces.

title: Great!
text:
I've had mine for a couple years now. They still work great and hold a seal even when re-used multiple times. I've heard a few complaints about them, so I wanted to mention a few things in my review that worked for me.

Here are some tips to getting the bags to work really well. Use the proper size bag and do not be tempted to overfill them - use fewer items in more bags and use the proper size bags. For instance, fold bulky bedding fewer times (so they're flatter) and place them in large bags rather than in smaller bags with a bulkier fold/stack. Place the items deep into the bag, and leave plenty of space near the seal. You don't want anything pushing the walls of the bag apart near the seal. When closing, pinch the clip firmly and go over the seal a few times, making sure to go all the way to the edges. Do not try to bend or fold the bags once they're collapsed and don't cram them into snug spaces (in other words, be sure to store them in such a way that if they do happen to break their seal and expand, that won't cause a problem).

title: Will This Suit Your Needs? Maybe...not.
text:
I just changed this to 2 stars because of the static cling. It makes this a pain to empty your ground coffee from the container and a pain to clean. Fortunately the vacuum cleaner does a great job cleaning. The rest of this review still stands.

I'll just start by answering the question. It depends. If you're one that's looking to upgrade from a blade grinder, this is going to be a definite upgrade. But I wouldn't say this is the best in it's class, since I'm not comparing it to any other disc burr grinders. If you're someone that brews several different ways, from French press to V60 to Aeropress to espresso, spend the extra $$$ on a burr grinder and keep looking. I have a conical for home use, but purchased this one for the 2 days a week I'm in the office to make my morning Aeropress cup. This is a much better alternative to a manual (hand crank, 6+minutes of grind time per cup) conical burr grinder!

This grinds well for V60 and Aeropress brews, but would be a pain in the arse for espresso since you cannot grind directly into your portafilter basket. Also, with the limited amount of settings, it's also impossible to dial into or fine tune your espresso grind. That being said, if you find a setting that works for your bean and espresso machine, this may work for you. How's that for clarity (hint of sarcasm)?

Here are the Pros:

1. It has 16 grind settings so you can grind for a decent range of brews. It's fine enough for V60 and Aeropress, which I also brewed this morning. Settings in between should be fine for your drip brewer with a cone or flat bottomed filter. For the reason mentioned above, I didn't attempt this with my espresso machine.

2. It produces a consistent enough grind, so you'll notice an improvement in cup flavor for drip or press brew methods.

3. It has a quiet motor. It's a grinder, so you would still have to pause your conversation while grinding, but I've heard much louder.

4. It has one of the lowest price points for a disc burr grinder. Since I was looking for a 2-day a week grinder, this mattered a lot to me. So even though there are things I don't like about this grinder, I'm keeping it.

So now the Cons:

1. This generates A LOT of static cling (see attached). Just remember to tap the grind container to alleviate some of the cling. It won't alleviate all of it, but it won't be as bad as the attached picture.

2. The ground coffee container design isn't very good. First, it has a top lid, which is needed since it produces so much static electricity, but ground coffee sticks to the lid and flies out when opened because of the static cling. Also, the container doesn't have a good pour spout to pour your ground coffee into your brewing device. My old Capresso conical burr grinder had a open top container with a curved face that made it easier to pour from.

3. Another poor design is the chute that goes from the grinder to the container drops in at a 90 degree angle. This means a lot of build up in the chute (see attached picture). If the chute would fall directly from the bottom of the grinder to the top of the container, this wouldn't be an issue. If you're going to use this as your primary grinder, this may be reason enough to spend a few extra dollars on a different disc burr grinder.

4. Clean up is messy at best if you try and use the little brush that comes with the grinder. Throw that brush away! I used my vacuum cleaner hose to clean out the chute from the top and bottom of the chute. This will keep your rogue ground coffee from escaping.

5. Removing the burr disc to clean your grinder changes your grind setting. Not a big issue since you can always set it back. But I find it an unnecessary step since I never had to consider that on my conical burr grinder. Then again, I did have to always set it back on my old Capresso. However, the design was better and easier to return to the previous setting.

So enough whining and complaining about the cons. Again, I'm keeping this since I'm only using it two days a week. I would only recommend this one for someone upgrading from a blade grinder and that can take the time to put up with the static cling and cleaning process. If you don't want to put that effort into your daily grind, and want to stay in the disc burr range, spend a little more for another grinder. Some conical burr grinders start in the 100 dollar range. If coffee is your religion, save, save, save, for a higher end conical burr grinder. Cheers!

Also, the magnets are super strong, and won't fall off at the first accidental touch like some other magnets do. Here's the downfall; the magnets on the back are strong, but jut out of the back of the magnet housing. Also, they are very rough and jagged. Especially with how strong the magnet is, it can easily scratch the surface of any fridge. It certainly scratched mine. Thankfully I tested it out on a part of my fridge that still had the plastic on it from when we first bought it, so the plastic worked sort of like a screen protector for a phone. But when I moved it to the side of my fridge, which is unprotected, the same problem obviously persisted. The sides of my fridge are now scratched, and I find that I have to be very careful with these magnets. To take them off I have to take them off very carefully, and not slide and pull them off, lets I leave a gash in the finish of my fridge. For a sturdier fridge with a lot of dings and a white finish it might not be so bad, but I have a stainless steel fridge, and these certainly can do a lot of damage on its finish. I would not recommend this product. 2 stars because they look nice and the magnets are really strong. I may still use these, but cover the back part of the magnet with some plastic wrap or tape or something.

It’s a versatile color that can easily coordinate with cherry, walnut and darker colors, and I opted to pair it with white contemporary chairs with light wood, just to brighten the feel of my house. My husband and I were both surprised by the thickness and beauty of the table when we opened the box. We were also surprised by how quickly this went together. Keurig tried to spin and characterize the use of non Keurig kcups as minimal by consumers by just talking about the mistake of user-filled my kcups not working anymore on the 2.0 but something they will support in the future in the next version. That said, they are cute & were purchased solely because they are bronze. When I decided not to use them, because the tablecloth clips I purchased worked better, my husband wasn't too happy.

Then, we ordered a couch protector. The protector works for a couch with a flip down table & reclining seats, but makes those functions unusable with the protector's back strap on. Without the strap, the back of the couch protector falls down. So... I proudly hauled out my little bronze anchors & fixed the problem by adding them as weights to the back of the couch protector. Protector stays put, couch is still fully functional, & hubby is happy I found a use for my very overpriced anchors :-) All is well.

title: Sleek Beautiful Design, Makes an Excellent Cup of Coffee!
text:
Excited to have finally received my OXO 12 Cup Coffee Maker! Will be doing a lot of entertaining over the holidays and this arrived just in time to break it in before the madness starts. It's a beautiful machine and was a breeze to setup. Reset the scale for the kettle, set the clock and we were ready to go. Did not have any of the issues mentioned in other posts but I have not brewed a full 12 cups yet. Setting the delay timer was simple and the result was a delicious cup of coffee the next morning. The combination of an electric kettle and a coffee maker is great for us because my wife is a tea drinker. Hot water is ready for her in the morning and so is my coffee!

Pros:
Makes great tasting coffee
Great for entertaining
Flexibility of an electric kettle for those who have tea drinkers in the house
Easy Setup
Love the backlit LCD and stainless steel, sleek modern look.

Cons
None that I have found yet

I'm a big believer in paying for quality, we wanted something that is easy to setup and will work right out of the box for years to come. Our experience with OXO products in the past has been very positive so we knew we could not go wrong with this purchase. Very happy with this product overall.

title: Honeywell Fresh Breeze Tower Fan
text:
I waited until I actually began to use it prior to writing a review as I purchased it towards the end of the winter... It's now May and in full use.
Pros-
The height of this fan is perfect - was a bit worried at first because our bed sits up high and our last fan was too short -- the height of this fan is absolutely perfect.
It's sturdy - doesn't move, lean, rattle, tilt or shake in either mode - the circular base seems to keep it firmly situated wherever you place it.
It's quiet - not loud or noisey at all -- even on the the highest speed setting it isn't overwhelming.
The all black color gives the fan a pretty sleek modern look so it doesnt stick out like an ugly piece of furniture.
It has the basic features of a fan - Hi, Medium, and Low speed settings as well as the digital display equipped with a timer feature - which I thought to be neat for say setting it for overnight use.

Cons -
The instructions for the base were a bit tricky but we figured it out relatively quickly
The remote - while having a light on it seems like a great idea -- I haven't found the need for it.

title: I love this handy alternative to outside grilling! Great results, super easy clean-up, faster prep time.
text: I’m the world’s least enthusiastic griller. Typically cooking dinner is a chore that I just want to get through so everyone can eat, so I can clean up and be done. I’m rarely excited about anything grill related: outside grills seem (to me) to be a lot more trouble than they’re worth and I’ve never understood why people would choose to stand outside with the bugs and the weather when they have a perfectly functional oven inside of their house. On the rare occasions that I get excited about a grilling thing, it’s typically short-lived and usually on behalf of one of my kids that love the whole prolonged grilling experience. The Smokeless Korean BBQ Plate is a notable exception to my typical yawn reflex when talking about grilling gear. This BBQ plate offers all of the things that my family loves about grilled food, including the health benefits, tender meats, and the locked-in-juices results. And this plate offers a terrific alternative to me, to standing outside, preheating the grill, cleaning a huge hard-to-manage grill, and seeing monster sized spiders that scurry under the grill. By using the Smokeless Korean BBQ Plate, I am able to avoid frying which makes the meal healthier, I can serve my family food with that barbequed taste that they love, and I can clean up by tucking the two pieces of the plate in the dishwasher! It’s a thousand times easier than using the outside gas grill. The first time I used it, I used water in the base – you do need to keep adding water while you cook if you have something (like chicken) that takes a while to grill. The second time that I used it I used a seasoned marinade and the flavor really does seep into the meat – I had doubted that it would. When using the marinade I did not have to refill the base even though it took a while for the meat to cook, for me this was a big plus – I had worried about how to add the marinade during cooking without making a sticky mess, it turns out it wasn’t a factor at all. Also, when using the marinade it made the house smell good even though there was no smoke from the BBQ plate which was terrific. I received this stovetop grill at a promotional cost in exchange for an unbiased review and it really does work well. It’s a terrific alternative to standing outside with the spiders, and I get quicker prep time, great results and super easy clean-up!

title: Excellent for the price.
text: Overall this works very well as a boiling kettle for "brew in a bag" (BIAB) beer. For the unfamiliar, this is the same kettle that forms the core of the "Grainfather" brewing system, which costs much more (although it has lots of other capabilities). It has a completely flat bottom with no exposed heating elements, and the only protrusion on the inside of the kettle which can snag is the drain outlet. In general it works exactly like you'd expect; you plug it in and turn it on, and it heats up. The only downsides are that it's a 120V unit, so compared to DIY kettles which use 240V water heater elements it's much slower to boil, and there's no temperature control; you need to add your own if you want anything besides full-on/full-off. There are lots of "PID controllers" that will maintain exactly the temperature you want, for not much money.

title: The honeymoon is over
text:
UPDATE 09/18/2015 When I first purchased this clothesline I was thrilled. But a few months into the relationship and the honeymoon is over. The problem is that the blasted peg/knob things on the bottom of the unit are not durable. And those peg/knob things are essential, because that is the key to keeping the lines taut. Both of mine have broken so I've done more than my fair share of cussing trying to finagle a way to prevent the lines from sagging. I still think this is a great design, the lines are long, retract easily, and there is plenty of line to hang multiple loads; unfortunately, the material is simply not durable. Deducting one star for each broken peg.

I've never had an outdoor clothesline, having always relied upon an electric dryer. But, in an effort to reduce our use of electricity (and, yes, save some money), I began looking at clotheslines. My husband was very much opposed to putting a permanent structure up, which I couldn't argue with. We looked at various clotheslines, including single string lines, as well as fold-down racks that mount to the wall, and those too, were either impractical (a single line won't be able to accommodate the volume of laundry we have) or unattractive. We wanted something that would provide quite a bit of space, but we wouldn't have to be walking to some remote area of the yard, because 1) we probably would be too lazy to utilize it, or 2) we'd forget to bring the laundry back in. This was the unit we settled on, for two reasons: 1) it has two separate lines which each provide miles of line (ok, 49 feet per line, but it feels like a lot!), and 2) though unsightly, it could be taken down easily when not in use. We've had this for about six weeks, and I have used it countless times since then, as have my husband and kids. It really works as promised. My husband mounted the base plate, which holds the unit, on the wall, and then put the two anchor/hook pieces to which the lines attach, in opposite areas. I think this is one of the best features of this unit. One line goes one direction, and the other line goes a completely different direction. We did this deliberately to utilize as much area under our covered patio, so the sun wouldn't fade the laundry (we are in the Phoenix area, therefore the sun is very intense), while also avoiding obstacles like the patio table, etc. The base plate and hooks are virtually unnoticeable when you are not using the dryer (meaning, I've taken the main unit down), which is wonderful. The lines themselves are easy to pull out and retract without any problem. The two little knobs on the bottom of the unit are used to keep the line taut. They are very easy to use and work perfectly. We placed the base plate and hooks high enough that we're able to hang our California King sized sheets without them touching the ground. I have found in the dry heat, the laundry - including jean shorts, socks, towels and thicker items - dry much, much faster than in the dryer. This was a really pleasant surprise. When it's a bit more humid (it is monsoon season here in Phoenix, after all), the clothes take about as long as the dryer would, maybe a bit longer. But for the vast majority of loads I have done, the laundry is dry before the washer has even completed its cycle for a second load. When I'm finished with the unit, it takes literally one minute to retract the lines and take the unit off the wall - which I prefer to do so it stays clean (and, as I mentioned, it's not the prettiest thing in the world). I wish I had done this years ago. I would highly recommend this retractable clothesline.

title: Beautiful pearls!
text: The Karen Davies website instructions are frustrating and they recommend their fondant, which simply is not available in the US.  Typical fondant, used to cover a cake, will NOT work with this mold.  It is too soft.  A 50/50 mix of fondant and gumpaste is necessary.  Don't bother with the technique shown on the website.  Instead, roll a log of the mix and place all the way down the middle of the mold which has been heavily dusted with super pearl luster dust. Roll toward the edges with a small roller, really pressing into the mold.  Use a palette knife to remove excess on the edges and turn upside down to unmold.  If you are putting this on a cake to eat, be aware that it is really thick and will have to be removed to consume the cake.  I used it on a styro dummy as a bottom layer and it was beautiful.

Customer service at Fagor asked the usual questions: no, it had not been dropped, yes, we tried the cord several times, no it was not damaged in any way. I bought this pressure cooker because Consumer Reports rated it higher than the Instant Pot. My husband wanted to get me an Instant Pot. I insisted on the Fagor. title: Not perfect, but better than the others I've tried
text:
I bought this pillow, the Travelrest Inflatable Travel Pillow and the J Pillow before a long overnight trip to Brazil. I brought all 3 with me hoping that one of them would work because I simply can't stay asleep for long on an airplane unless I'm lying flat. None of them miraculously allowed me to sleep uninterrupted for 6 hours but overall this one was the best. Feel free to check out my reviews on the others.

Pros:
- The big difference for me between this and the others is that this keeps my head from flopping left, right or forward. So when reclined 18 degrees, or whatever you get in economy class, it made for a pretty stable sleep
- The memory foam contours to your body and the material is soft and comfortable. And it doesn't feel cool as some inflatables do

Cons:
- it's bulkier than inflatables, there's no way around it. It comes with a pouch with a velcro strap that helps keep it in place once you compress it but it's still a cylinder about 6" tall and 6" diameter when packed, maybe a little less if you squish it between some other stuff.
- the plastic clasps that hold the laces together (to keep the pillow under your chin) are pretty flimsy. My clasp stopped holding on the first flight after using it a few times and I had to play with it a while to fix it. Without that clasp the pillow just doesn't work because your head can flop forward. It's only a matter of time before it breaks for good. The clasps don't match the quality of the rest of the pillow.

I managed to sleep about 2 1/2 hours straight with this pillow, and about 5 1/2 total on my overnight flight to Brazil. My previous record was about 2 hours total and I had a stiff neck. No stiff neck at all this time. I've used it a couple of other times since the Brazil trip and I still like it. If I can find a pillow that allows me to sleep 5 hours straight in economy class I'll buy it, but until then this is my go-to pillow.

title: Thermo pro probe well worth price @ $11.00.

I compared them for accuracy to the Thermapen by Thermoworks and found them to give readings as fast as the Thermapen and as accurate using an ice water bath for calibration. However the construction is no where near as solid as the Thermapen and thus I would still go for the Thermapen by Thermoworks for my own use as I've had it for over 3 years and it's still perfect. The construction of the $10.99 Thermo pen is in MHO  no where near as solid as the Thermapen but for the price and weekend cooks the price and accuracy offered over dial reading devices is a no brainer. Users of these type of temperature reading devices seem to be confusing with readings varying in what is being cooked during the cooking process, but fail to realize that items cook from outside in and these devices give accurate readings of temperatures which will vary due to the depth of insertion of the probe reading as it is so quick to respond with a temp reading. title: Love this product, but it's not for everyone...
text:
I love this mini food processor. I really dislike clutter and buying a big food processor was out of the question as it would take up too much room to store. This food processor is the perfect size and the color matches my kitchen backsplash really well so I don't even mind leaving it out on display! I absolutely hate the sight of cords and this processor has a reel at the bottom so that you can hide the cord out of site. The container is fairly easy to twist off of the base (as long as you use both hands) and every piece that touches food is totally removable and easy to clean. Did I mention I absolutely love this processor??

The only reason why I took away one star is because I did not find the description accurate. Based on the name of the product, it supposedly processes 3.5 cups of ingredients. However, when I'd thrown in about 2 cups worth of garlic (no, I wasn't trying to fend off vampires...just cooking in bulk :P), I noticed that it was almost full. I may have been able to throw in a bit more, but I don't think it would've been able to handle that much more than 2 cups worth of ingredients if you want the machine to mince well. I think 3.5 cup would probably render the blades almost immovable...if you can even close the lid properly. However, I hardly ever need more than 2 cups of ingredients minced at a time and it took less than a minute to completely mince my 2 cups of garlic. It is so easy to use that I do not mind processing in batches when necessary. The instructions do break out various capacity for different types of ingredients (from 1.5C liquid to 3C nuts), but it's misleading that it is not posted in the product description on the site while the name of the product boasts 3.5 cups. So while I love this processor, you may want to buy something larger if you constantly cook in bulk and require more than 2 cups of ingredients processed at once.

title: A Definite Upgrade From the DCC-1200 (Brew Central 12C) Model
text:
I'm an unabashed fan of Cuisinart's small appliance line. Except for my Kitchen-Aid stand mixer, all of my small appliances wear the Cuisinart brand. (Only one Cuisinart product has so badly disappointed me that I could never recommend it...the Cuisinart line of ceramic non-stick skillets.)

PROS:
- Attractive on the countertop. You won't be tempted to put it in an appliance garage or hide it under the sink.
- Intuitive operation. You do not need to drag out the instructions to make your coffee.
- UPGRADE! Unlike the Brew Central, this model does not employ #6-font for its control labels. This is no small deal when you are bleary-eyed and have yet to have even one cup of coffee.
- The dispensed hot water comes out at 195F. Plenty hot enough for my tea.
- Dispensed hot water is ready in 3-4 minutes. My microwave heats water faster, but you also have to add time to gather the necessary Pyrex measuring cup, the water, etc.
- The coffee tastes good. I did not notice any off tastes that were reported by other reviewers...either in the coffee or in the hot water.
- UPGRADE! Easier to fill than the Brew Central. Yes, the fill point for the reservoir is still located at the top-back of the machine. So, yes, you will have to pull the CHW-12 out from under cabinets to fill it. And, yes, if you are short in stature, filling can be problematic. But...
- UPGRADE! The CHW-12 has a sight gauge 'water gauge' on the side of the coffee maker. No more peering into the internals trying to see the 'steps' inside that indicate fill level.
- BONUS! If you are replacing your Brew Central with the CHW-12, save the decanter, decanter lid, filter basket, filter basket holder, and water filter holder. They all fit the CHW-12 too. A real bonus for folks who tend to break decanters.
- Water dispenser accommodates tall mugs and travel cups.
- UPGRADE! The lid and 'shower' are not one-piece design (as they were with the Brew Central). Raising the lid on my Brew Central sounded like Dracula's crypt opening.
- UPGRADE! The teeny-tiny LED indicators on the Brew Central were replaced with super-bright, larger LEDs on the Coffee Plus.

CONS:
- It's easy to accidentally spill ground coffee into either water reservoir. But if you add the coffee to the filter basket with the filter basket removed from the coffee-maker, this 'con' disappears.
- Some of the product descriptions touted a backlit clock. Either mine never had this feature, or it doesn't work. Not really a deal-breaker for me.
- The lock on the hot water dispenser seems to be a safety nanny feature. A curious child could just as easily be scalded by the hot coffee in the decanter three inches away. At least one is not obligated by default to use the lock.
- The reservoir for the hot water dispenser could be bigger. But the footprint of the machine would get bigger too.
- Short power cord. Not at all Cuisinart's fault. This is a "Thank you, Safety Nanny" feature.
- The hot water feature (especially when its tank is filled) adds a significant amount of weight to the machine. Since its non-skid rubber feet work well, you have to pick up slightly on the machine when moving it. People with marked deficits in upper body strength may find moving the CHW-12 a bit awkward or strenuous.
- The instructions caution users to 'always unplug' the unit 'when not in use'. Doing so will wipe out the machine's volatile memory...requiring that the clock, brew start timer, brew off limit, and carafe heating time all be re-set. But, the machine will retain its memory for one minute with the power unplugged, giving users plenty of time to add water or move the machine.
- I feel that many of my 'cons' above are pretty nit-picky. This one...is not. There is no timed auto-off feature for the hot water heater. I might 'break the rules' by leaving the machine plugged in, but I would never leave the house or go to bed with the hot water heater 'on'. I believe this to be a significant design flaw.

I really like this coffee-maker. My Brew Central lasted 3 1/2 years with only once-daily use. Since the Coffee Plus is essentially the Brew Central with an added hot water dispenser, I am hopeful that the Coffee Plus will live a bit longer. Coffee-makers priced in the $100 (and up) range should outlive a $20 Mr. Coffee. OTOH, increased complexity and increased number of features tend to shorten mean time between failures for most devices. Despite my concern about longevity, I am somewhat comforted because Cuisinart provides a generous 3-year warranty on the CHW-12.

title: Decent for rice but not much else
text:
Let me start by saying that I love the little rice cooker I have. It's not very big; it makes, at most, about 3 "cups" of rice (which I think is 1-1/2 real cups of rice), but I don't need to make more than that at any one time so no problem. However, my old rice cooker is just that-- old. The coating on the bowl is starting to scrape up, so we've been thinking about getting a new one. When this rice cooker became available to review through the Vine program I was excited. It was bigger than the one we have and supposedly cooks other things too. Sounds perfect. Not so much in reality.

The Pros:
1. It did a decent job of cooking the 3 "cups" of rice that I made in it. It was a little firmer than I'm used to, but it was still good.
2. If you need to cook a lot of rice, this gizmo can do it. It can cook 10 "cups" of rice. By cups, I mean the cup measure that comes with the cooker. I think this cup equals about a real 1/2 cup, so it can make about 5 actual cups of rice. If you need rice for a group, this can handle it.
3. There is a delay start feature.
4. The buttons on the top are easy to use.
5. The risotto setting is part pro, part con. It's a neat feature, though I'm not sure how well it works. My 17 yr. old daughter made the risotto recipe that comes in the little cookbook provided. She knew to use the rice measuring cup for the risotto bit used a standard measuring cup for the liquids, so it was too liquidy when it was supposed to be done. I resolved the problem by keeping the lid open and leaving it on the warm setting while stirring it for a few minutes. This helped some of the liquid boil off and get to the right consistency for risotto. I can't vouch for what the consistency would be if the recipe was followed correctly, but the liquid to arborio ratio seemed lower than for more traditional risotto recipes. The recipe itself was also pretty bland. I might try it again using my own recipe.

The Cons:
1. It's big. That's the first thing I thought when I took it out of the box. Wow, it's big. And where am I going to keep this thing? It's definitely bigger than I thought it would be. Not as big as a crockpot, but bigger than most standard rice cookers I've seen in the store.
2. The markings on the insert pot are very hard to read. I basically needed a flashlight and my reading glasses to see the numbers imprinted on the inside. These numbers are used when putting the water in to cook rice. I wish they stood out a little better. The coloring makes it hard to read,
3. There are no instructions on how to make plain old rice. If I hadn't used a rice cooker before, I wouldn't know what to do. For anyone who isn't familiar with rice cookers, you need to measure your rice using the cup provided. Put that into the insert. Rinse the rice until the water is almost clear. (Not sure if the rinsing is required but it helps get the starch off, I think, and keeps it from getting that rice foam while it's boiling and makes nice rice that's not gummy.) then you have to fill the insert with water up to the number/line that corresponds to the number of cups you put in. If you put in 2 cups, fill the water to the number 2. The cup provided is not the same as a standard measuring cup. I think it's closer to a half cup. For our family of 4, I make 2 "cups" of rice. After you get the right amount of rice and water in the insert, you close the lid and push the rice button. That's it. However, instructions should be provided.
4. The "slow cooker" setting isn't really a slow cooker as all the "slow cooker" recipes provided in the book cook for 20-60 minutes. Nothing like a real slow cooker recipe. I'm not sure you could use it for a traditional slow cooker recipe as a I wouldn't know how long to cook it for. It must run hotter than a normal slow cooker.
5. The recipes provided don't look all that appetizing to our family, so the little recipe boom provided isn't very helpful.
6. The recipes in the book are a little confusing. On the first page of the book in the corner, in a small font, there is a note that says "The cup measurements mentioned in some of the recipes use the rice measuring cup supplied with your appliance. Fill the cup with ingredients up to the rim." This note should be more prominently displayed and should be a bit clearer. It should state that ALL cup measurements mentioned in recipes refer to the rice cup provided and not a traditional cup measure.

Overall, this cooker makes decent rice and passable risotto but I'm not sure any of the other settings are really worth using. Maybe other people will disagree. Unless you need to cook a lot of rice and want to try it's other features and see if they are better suited to your tastes and needs, I can't wholeheartedly recommend this. Personally, I think I would prefer a smaller, simpler rice cooker that is easy to store.

That said - the knife is a work of art. Surprisingly light, extremely well made / well-balanced and RAZOR sharp (and I do mean RAZOR sharp!!!). It looks absolutely beautiful and works even better. title: Just what I needed. Cheap looking but durable. Gets the job done.
text:
I wasn’t looking for something amazing and just wanted a bulk order of hangers that I could use for my everyday dress shirts and for travel. I will be honest. These probably aren’t the highest quality in my opinion. I have tried other hangers in the past that were more sturdier. The issue is that those hangers are also more bulkier. I also have very lightweight sleek looking hangers with felt on them but I found that those break way too easily. I have a lot of dress shirts that I keep accumulating and needed a lot of hangers to hang them in my closet while at the same time making sure they aren’t too bulky to save some space. I also wanted durable hangers because a lot of time I’m traveling and I take my clothes with me in the car. For those purposes, these hangers work perfectly fine. You can definitely tell right away that they may not be the nicest hangers but so far they are holding up well and doing their job. I will update my review if I notice any problems in the future. One of the nice things about these hangers is that they come with those little hooks so you can hang certain shirts that otherwise might slide off your hanger, especially those low cut ones or v neck sweaters. I would definitely recommend these if you’re looking for a bulk order of cheap hangers that are pretty durable. If you want to hang heavier items like suits or blazer jackets I would probably look elsewhere.

title: 350w = ~1/2HP, not 1HP
text:
Just to clear up any confusion the power rating on this is misleading as 1HP = 746watt, but if you search around, this 6000 HP is a 350w model. Claiming peak power on this model compared to the "running" power of all of the other models seems a bit dishonest. Note that this model is slightly more powerful than the Artisan (and moreso than the Classic) but has the advantage of the 6qt lift bowl. Another reviewer mentioned the height of the machine being an issue, but I had an opposite experience. I believe this model is about 16.5"-17" high, most cabinets are about 18" from the counter, so it's no issue getting it under them. In addition, because this mixer lifts the bowl and not the motor, it's actually shorter than the tilt model when removing the bowl or paddle.

Personally I have the [[ASIN:B0002Y5X9W Professional 600 Series 6-Quart]] model and love it. Found a reman'd example at another site for less than this one here. I have however, used the 6000 HP quite a bit at a friends house, and it is the same KitchenAid quality as any of them. The only thing this model can't do is mix a LOT of bread at once, without overheating and shutting down. If you aren't making 3-4 loaves of sourdough at a time, you should be fine with this.

title: I thought it was good until I seen what else was out there
text:
I have used this dehydrator for several years now. I thought it was good until I seen what else was out there. What I don't like about this is:
1. the trays get dirty with stuck on food. It is impossible to remove the dried on food completely. I have soaked them in the tub. I have pressure washed them outside with my hydroblaster. And I have brushed them with a bristle brush with much elbow grease. It is difficult to get them to my standard of acceptable cleanliness.
2. the trays are not dishwasher safe. I tried to clean them in my dishwasher and they warped beyond recognization.
3. there is no temperature adjustment.
4. in trying to dehydrate wet food such as tomatoes, water will condense on all the exterior walls then run down the inside. Moist foods should be limited to just a few trays.
5. the on and off switch is useless. It only adds to the cost and plugging the machine in or unplugging the machine is much safer since the plug is only right beside it.

All in all, this is a nice dehydrator and dehydrates food within it capability but is only worth $10 to $20.

title: Dash, Vitamix, Blendtech, or Ninja..... Honest review
text:
I do not own this particuar Blender, so All I'm here to do is give you the specs between this blender, and the Vitamix Professional Series 300, 750(I own) , 780 and 7500.

Dash Blender
$200-$250
1400W, 2.25 HP, 240Mph, and 35,000 RPM, Length of blades unknown
1 year warranty or 7 year warranty (through HSN)
HSN Offers Easy Pay

Vitamix Blender Professional Series 300, 750, 780 and 7500
$559 - $719 (New)
1600W, 2.20HP, 270 MPH, and 22,700 RPM, Blades 4"
7 year warranty with option to purchase a 10 year warranty
Order Through Vitamix and you can pay in Payments as well. Also you can order wet containers, dry containers , cook books, nut bags, spatulas, cutting boards, and more... and do payments on those as well.

If I had the extra $ and owned my own home ( you need to have a complete seperate circut in your breaker box for it and you can have it insalled as an undermount on the counter-top for a nice sleek and clean permanant look. I would have bought the Tom Dickson Extreme Blender by Blendtech (this is the only one at the time that could compare and surpass my Vitamix Pro 750).

Something is telling me that if I did extensive research on this Dash Chef Series Blender, that I would find the same problems as I did with the Ninja Blenders. Basically you get what you pay for, and the best in the ine is the Vitamix Professional 750, 780 (if you want digital touch). If you can afford the $1100 Tom Dickson, go with that!

Just my $0.02........ Good Blending

text:

Not only did they say they would replace the part but would ship it out priority mail (which I received in 2 days) but the representative talked me through the instructions and told me I could put the desk together without the broken part and put it on when the new one arrived. He was right and I was very happy as I had parts scattered around for assembly. As far as I am concerned this is what great customer service is. By the way the desk looks great and I am not going to look for the roll top now.

2nd post - sorry I forgot to mention that the desk is not that difficult to assemble. My suggestion is take your time, give yourself room to spread the parts out and if at all possible assemble as close to the area where you are going to put it as it is heavy and does need two people to move. title: Smells, but goes away after a few weeks.
text:
Mattress came nicely packed, wasn't too heavy (I was able to lift it up the stairs by myself. Easy to open if you have a blade. 1 huge problem I had with it, is that it smelled REALLY bad. I had to have my window open, which didn't really do anything at all. The whole smell consumed my small room. I let it air out for about 6 hours until I had to go to sleep, which did nothing. Still smelled really bad, and was tossing and turning on it and having bad dreams about the smell while I was sleeping on it. Woke up with the stench stuck in my nostrils for the rest of the day, which made me feel really nauseous. I was still able to smell that same nauseating smell for 2 weeks to a month before it finally went away completely. So...if you have a sensitive nose...I would just be cautious about the mattress. The smell did completely go away for me so in the end, I got a cheap mattress that is pretty nice in feel with the expense of me feeling like I wanted to puke for the first couple of weeks sleeping on it.

The mattress is soft, firm, but not too firm. Really good for the price, maybe even better than the double pillow top mattress I had in the past that cost over 2 times as much as this mattress. I just really wish they had a way of getting rid of that awful smell before shipping it, because then it would be perfect.

title: Receipe for the best yogurt ever!
text: Bought this based on reviews of others and glad I did. It took a couple tries to get the thick Greek yogurt I was looking for. I use 4 cups of whole milk, heat to 170' to 180'. Cool 1 cup and add  2 teaspoons of Red Mill tapioca flour, add 6 ounces greek yogurt (bought or from last batch) to cooled milk. When milk has cooked down to around 100', I add the 1 cup milk, flour and yogurt to batch. I then put in yogurt maker and let it go for 5 hours, and leave in the machine for 8 hours. I have found I do not have to strain this and the thickness is perfect thick greek yogurt. Add honey and a little vanilla, and wow you can't get may better than this.  I know some people will down on me because of the whole milk, but people my Great grandparents, my parents all grew up on whole milk and Daddy is turning 89 years young this year. Sometimes going whole fat, eaten in moderation isn't going to hurt you!

title: Easy to use product
text: I purchased this product to make it easier for my children to open and pour their own cereal and to better organize my pantry. This product is easy for little hands to open. The open spout is well designed with a solid close and an easy open. The 'pull-up' tab for the open spout is large and easy to access. The actual red lid itself is more difficult to open and reseal which works well for me because I do not want it accidentally popping open and dumping the contents. Also, I do not intend to be refilling it often. The back of the container indents slightly for a hand hold but, at 3-inches wide, it is still too large for my children to wrap their fingers around. They would need to hold the entire container with both hands and not use the hand hold. A adult can easily use the hand hold. The product is rectangular which I like because it does not waste space in the pantry. I like that it has a flush top and almost flush sides which mean they stack in close to each other. I have included photos for different size cereal boxes and how much their contents fill each container. This product is large enough to hold Family Sized cereal box amounts without a problem. The side of the container has marks indicating cups on one side and liters on the other side. The stickers were difficult to remove and needed soap, water, and goo gone to get all the residue off. I would purchase again and recommend this product.  I only wish this product came in a different color options besides red.

title: YOU DON'T ACTUALLY GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR!
text:
[[ASIN:B007UI919Q Herman Miller Aeron Task Chair: Highly Adjustable w/PostureFit Lumbar Support - Fully Adjustable Vinyl Arms - Tilt Limiter - Size C - Standard Carpet Casters - Titanium Frame/White-Gold Tuxedo Pellicle]]
WRONG CHAIR JUST ARRIVED~! ..And apparently there was almost NO WAY TO AVOID THE MISTAKE; unless you had taken an advanced continuing education course in deciphering the shameful, Herman Miller, Amazon Listing mayhem, which exist on almost every listing!

The long and the short of it is... The "Herman Miller Aeron Task Chair: Highly Adjustable w/PostureFit Lumbar Support - Fully Adjustable Vinyl Arms - Tilt Limiter - Size C - Standard Carpet Casters - Titanium Frame/White-Gold Tuxedo Pellicle" - DOES NOT include a "Seat Tilt Adjustment", DESPITE the photos within the listings gallery showing otherwise! ...and the same colored chair sold by a different Amazon vendor, described as ""Fully Loaded Highly Adjustable", also doesn't provide this feature! (You must find one that simply says "FULLY ADJUSTABLE", and NOT have that only pertaining to the arms!)

In case you were not already aware form experience... The "Seat Tilt Adjustment",is one of the most EXCEPTIONAL capabilities of a "highly", or better yet, "FULLY" adjustable Herman Miller Aeron chair! (I have personally found...) When it comes to eliminating fatigue after a long day of typing, coding, or working on desk based document and task; nothing alleviates your back's stress better than being able to re-position the angle of "attack" on your muscles and spine!

Consequential to this order fulfillment frustration; I also painfully answered another potential buyer's posted question:
"Does this seat have Tilt Limiter with Seat Angle Adjustment, Adjustable Arms, and Black Leather Armpads? "
(Source: https://www.amazon.com/forum/-/Tx18H7KVKM4QDN3/ref=ask_dp_dpmw_al_hza?asin=B007UI919Q )
...The previously posted, answer was a "YES"! ...THIS IS WRONG!
...I hope other buyers choose to say "show more" when reading the answers!

ACTUAL ANSWER:
NO!!
A "Fully Loaded", "Highly adjustable" chair, with "Fully adjustable arms"; is NOT the same as a "FULLY ADJUSTABLE CHAIR!" Ridiculously confusing!! The chair described in the following manor (below) DOES NOT come with a Seat Angle Adjustment!! Despite the fact that the photos included in the gallery, include one which evidently has BOTH levers necessary on the left side of the chair to make such adjustments! The one which just arrived at my house can NOT adjust the seat tilt!! - Here is the description of the exact color and model I ordered - "Herman Miller Aeron Task Chair: Highly Adjustable w/PostureFit Lumbar Support - Fully Adjustable Vinyl Arms - Tilt Limiter - Size C - Standard Carpet Casters - Titanium Frame/White-Gold Tuxedo Pellicle"
~ end of short answer ~

~ continuation of time-consuming, ridiculous research, required in order to get the CORRECT chair! ~
This chair in the same color, but with different mesh pattern, also (MISTAKENLY) shows photos with both levers on the left side, required for "seat tilt adjustment"; however, do to the fact the description offers no clarity in this regard, it is doubtful the right product would arrive! AND GET THIS... It describes itself as a "Fully Loaded Highly Adjustable Large Size (C) - PostureFit Lumbar Back Support Cushion Titanium Smoke Frame Classic Quartz Pellicle"
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004ZGE4C0/ref=ox_sc_act_title_2?ie=UTF8&psc=1&smid=A14X2WOLPJFQSS
"FULLY LOADED" - I think not... At least not from the description!! But yeah... It's only $1,000 dollars for a plastic chair... right!!?? ...Smh!

I WONDER HOW MUCH IT WOULD HAVE COST TO ACTUALLY GET THE CHAIR I WANTED?
(Stated Sarcastically)

After all of this annoyance in trying to get the style and color, NOT TO MENTION FEATURES, I wanted and thought were described (or implied) and most certainly pictured in the gallery; I am now having to order the standard black color, with the original styled Pellicle woven style mesh; sacrificing some of the "form", for better "function"! The back is more important at this point, than the beauty! (I REALLY DIDN"T WANT BLACK AGAIN!)

And despite this particular, replacement's listings having a rather mundane description: "
"Herman Miller Aeron Chair - Fully Adjustable, C size, Adjustable PostureFit, Carpet Casters";
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01DGI2ENI/ref=crt_ewc_title_dp_1?ie=UTF8&psc=1&smid=ATVPDKIKX0DER
...it fortunately goes into much better details under it's "Detail" sections; including the claim that it does indeed include, "Kinemat tilt mechanism allows the chair to move with your body; pivot points align with the hips, knees, and ankles for a natural recline motion" MOREOVER, "Features tilt limiter with seat angle adjustment, fully adjustable arms, adjustable lumbar, graphite base and frame, black armpads, and carpet casters"

To require a potential buyer, to have to become an EXPERT in deciphering these ridiculously inaccurate descriptions and claims; while also expecting them to IGNORE the photo galleries COMPLETELY!; is a bit RIDICULOUS! (Not to mention dishonest and misleading!)

title: OUTSTANDING PRODUCT - VERY GOOD VALUE
text:
This funny looking little gadget is The Most Indispensable kitchen helper I've come across in a long, long time. I got my dough docker. on time, and nicely packed in a plastic bubble pouch.

It is made completely of good quality plastic. I dropped it, so I KNOW it's good quality. Nothing broke. It's easy to clean. I ran it through the dishwasher, top-rack, with no problem. It held up fine.

I tried it out immediately with shortbread. It made the best batch I've made in quite a while. No raw spots. No tough spots. Just heavenly, tender crunch. The holes it makes in the dough provide very even baking and tenderness. And it's SO much better than a fork. I pierced [docked] an 8x10 pan of shortbread in about 5 seconds. Try that with a fork. The ultimate turtle race.

The roller glides along quickly and easily, It pierces deep enough, and spaced well, to totally eliminate any risk of steaming the dough into being tough,which anyone who makes shortbread knows can happen if you don't pierce thoroughly. Those batches become cookie crumbs simply because they're too hard to eat. This will Not happen with the docker.

The Docker makes clean holes and does not tear or mess up the dough's surface like a fork often does. The shortbread cookies came out looking attractive enough for company.

I dreamed someone would invent something like this, and one day there it was on Amazon. I couldn't believe my eyes! I jumped on it. It was exactly what I imagined it should look like.

It's so unique that I never hesitated at the price. It's so well made that it is worth every penny.

I love homemade pizza, but the crust eludes me. I stick to deep-dish to avoid embarrassment. Forget pie crusts. I'm famous for horrible ones where everybody eats just the filling.

But this Docker should change my baking reputation for the better as I use it for different recipes. Pizza crust will be my next adventure, and then I will attempt a pie crust.

With my new toy, I won't need luck this time.

title: Details, details... 5/17/15 (will update after exchange) (Updated 6/5/15)
text:
This immersion blender is not the small, lightweight hand blender you've bought in the past for $25. This blender has a much larger, and more powerful motor and has added weight from that; it also has a heavy duty design, waterproof buttons, safety lock... It really is designed for industrial use, not just a morning smoothie. Unfortunately, it is has a single flaw, that for the most part, renders it useless.

The blade, which is curved and sharpened on one side, and coved and blunt on the other, spins with the blunt edge leading and the sharp edge trailing. This is fine for making foams, or incorporating air into a liquid, even pureeing soft foods or making smoothies as the motor has more than enough power to make up for the dull leading edge. When the blunt leading edge of the blade encounters harder foods, (partly cooked carrots in my test) the blade will smash threw some of the foods, jam on others, and slow the motor to the point that stalls, despite its power, never fully pureeing the the soup (in my case). Similarly, tomato skins remain mostly intact and wrapped tightly around the blade due to this one small flaw.

I tested to see if this was simply the leads of the cord being switched during assembly with an old extension cord that was missing its ground (third prong), but no, the motor only rotates in one direction, so the blade was affixed backwards.

Pros:
1) Power
2) Durability, design, heavy power cord, waterproof buttons
3) NSF certified (no more trouble from Health Inspectors)
4) Easy of use

Cons:
1) Backwards blade rotation

The bottom line on this is, that at the moment, I would suggest NOT purchasing this KitchenAid Commercial Immersion Blender to any one, at least not until they correct the flaw in production.

(I have set up a return for the blender I purchased for exchange, I will update this review when I receive/test the replacement. I hope I received the only one with this flaw and the replacement is unaffected)

Update:

I received the replacement hand blender 2 days after requesting an exchange, return shipping labels were provided to me by Amazon (love amazon)

The new hand blenders blade rotates in the correct direction, with the sharpened edge leading and the dull edge trailing. I have only had the chance to try it out once on a milkshake, but the difference the blade rotation makes is noticeable even there. Now the blender pulls itself down into liquid being blended, partly suctioning itself against the bottom of the container. I could not be happier with this hand blender now.

"Pros:

3) NSF certified (no more trouble from Health Inspectors)

Cons:

The bottom line, I would recommend this KitchenAid hand blender to anyone in a professional kitchen who needs a medium sized immersion blender. title: Recommended!!
text: I received this as an Amazon gift from my mom. Let’s skip the “your spoiled” part. I know! This was an unexpected gift that I have been wanting for a while now but couldn’t see myself spending the money yet. Coming from Nespresso’s Lattissima Pro for the last 4 years,  I was super excited to be able to change coffee beans and grind a fresh cup of coffee or cappuccino. I’ve been through about 2.5 12oz bags since receiving it before Christmas. I agree on the difficult setup part said in other reviews. Trying to make that perfect cappuccino setting took some time. It took probably a half a bag just to do that. I’m at 8 seconds of milk froth and 1oz of espresso. Now here is where Jura loses 1 star from me. 1. The milk froth....these pieces must be maintained if you expect to get milk froth from this machine. It must be maintained daily. I went from a machine that I could just pull out the milk container, place in the fridge and walk away to having to conduct maintenance after every cappuccino sitting. I even went as far as buying the milk container accessory to help streamline this process. I thought I could get back to that. After trial and error I now have my routine of a full cleaning for the milk system. I no longer save my milk for a couple of days in the fridge like I used to. 2. I wish the machine gave me more froth control, but I see the E8 allows that. I should be able to adjust the froth instantly. 3. The first second of froth is hot water and steam. You have to time it right when putting your cup under the spout if you want to avoid that. You can also play with the knob and slowly turn it to control the timing of all of this. I even cut the milk line shorter to decrease the excess steamed water. Otherwise, you end up with extra water In your milk froth. I’ve cracked the code on this. 4. My milk froth attachment pops off every now and then from too much pressure when I turn the knob. Haven’t figured out why yet. It’s probably happened twice already. At this point, it doesn’t bother me as much. This machine produces excellent cups of both coffee and cappuccino’s. I no longer feel that need or want to go to a cafe to get a cup of cappuccino. I highly recommend this machine even with the small issues I’ve came across. On another note, my close friend just got his Breville touch in the same price range. I prefer the convenience of the automatic machines for my daily schedule over that type of machine. Also love that family members can just come in and make a single cup of coffee without any extra knowledge of the machine. This is a solid choice for a machine in this price range! Happy shopping.

title: Yes... you can use it for Deluxe Mac and Cheese
text:
Very convenient to use.

You can use this for deluxe mac and cheese, you just have to know how to do it. Through trial and error, here's what I've found...

add noodles and water to a bit above the fill line.

Microwave on high for about 7 minutes 30 seconds... pause and stir whenever it looks like the water is going to bubble over, then continue heating.

After that time is up, you should be left with steaming hot moist noodles and no water.

Add in your cheese sauce, maybe a little shredded cheese, salt and/or pepper to your taste. Stir well. Microwave for another 45 second, stir, and then a final 45 seconds. Stir and eat.

This assumes you have an 1100W microwave, otherwise times may vary a bit, but you get the idea.

Luxury plus Affordability

The washcloths feel as good as they look. The company is acclaimed as having the top five selling towels on Amazon, and I can see why this is true. They are thick and are soft on the skin, and they truly keep getting softer with every wash.

A plus is that they are affordable. I cannot find towels of this quality, and for this price elsewhere. At just a little over two dollars for each towel, they are priced within a reasonable range, and worth it!

It is comforting to know that the materials are made in a mill that is chemical and pesticide free, and the company is willing to certify this upon request. Cons:

title: Hard to Find a Place to Attach It
text:
The Victorio VKP1024 Deluxe Hand Operated Grain Mill was great, except there was no place in my house to attach it. I had to take it to my daughter's house to use it, and the only place at my daughter's I could use the mill was a granite-top table. The instructions say to attach the mill to a surface with straight sides and to push it all the way against the surface until it stops. That means you have to have a counter with at least a 2 inch overhang, and my counters and my daughter's counters have only a 1 inch overhang. Also, the counters have to have straight sides, which means if you have rounded or beveled edges on your counter tops, the mill will not stay put at all. So, even if you have a bar where you could attach the mill, if the bar does not have straight sides, it just will not attach. However, it was easy to attach the mill to the 2 inch thick granite table top, and it stayed in place with only occasional re-tightening.

As far as the operation of the mill, I loved it, and the instructions were clear. A lot of problems people have had with mills is likely that they haven't read the instructions or the instructions were hard to understand. These instructions say that before using, grind 2 cups of plain, white rice to clean the mill, then throw the rice away. They say to expect small metal particles in the rice, but I did not see any.

The adjustment knob stayed in position and the flour seemed fine enough, although I am new to grinding flour and making bread. The handle was easy to turn, although I did get a workout when grinding 7 cups of flour! The wheat berries fed through smoothly and the flour dropped into the bowl without making a mess.

My next mill was a less-expensive Back to Basics that is supposed to be the same as the VICTORIO VKP1012, and the pictures sure do look the same. Let me assure you, the Back to Basics does not operate the same as this Victorio VKP1024! The Back to Basic assembles very differently than this Victorio VKP1012, and it is definitely not as good. I’m still looking for a hand operated grain mill.

If Victorio would fix the attachment problem of the VKP1024 so that it would attach to a standard 1 inch counter overhang, I would definitely repurchase it.

title: The sets do not come with large pots like this, so we needed something larger
text:
We only use Mauviel pots and pans as we try not to use any cookware that has non-stick and other coatings that can be harmful. Most of our cookware is from the copper and stainless steel Mauviel collection - this was the first all stainless steel one. We bought it because it was an affordable and it is a decent, large size. The sets do not come with large pots like this, so we needed something larger. It does cook well and evenly. The handle of this is the same stainless steel as the pot itself and gets blazing hot fast - really fast! So have a pot holder, hot hand, or towel ready to use if you need to pick this up straight from a hot stove. The same with goes for the handle on the lid. You will burn yourself if not. The handle is extra long, so much so that I have to say, I've never seen a handle this long on any pot, of any size, ever. With a handle this length, you have to be careful which way you turn it if you're cooking with multiple burners or have small children.

title: AMAZON SENT ME A USED, DAMAGED PRODUCT.

They claimed this was a machine that only had a slight cosmetic flaw on top, but was otherwise new, with everything in the package.  I received the machine and first noticed there were no instructions.  So, I figured out how to use it--easy enough.  About 20 minutes after I made my drink (yes, very lukewarm, as everyone has complained.) the unit sent out a SPARK while it was sitting on the countertop, plugged in. Spark came from the machine, not the plug. Huh??? WTF?  I called Nespresso and they said they haven't had that problem.  Through the course of the conversation, I found out Amazon's wonderful "deal"  was also missing one of the coils that goes to the aerocino milk frother, and the 16-pod sampler.  We concluded that this was definitely a USED product, and that the previous owner probably dropped it or something, made off with the coffee pods, and sent it back.  Disappointed in Amazon; I haven't had any problems like this with them, ever.  I wound up purchasing directly from Nespresso.  I got an Inissia, which doesn't look as nice as the Pixie, but does the same thing. I paid $198 with the aerocino, including $6 shipping.  They are sending me a free gift for all my hassles.
