title: Love my Zinus Contemporary Metal and Wood Platform Bed !
text:
I ordered my Zinus Contemporary Metal and Wood Platform Bed with Wood Slat Support in queen size. I needed a platform bed that I could put a memory foam mattress on and didn't want to have to use a box spring mattress. Well I had read a handful of negative reviews about parts missing, box torn up, hard to put together. Well in my personnel experience that all could not be farther from the truth. First it showed up at my house very quickly. The box was in perfect shape, not torn or opened in any way. It is heavy, but then you need to realize that this is an entire bed taken apart and put in a box so yes it is going to be heavy. When I opened the box I was surprised that it was actually double boxed. Box inside of a box. I opened it in my kitchen and took all the parts in my bedroom to put it together without the mess of the box in there to deal with. The pieces well all individually plastic wrapped. there is also foam strips and pieces wrapped up to keep from making a mess inside to take up the extra room. I have never seen anyone wrap styrofoam to keep from making a mess. All of the parts were in perfect shape. No scratches, dents etc... All of the screws were shrink wrapped to a piece of cardboard to keep them in place. Then to top it off they also put a couple extra of each one as spares in the package as well and labeled them as such. There was also an allen (Hex) wrench in the package too since all of the screws are all allen head screws. They have included 2 sheets of paper with pictures of a piece by piece instructions. They also used a numbering system such as both pieces that go together will be #1. Then connect both #2's together and so on. Every piece fit perfectly together. The screw holes and screws all went together without any additional force. The wood slats all connected together with hook and loop ( Velcro type) strips. the bed frame has the opposite side and they all stick together very well. The entire bed was very solid with no movement what so ever when I was done with it. The black frame with the light colored wood looks great to me. I couldn't have been more pleased.
I do not work for or even know where this company who made the bed are located. What I do know is when I see a company who strives to correct any gripes against their product from happening again so that their customers are as pleased as I am with their product. As I was putting the bed together I was so happy and impressed I made my mind up that night that I was going to give them the review they deserved.

I have been sleeping on the bed for two weeks now and it is still very solid with zero squeaks. Mattress doesn't move at all. Super happy with the purchase!

title: Not as good as the eufy robovac 11!
text:
I purchased a eufy brand, robovac 11 for my place. I love it. Transitions from hard floor to tall carpet easily. I find that it's "logic" works well too. I bought two of these iLife a4s vacuums for my mom after she saw mine in action. I bought it because it looked exactly the same, and it boasted a longer run time vs. the eufy. Also, I found out the heap filters are 1" longer than the eufy and therefore have more surface area, which is always a good thing. So, I thought this was a superior product.

Nope! Once I received it I realized both vacuums have the same mah rating of their batteries: 2600mah. So the run-time is just exaggerated for the iLife. I know both vacuums just have four 18650 lithium ion batteries wired in series inside - but I was hoping the iLife had more. Not the case.
And most importantly: the iLife could not transition from a hardwood floor to a Persian rug. I couldn't believe it when I saw it. I just treated it like a wall and turned around. I brought over the eufy robovac, and placed it in the exact same place of the iLife a4s, and it jumped onto the rug no problem. I flipped over both vacuums and realized why: the robovac 11 has a tapered lip which rides up onto the carpet, while the iLife a4s has a sharp 90 degree lip.

Also it's interesting to note that the roller brush underneath of the eufy and iLife are different. The eufy has a spiral pattern of bristles on the roller like any vacuum: but it also has rubber lips inbetween the rows of bristles , which I believe is to aid in suction power.

While that is factual, this is just subjective: I found the logic of the vacuum to be poor compared to the eufy. It had trouble finding its way home, and it's just hard to explain, but in general, it's maneuvering was just not as good as the robovac. That is just my opinion. But the battery capacity and sharp lip that prevents it from going on carpet? Definitely true.

At the time, I got my robovac at a killer deal for $150, and I picked up this iLife a4s for $200. Now I see the robovac is $220 at best. I would absolutely not recommend the iLife over the robovac at any price.

title: a real review.
text:
I was hesitant to purchase this mattress. I mean who in their right mind buys a mattress off of Amazon. Well I did. We needed a mattress and our last $2500 beautyrest was worn out in only 5 years. So we decided on this the 15" mattress.
The first day - When it arrived it was rolled up about the size of a water heater. we unwrapped the mattress on our existing box springs from the old mattress. This mattress weighs a lot. We allowed it to rest for a few hour and slept on it the first night. There is a good odor from the mattress it is foam after all. The smell goes away after a about 6-8 weeks.
6 Months later - This mattress is very supportive. It does retain some body heat. I am 6'5" and 285lbs and the mattress is not the softest. Once it conforms to your body the foam does lose some of its softness. And it does not bounce back right away. I still toss and turn on this mattress but that being said I've gotten the best nights sleeps on this mattress then I've ever had.
7 months -
Having slept on a real temperpedic for a week at a families house the temperpedic is a way better mattress. It's cooler, softer, and rebounds much quicker when you turn over but it's also 4 -6 times the cost.
I am very happy with my mattress.

text:

1 year manufacturers warranty- (check- 2 once registered)

I left to run a few errands and when I came back I could not believe how much was in the dust bin. I keep the floors clean, or so I thought, but Otis took it to the next level.

text:
I purchased these a couple of years ago to work on fine motor skills with our son, who has a rather long list of diagnoses at this point that come with global developmental delays. At the time, I wanted this as part of a fine motor progression for stringing beads. He had become very successful with larger two inch beads, and I thought this would be a good next step progression and challenge for the beads, and I liked that there were pattern cards. And even though we've now progressed to stringing cheerios, I have recently placed this back in my rotation for therapy targets and tasks because of the pattern cards, which was something we could not work with him on at the time of purchase.

So, durability wise, we have no issues with this product. The strings have been holding up. For our little man, because of the nature of his challenges, we did have to knot one end of each string to keep the beads on and give him a good basis for adding more beads without getting frustrated. That is something we still need.

If you have a kiddo who is a chewer or has impulse control issues, this is a toy that you will need to closely supervise and may still stress the living day lights out of you from time to time. For example, today I was working on a pattern card that involve the cylindrical beads. Which are a lovely size for esophageal obstruction, and my little man (who is 5 and has problems with impulse control, chewing, and risk assessment) kept running off with them the moment he sat down and popping them in his mouth. His first stop with one of the beads was my yoga ball where he proceeded to bounce it into the back of his throat, and with another he ran up the stairs and coughed it into the back of his throat. Because he's quick, he got away from the table those two times before I could grab him, and I was fortunately able to still reach him and the bead quick enough to sweep it before it went down. The moral of the story is I think this is a great toy for fine motor, but depending on the nature of your child's disabilities there is definitely an element of risk that you can not turn your back on. Pretty much ever.

So since he is a chewer, I can say the paint holds up well enough for those times he's managed to get one in his mouth. I think this is a great multi functional teaching tool for a typically developing child as well as one with specialized needs. It's good for patterns, colors, shapes, fine motor, and creativity, and as it also has had no quality control issues, it is definitely a 5 star toy with supervision if needed.

title: I wanted to love it....but I think it's possessed.
text:
I purchased this grinder last year as an upgrade from my KRUPS F203 Electric Coffee Grinder that I owned. I wanted to love this grinder I really really did.......but I don't.

I love the fact that it has a bean hopper and the ground coffee is in a separate container. I also love the automatic timer so when I push the button it correctly grinds the amount of beans I need for the 6 cups of coffee I make every morning in my auto-drip coffee maker.....when it works right. Yes I said when it works right. When it doesn't work right, this is what happens:

Doesn't work right option #1: I get up in the morning, go downstairs, push the button and nothing happens. I pull the ground coffee container all the way out and push it back in until it clicks in place. Push the button, nothing. Pull the bean hopper lid all the way off, push it back down in place all the way. Push the button, nothing. Pull the grounds container all the way out. Pull the lid off the bean hopper. Grab my coffee bean container, open it, pick up and invert the coffee grinder pouring all the coffee beans (and some partially ground ones, back into the coffee bean jar, watch the burring grinding wheel fall out and into the coffee jar. Set the coffee grinder back down, remove burr wheel from coffee jar and re-seat it in the grinder turning clockwise until it "feels" firmly seated. Re-scoop the coffee beans back into the hopper. Replace the hopper lid and the ground coffee container, push the button and NOW it works. Clean up the ground coffee beans that fell on my counter while pour the coffee beans out of the grinder.

Doesn't work right option #2: I get up in the morning, go downstairs, push the button and it starts grinding and then suddenly the motor is whirring like a demon and no grinding is happening. I look and oh, the burr wheel isn't seated in the socket anymore and has popped up and resting at an angle amidst the coffee beans. See "Doesn't work right option # 1" for solution steps.

Doesn't work right option #3: I get up in the morning, go downstairs, push the button and the grinder apparently has decided I need twice the volume of ground coffee beans because it starts grinding and doesn't stop until the bean hopper is almost completely empty and I have 2-3x the amount of ground coffee I normally do. So I have to pull out my ground coffee scoop and scoop the ground coffee out of the container (or pour it into a bowl) and scoop to get the measured amount for my coffee maker. Then I have to clean my counter and wash my hands to clean up the ground coffee particles. Kind of defeats the purpose of it grinding a premeasured amount if I have to measure it myself.

Finally, as at least one reviewer has pointed out, ground coffee particles end up accumulating all over my counter. I pull my grinder forward from under my upper kitchen cabinets before I use it every morning so how then does ground coffee accumulate along the back of the counter??? I got so frustrated with the ground coffee accumulation that I bought a cheap plastic tray to sit my coffee grinder and coffee maker in, just to contain the ground coffee accumulation within the tray. When the ground coffee accumulation in the tray reaches scoopable levels I know it's cleaning time. Oh, and several reviewers have said this grinder is so much quieter than other grinders.....REALLY?! Its just as loud as my Krups....the only difference is I can walk away from it if I'm on the phone.

Krups grinder: CONS: No bean hopper, no grounds container, no timer, therefore I have to physically hold the button until it shuts off, no pre-set quantity. PROS: NO mysteriously accumulating ground coffee all over my counters, no disassembling and reassembling to figure out why it's not running...if its not running it's because I'm not pushing and holding the button.

DeLonghi grinder: PROS: love the bean hopper, love the grounds container, love the pre-set quantity, love the pre-set timer. CONS: mysterious accumulation of coffee grounds everywhere on my counter; has a less than pleasant temperament some mornings and decides it's not going to work right (see above).

I've reached my patience limit between it's temparmental days and the mysterious coffee accumulation and now I'm on the lookout for another coffee grinder. I wanted to love it....but I just can't.

title: An absolute must for a cook! Worth every, single penny!
text:
BEST. PURCHASE. EVER.

Seriously, once you go Instant, you never go back! I bought this when it went on major sale as I had been wanting one for ages! Luckily, Michelle Tam from NomNomPaleo had linked this to her IG when it went on sale and thanks to one click purchase on Amazon, I got it right before they sold out! :) It is daunting to use at first, especially if you've never used a pressure cooker before. But once you read the manual (yes, you MUST read it...much safer than just winging it), it will honestly change the way you cook. I've made stews, soups, braised meats, boiled eggs, rice, homemade yogurt, etc. and use it almost daily. A meal that would have taken me 3+ hours in a slow cooker gets done in less than an hour with the IP. There are newer models of Instant Pot that I could have purchased, but for $70 for this older model, it has been worth every penny and essentially does the same thing as the newer model. If you enjoy quick hot healthy meals, without the long wait or huge mess, this item is a MUST.

On a side note: the manual does state that the rubber ring on the lid will need replacing occasionally (can't remember how often from the top of my head) but I did notice that I needed to replace mine at least once a year because of how often I use it. If you don't replace it when it needs it, the pressure cooker will NOT build pressure. So keeps this in mind. Some people have complained about certain food smells not leaving the IP after washing the stainless steel pot insert, but I've noticed that the rubber ring does hold onto really strong smells (i.e. if you cook a curry in it) so in order to get rid of that smell permanently, I absolutely had to replace the ring. You can try washing it but I found that certain food odors are just more stubborn than others. Just a heads up!

title: Nice product!
text:
I gave this sign 4 out of 5 stars due to an incorrect punched reflective backing. When It turned on at night 1 of the 3 LED's didn't look right. It was very dim. The package says "No user servicable parts inside" but don't believe that. I took the front bracket that holds the letters/number in off and removed the screw holding the plastic. Once I did that I could see that there were three LED's and a shiny backing to make it reflect. The reflective material is hole punched for each LED. Well, LED 3 had a hanging hole punch piece. I removed that part and looks normal now. Some other observations..

* The whole product is easily serviceable. You can tweak it for sure. There's a piece of plastic that makes the LED's look fuzzy instead of clear and its a whiteish color. I'm sure you can change that to a different color if you want :-). The back side gives you access to the 3 LED's and the battery assembly. Its also easy to mess with if you feel like modifying it.
* The plastic assembly seems pretty sturdy to me. The quality is good
* They give you enough numbers and letters so don't worry there. They snap into sockets so its easily to center everything.
* You can hang it on your wall or use the spikes supplied. I prefered the hanging it because once you break out that weed eater you might ruin it. Also some punk kid could steal it.
* The LED's are fairly easy to see instead of having a bar of plastic that distributes the light and block the LED from easily being seen. Some people may not like this but its no biggie to me. If it is, modify it...Hobby Lobby could help :) There's an attached picture but just note my camera sucks! the LED's look big in the picture but they are not, they are standard small LED's. Its think its due to the darkness.
* The battery is in plastic. So I basically installed it and it didn't work. I didn't notice the plastic at first, once removed it worked.

I like it! I will buy it again for my BnB and my mom's house. Pretty nifty for the price.

text: I paid $70 for this machine, so I don't expect it to be commercial grade.  Have only had for a few days; can't address the longevity of the unit. Everything was ground with the fine plate and I didn't have a problem with clogging (there was plenty of cartilage wrapped around the blades and auger, but the grinder still functioned).  I stopped midway to clean the blades.  I was not kind to the machine. I fed everything in with only minimal trimming or cubing.  There was a lot of gristle/silver skin/ tendons/etc. going in, and the machine handled it without too much difficulty.  I did manage to overheat the motor at one point and had to let it cool off, but, in fairness, I believe I was being more abusive to the grinder than a reasonable person would be. title: This Is the ONE!
text:
I have had several cooking thermometers and I believe this one is the best. I know it is accurate because I was able to test it against an infrared temperature reader. I used it right out of the box for a couple of experiments and then tested my perfectly cooked chicken. Excellent! It reads fast and doesn't leave a gaping hole in the food.

But here's the real story. My water heater had been acting odd---the water was too hot. Then too cold. Then no hot water. Then what seemed like scalding water. I replaced the elements---easy stuff first, right? And it seemed to level off. But there was some dispute around the ranch about whether the water was coming out too hot. So I carefully set both thermostats to 125 degrees and after 4 hours, I measured the water temp. 126 degrees. So I went up to 145 degrees and was able to know with a degree of certainty what my water heater was producing. This device has helped me with several dinners and fixing the water heater. I wish it could do dishes!

Great device for the kitchen. Look, most of these digital thermometers are for meat only---so they have a limited range. You can use this one to measure boiling sugar mixes for candy making---that's great. And for the delicate dishes like custards? You can trust the accuracy.

So they sent me one of these to evaluate and I give it 5 stars. It is a superb product. Buy with confidence! Great company too---they really care about their products.

title: Very impressed
text:
This cast iron casserole is really nice! It's quite sturdy and heavy, which you would expect with cast iron, and looks to be extremely well made. The beautiful red finish is perfect and I could find no imperfections. It's pretty much ready right out of the box. A quick clean, and you're on your way (no seasoning required).

There's a unique feature on the lid of this casserole dish - basting dots. These little divots in the lid help collect steam and have it drip down evenly over what you're cooking. Helps keep food moist, which is a really great feature! I also like how easy this is to clean. It is dishwasher safe, but it's very easy to hand wash (which is good because I have no dishwasher!). I made a cabbage stew in it, and it cooked it perfectly.

I have two Le Creuset pans and I think this is equal in quality. In fact, there's one thing I like even better - the black interior! My Le Creuset pans have a white interior and they end up with brown stains, which can be a pain to remove. [Note - for those that have the same problem, try Bar Keeper's Friend]. I also like there there is no plastic handle on this, which means it's also oven-safe to 500 degrees. This can also be used outside on grills if you're so inclined!

Overall, I'm very impressed with the quality and love the low price! I was so fortunate to review this through Amazon Vine, but I try to write reviews as if I had paid the full purchase price, because I feel it is only fair for those who read and rely on reviews. I definitely recommend this product.

text: I really like the low wattage, low noise quality of this compared to a competitor's 6 inch fan. Both fans I've used have the same quality clip, which attaches easily to an [[ASIN:B005SG1FE6 Alera Wire Shelving Unit]] for example.  This fan curiously has a white, 3-wire, high wattage 14 gauge AWG stranded cord for only 24 watts of fan.  That's either funny, or wasteful, or a brilliant adherence to commercial building codes.  If you are in the market for a very personal range fan, this is a great choice.  If you'd like more white noise and a bit more air movement for a bedroom, then you might consider a 12 inch run on low, like the excellent [[ASIN:B00C4QP8KU Rowenta Table Fan]] or the [[ASIN:B000CQTG98 Air King Commercial wall fan]]. title: AWESOME!
text:
Love it! I have it on my desk at work and have been using it to welcome new team members or acknowledge specific days. I even have 2 coworkers who have bought one as well.

A couple things to note:

title: The best of all Technivorm models!
text: I originally purchased the newer KGB741 Moccamaster machine but ended up returning it because I didn't like the auto drip stop brew basket or carafe.  I feel this KB741 model is superior because it has fewer moving parts to become clogged, and also has a better carafe and handle design. Furthermore, it is cheaper!  I confirmed with several vendors that the sole difference between this KB741 and the KBG741 is the brew basket design and carafe. That's it. Very rarely with any Moccamaster will you need to interrupt the brew cycle to pour a mug which I feel negates any need for auto drip stop. This machine brews coffee so quickly it is a non issue.  Just be patient for a few minutes.  I suggest choosing any Moccamaster model with the glass carafe over the more highly priced thermal carafe models. The glass carafe is far easier to keep clean and the individual burner ensures your coffee does not get burnt while maintaining optimal temperature. All Moccamasters are identical internally and make coffee which tastes markedly better compared to mass market drip machines. The hype is legitimate when it comes to water temperature and coffee ground saturation.  The Starbucks coffee I brew with this machine tastes a lot better than the same blend on my old mass market drip machine. If you enjoy drinking coffee you should invest in this quality machine. The brushed raw metal finish looks very classic and goes with anything- which is important since Moccamaster machines will last a very long time if maintained properly.

title: My Mind Was Blown by the Beauty and Low Price
text:
If you want something that is elegant, large and mades a STATEMENT without breaking the bank, this is your coffee table! I searched for a long time for just the right thing and have seen furniture of this type that sold for $1000.00 and up - and they weren't this beautiful and classy looking. It is the centerpiece of our living room.

*BEAUTIFUL: This is eye popping for it's graceful lines and elegance.

*ECONOMICAL: About 1/5th to 1/10 the price of comparable furniture. (It is a little more expensive on Amazon than it is elsewhere. I found it locally at American Furniture Warehouse for $199.99, and we were able to pick it up from the store. The saving wasn't significant, but I have had trouble in the past with furniture arriving from Amazon.com with damage, so I was glad to find it close by so that I could return it easily if there was a problem.) No matter where you buy it, it is a great deal by anyone's standards.

*EASY ASSEMBLY: It is a snap to assemble and it really, really sturdy. Plan on around 45 minutes to put it together.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The only 2 downsides:

*EASY TO DAMAGE: I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 stars because it came with a little "ding" on the metal centerpiece. However, the damage was small and considering the "antique" feel of the piece, the dent isn't really too noticeable. It doesn't detract from the look at all. I wouldn't want it to be TOO banged up, though, so make sure that the seller gives easy returns before purchasing. Since It is easy to put dents in it, THIS DOES NOT BELONG IN A HOUSE WITH SMALL CHILDREN. Older children and teens should be OK as long as they have learned to respect property and know to play hard outside. I do not have small kids and my living room is one of those lightly used rooms, so it is perfect for me.

title: Beautiful little machine, horrifying ergonomics
text:
This little coffee mill does exactly what it says it does, grind coffee. It has an adjustable grind size and stays set to the grind you want. The parts are all reasonably well made. There is a convenient lid that allows you to save ground coffee if you don't want to use it all at once. It's beautiful in its simplicity. Very nice. What's the problem then? Why only three stars?
The problem is the ergonomics are bad. Really, really bad. You put the coffee into that top part, then you start grinding. Oh, wait, it's completely top heavy at this point and you find yourself using all your strength to hold the thing in place on the counter. As the bottom part fills up, it doesn't really get any better. My left forearm is now cramping trying to hold the thing still while I grind away at the crank on top. (If you don't hold it vertical, the grinding doesn't work very well). I suppose I could ask my weightlifter neighbor to come in and hold the thing down while I crank it, but what I typically do now, because I like the thing, I really do, is sit down and clamp it between my knees. (No, I am not making this up.) Then it's almost stable enough to use. Still not convenient, but manageable.
Also, it's a good thing I only use it on the weekends as it takes 5 minutes of grinding to get enough coffee for my 1 liter press pot. You know I used to grind coffee for a month at a time in the grocery store and I bought this because I was tired of my coffee-flavored coffee having a hint of hazel nut latte because the idiots in the store couldn't read the "No Flavored Coffee" sign on the grinder. Maybe it's time to pony up the $200 to get an electric ceramic mill. Or maybe I could attach an electric drill to the top of this one! It's Saturday and I am not doing anything else today. Hold my beer and watch this.

title: You get what you pay for, in this case...
text:
I've been using Amazon to make purchases for many years, hundreds of items and I have never left a single review. Just felt I'd leave that for others. I've been feeling more and more compelled to start leaving reviews lately but haven't gotten around to it. Laziness, I guess. So with all that being said, this is the straw that broke the camels back, so to speak. For the last 11 or 12 years, I've been using a 12 piece "Emerill All-Clad" non-stick set that was given to me as a gift. Most pieces in this set saw daily use. As my kids grew older and got more adventurous in the kitchen, they started using these and well...abused them by using metal utensils, stacking them on top of each other in the cupboards when putting them away, etc. It drove me nuts but at the same time, was happy to see them getting into cooking. Well, time (and the kids) have taken their toll on them and a few items need replacing, particularly the saute pans. The non-stick surface is non-existent and they are getting increasingly more and more frustrating to cook with.

So with that stage being set, I began looking into a replacement set. Not having the kind of spare cash laying around to purchase an identical (or near) replacement set (approximately $200), I started looking "lower on the ladder". I came across this set, saw it was pretty highly rated and yet very affordable. Read through many reviews, saw descriptions like solid, heavy bottom, sturdy feel, etc. etc and thought I'd go ahead and make the plunge. For the price, I wasn't expecting them to match the Emerill All Clads in quality but I felt they'd be suitable for my needs, so I ordered them.

I live within 2 miles from an Amazon warehouse. This means that about 95% of the items I order that say "Sold by Amazon" arrive at my doorstep within 2 days, even when I select the free standard shipping that says it will take 5-7 days or whatever it says. Honestly, I don't pay attention to it because I know that it will arrive sooner than what it says. So when this order sat around for 4 or 5 days without being shipped, I started getting frustrated. On day 4 or 5 I checked the shipping status and it had still not been shipped but I also noticed that the price had gone down approximately $15 from when I had originally placed the order. It still gave me the option to cancel, so I did and re-ordered at the lower price. Oddly enough, the new order showed it shipped the same day I ordered, and as with previous orders, it showed up on my doorstep 2 days later.

First thing I noticed as I pulled the first piece out, was how disappointingly cheap and thin they felt. I would definitely NOT describe these as being "heavy bottomed" by any means. They felt like a sets of pots and pans that were worth every penny I paid for them and that's not a compliment. I continued to pull the next piece out, though I'm not really sure why because at this point, in my head I had already thought to myself "I'm not keeping these". As I got further into the box, I pulled out a lid for one of the stock pots and it was broken and swing around. It had become detached from it's connective piece, which upon further inspection, looks like it includes a plastic washer? I know the lids don't normally see direct heat but you're definitely not going to be using these in the oven. Anyway, at this point I boxed it all back up and clicked the "Return Item" button for I think, the very first time, as far as I can remember.

Maybe I had too high of expectations or maybe I'm spoiled and it's just an unfair comparison. I obviously never got a chance to cook with these so I can't comment on how that turned out but I had visions of scorched food and blackened pan bottoms in my head. Guess I'll just have to deal with my current set for now and save up for a step up in quality. For 2-3 times the price, I'm gonna stick with the non-stick (no pun intended) Emeril All-Clads. I just can't see this set having any longevity to them, but again, that's just speculation on my part.

title: Personal Injury (Burn) Hazard and Inconvenient Features
text:
I just received this coffee maker today and therefore cannot comment on its performance as of yet. But I feel that users/potential users should be aware of a burn hazard this coffee maker poses.

The (glass) carafe has a hollow, plastic handle. My wife placed the carafe in the dishwasher for initial cleaning and was burned by scalding hot water when she removed it from the dishwasher. The carafe has a hollow, plastic handle with an opening at the hilt of the handle. She placed the carafe upside down on the upper dishwasher rack as you would place a drinking glass (obviously so that dishwasher water would get up into the carafe and drain out again). That placement made the open end of the hollow handle point upward, so the handle filled up with hot dishwasher water, but it had no way to drain out. Not realizing that the handle was full of hot water, she spilled it on herself, causing a painful burn. If you place the carafe in your dishwasher, be aware that the handle will be full of hot water when you take it out of the dishwasher.

In addition to the burn hazard, the coffee maker is aggravating because the instructions say to unplug it when not in use but it only has a one-minute memory hold for the settings. Therefore everything has to be reset each time it is plugged back in for use.

title: Unusable due to Overheating/Sweating
text:
The protector is indeed noiseless, and it did not change the feel of our mattress. However, this product is completely unusable due to the heat it traps in the bed.

My wife and I keep the house cool (~67 degrees) at night and always sleep with the fan on. We have NEVER had a problem with overheating in the bed until we bought this product. Since buying this product we have been having huge overheating/sweating issues. We've literally been woken up in the middle of the night in a pool of our own sweat.

We tried throwing off the cover and sleeping only with the sheets, which helped slightly but still we woke up the next morning drenched in sweat. The next night we tested sleeping with the sheets and cover, but with no mattress protector, and ... success. Comfortable, cool sleep all night. No sweat.

I don't know if this is a problem inherent in all waterproof mattress protectors as we've never used one before, but the heat makes this product unusable. Complete waste of money.

title: So far, so good -- but I'm not expecting miracles!
text:
Buying non-stick cookware these days can be a nightmare. Over the past decade I've purchased three pricy sets (Calphalon, Scan Pan, and Anolon), each promising to provide years of non-stick cooking excellence. Well, they all failed - and they all failed within the first year. So when I purchased this T-Fal set, I wasn't expecting much. The major benefit, I thought, was the price - even if it didn't last, at least I wasn't investing a small fortune. I could buy ten sets of T-Fal for the price of one set of Calphalon!

So, what's the verdict? The T-Fal works as well as any of the pricier pans ever did. The pans aren't as heavy and expensive-feeling as the others I've owned. But the handles are comfortable (and they stay cool during cooking), you can use them in the oven (at 350 degrees), and the lids are glass with little holes for venting steam (ensuring that the pans won't overheat). I like the size of the 5-quart Dutch oven, which has a larger surface area than most such large pots (and I like the steamer basket that fits inside - it's great for steaming veggies). The two sauce pans are nicely sized, too - the little 1-quart pan is perfect for whipping up a quick sauce. The skillets are definitely smaller than those included with my pricier sets - I'm not sure what I'll use the tiny 8-inch skillet for. But the other two skillets (9.5 and 11 inches) are perfectly serviceable, especially since I'm usually just cooking for two. I did purchase two larger T-Fal skillets separately to supplement this set.

Are they really non-stick? Yes! But then so were my other sets . . . at first. The instructions for use are pretty much the same for all of the non-stick cookware I've used: 1) "season" the pans with a little vegetable oil before first use, 2) avoid high heat, 3) allow hot pans to cool before exposing them to cold water, 4) avoid cooking sprays, and 5) use plastic utensils. And I'm following these directions, hoping that this time my pots and pans will last long enough for me to fall in love with them. But yes, they do work as advertised.

But why did my previous pans (which were much more expensive) fail within the first year of use? I'm not sure. And that's my concern now. Because if I don't know what went wrong with the other pans, how can I prevent things from going wrong with these? But so far, I'm happy with this cookware set. I'm also not expecting miracles. If these pans last a year, I'll feel my money was well-spent.

Aside from the cutting board issue, this is a pretty decent value. I like it. And I am picky about my kitchen/pantry stuff.

title: Good Set of Ventless Logs
text:
We purchased these 24" ventless gas logs from Lowes to replace our old gas logs. Few things we noticed installing this unit is make sure you have masonry screws on hand to secure the unit to the floor of your fireplace, they're not included. Installation was easy and took approximately 30 minutes. Receiver and remote/thermostat were easy to program as well. Longest part of the whole process was laying out the logs because ours came unlabeled.

The remote is a nice feature. Note if you are expecting to use the remote with this unit, your pilot light has to remain lit. Otherwise, I recommend turning the pilot off while not in use. With the pilot constantly lit it can use approximately 8 gallons a month alone.

Another thing we noticed is there is a little bit of a lag on the thermostat setting, we even took our remote on the porch when it was 50 degrees out and the thermostat reading remained at 75.

All in all this is a good little unit. The ember tray adds extra ambiance and the logs themselves add just enough heat for our living area.

title: Gear Levered Juicer!!
text:
As a veteran bartender I will tell you this is one of the best juicers on the market. I used this at my bar for years and the material holds up well to the abuse of commercial dishwashers and constant use. We use to have the metal ones with the paint coating and let me tell you do NOT buy those!!!!! First- they pivot at the point above the cup which does not go in line with the force you are exerting on the handles and thus less juice. This awesome geared hinge changes the fulcrum to a point closer and right over the cup to allow more directly in line with your hand pressure.
Second the painted ones with all the exposure to the citrus acid and being banged around started to flake off paint into the drinks I was making!!! yeah not cool.....
The only suggestion I would love to see from chef'n is a super deluxe model made out of heavy duty stainless steel handles-- sure the cost would be probably up around $100 but for commercial use in the bar it would be awesome. After 3 years of constant use at the bar we had to get a new one as the handles on the old one began to flex too much that they would touch at only 50% squeeze and thus would yield less juice but 3 years of use in a bar every day....and to replace it for only $20 what a deal.

title: Best product on the market for the price
text:
This desk is great! I spent a long time looking for standing desk options, but they all seemed too expensive. I found this option and immediately was interested. The shipping was delayed, but I assume that was a problem with the shipping company and not with the company.

Assembly
Putting this together was a breeze, I'm pretty handy but I think someone with minimal skills would be able to accomplish this without too much effort. All the tools and hardware you need is provided, and it went together pretty quickly. I'd say I had the whole thing together in about 90 minutes (including mounting the desktop).

Quality
The quality of this product is very high. There are other options out there which cost more and may be better, quieter, etc. But for the price, this is the best product currently on the market. It is solid and extremely stable. The only thing I wish it had would be better cable management, especially for going up and down. But it's not something that would prevent me from wanting to purchase it again.

Use
I got this to be the first standup desk in our office so my colleagues could also give it try. That means it goes up and down and is adjusted quite a bit. So far so good, I've had it for over a month and it is still in great working condition.

Overall, I highly recommend this product to anyone considering a standup desk option. I got a desktop from IKEA to mount to the top of this instead of the standard one which comes with it, which took a bit of extra work but the end result is great. I'm looking forward to using this product for years to come!

The king size shams are HUGE, but shrank to the correct size after washing in hot water and long drying time. So, this means that the quilt will also shrink, so launder with care. I plan to wash in cold and line dry because I love the size it is now.
I purchased the quilt in part due to the rich chocolate brown border shown in the photo. Turns out this border is a purple and taupe paisley, not dark brown. The colors are slightly less vibrant than the photo and I was initially disappointed by this but after a short time decided I like it very much.
The weight is what I would consider mid-weight. It is constructed surprisingly well.
This quilt fits well in my contemporary country home. The black pieces match our black framed contemporary art nicely.The overall pattern is masculine enough for a man, and I enjoy the small floral patterned pieces that are not overly flowery.
The quilting is printed on the fabric, but the all-over vermicelli stitching does a great job at making it look as if the quilt were pieced.
A great variety of throw pillows and sheets will work with this quilt, which is nice. It has so many colors, you could put practically any color throw with it. I gave it 3 stars instead of 4 because the colors were less vibrant than the photo and the shrinkage is worrisome, otherwise I really like it.

title: gimmicky lid jams frequently and is hard to clean
text:
I really wanted to like this mug, but the finicky top is driving me crazy. The double wall steel bottom works great and keeps my tea or coffee hot for hours. The spill-proof top uses a weird internal clicky seal mechanism. You're supposed to click down on a button in the middle of the lid to open it and drink. Unfortunately, this mechanism frequently jams and I have to disassemble it and put it back together to make it work again. You also need to disassemble it to clean it (important if you use cream or sugar or other moldy substances). Disassembly is not an easy or obvious process, so I hate each time I have to do this.

Desktop mugs really do not have to be spill-proof. The wide bottom on these mugs already reduces the risk of spilling. Why couldn't they use a much simpler lid that just keeps your drink hot without being so complex to clean or even keep working smoothly? For the price of this mug, I expect a better design.

title: Not well made -- pieces don't fit together properly
text:
This corner shelf unit could have been useful and attractive, but it is not well made. The parts don’t fit together as well as they should, which caused the end result to be slightly cockeyed (see the pictures I’ve posted with this review). Additionally, the screws actually caused the wood to crack in places, which is clearly visible in the finished product. And to make matters worse, the shelf is not level – it’s unstable enough to make it unsuitable for displaying any fragile items.

I do like the look of this shelf, and had it been a better quality product, I would have been happy to use it in my home. Assembly was fairly easy (and you don’t need any additional tools to put this together – an Allen wrench is included, which is the only thing necessary to attach the screws). But the wooden dowels, which should be uniform, are slightly different in width and length. This made it impossible to put the shelf together without some of the pieces lining up incorrectly (and I tried several times). And there was an odd bluish stain on a prominent piece of the wood, near the top of the shelf -- this is very noticeable in the finished product.

Bottom line, had I actually paid money for this, I would have returned it. It is definitely not worth the $60 price tag.

title: Dont buy the Medium unless you like sleeping on Rocks
text:
Bed is well made and arrived quickly. The manufacturing quality looks great and the Charcoal layer does in fact sleep cooler than other "Gel" memory foam mattresses I have tried.

However the firmness rating of "Medium" is totally Deceptive by normal US standards. The sleep feel is a VERY big disappointment after so many "good" reviews. Both the Foam and inner springs are VERY, VERY hard as a result only your pressure points such as Hip, Shoulder etc contact the lower layer and it puts LOTS of pressure on your joints. I'm 210 and 5' 9" so pretty average and a slide sleeper so perhaps if you were 110 lb light weight back sleeper you might like this but if you move around or try your side, forget it!

I have a 13 bedroom cabin and have bought hundreds of mattresses Serta, Sleep Number, Simmons, as well as a few from Amazon. This is by far one of the least comfortable mattress I have ever slept on, my hip and neck are hurting right now and I have been up 3 hours.

After 2 weeks or break in including asking my kids to jump on it for an hour its still hurts to sleep on.
Maybe the Medium Plush is softer but we are Returning this one! Hopefully Amazon will let us get something more comfortable.

PS: Amazon called and is working with us to get a new mattress so thanks!

title: Make Some Room In Your Baking Cabinet!
text:
I've now used this on 6 different recipes so far, and all have turned out wonderfully. They all were perfectly baked through, yet moist. The outsides were evenly golden. If you wait at least the suggested 20 minutes, they practically jump out when turned over onto a rack. I have sprayed with Pam each time before piping the dough into the cavities. A tip to accomplish this with the least mess, BTW, is to put the pan on your open dishwasher door, then spray away. No having to clean up the counter from overspray.

Clean up is very easy with hot, soapy water. If anything sticks, an old toothbrush will make quick work of it. Most of the water runs off quickly, so air drying takes very little time. This astoundingly flexible pan must be used on a cookie sheet for stabilization while filling the wells and during baking. Many have already mentioned the cotton sack for storage, which is an appreciated touch.

As for the recipes, the email contained 2 links, each with only 2 recipes apiece, one of which was Paleo. You'll find, however, no shortage of phenomenal recipes by googling "baked donut recipes." I have found some extraordinary ones, such as the ones I've already made: knock-off Entenmann's crumb donuts (first picture - even better than the real thing!) triple chocolate with chocolate glaze, chocolate with vanilla glaze, browned butter with strawberry glaze, and apple spice with cinnamon sugar (all in the second picture.) Have also made banana buttermilk donuts with maple glaze. The results of each were items I was very proud to serve. Not even one bad recipe yet.

Baked donut recipes seem to follow the same, basic procedure: whisk the dry ingredients in a bowl, combine the wet ingredients (including the egg) and fold them together gently. No mixer. For the most tender crumb, light hand mixing is best. Most bake in under 12 minutes. So you can make them in less time than it takes to find your keys, jump in the car and drive to your favorite donut store, wait in line to order, then reverse the process. Plus, they'll be exquisitely fresh, unlike some you get in a donut shop later in the day. You can even satisfy a late night craving, while in your PJs. What's not to like?

I have found that filling the cavities 3/4 full gives the best shaped donuts. To test for proper doneness, the easiest way is to lightly touch the tops. When they give some resistance and spring back, i.e. no impression is left, they're done. When it comes to this pan, believe the overwhelming preponderance of the reviews. If you're like me, the last thing you want is another piece of baking equipment to store. But in this case, after dragging my feet for the better part of a year, I'm so glad I took the plunge. Don't do what I did. Just buy it, already!!

title: It delivers, and how !!
text: I wish I could give this 7 stars for what this contraption is able to produce - a light, airy and abundant froth that will give the most skillful employees in Starbucks a run for their money. I love my cappuccino and to be able to make a better one at home than the best coffee shops with the help of this Norpro frother is so awesome and economical. I have now used this for over a month. After a couple of tries in the beginning I figured how to get the perfect froth every time. Its no rocket science. Use 2% cold milk, fill it to the graduated line and pump for about 30 - 40 times when you will see some froth build up. Then take out the pump and put the glass beaker in the microwave. In about 40-50 seconds the milk heats up and so does the froth from the cold milk. As the froth heats, it will expand, become airy and rise up. Keep an eye on the beaker in the microwave so that you can stop the microwave just as the froth reaches the brim. This heated froth is not only light and airy but also more stable than the one that you achieved by pumping the cold milk. Mix the milk in the fresh brewed coffee and then mix half the froth into the coffee as well. Spoon the rest of the froth over the coffee to get a thick crown (like on a beer). Sprinkle some chocolate/cinnamon/allspice powder and enjoy a perfectly crafted cappuccino and say goodbye to the coffee shops who rip you off. I have even made one in spill-proof steel mug, taken to office and still found a decent froth floating on it after about an hour. I am ordering one more of this frother because the glass beaker is really thin and fragile and as reported by many reviewers, may break if it were to knock against the kitchen sink or tap. That is the only drawback but it should not stop you from buying this otherwise perfect contraption.

title: I took off two stars for the noise and light but it works very well for my purposes.
text:
THE NOISE
I read the reviews on several brands and models of air purifiers and landed on this one. For the price, it met my needs better than the others in that it covers a much larger area than one medium-sized room. That said, it is LOUD! I expected it to be somewhat noisy, but absolutely never dreamed it could possibly be THIS loud!! Reviewers said it was loud but the word "loud" is subjective; what may be really disturbing to one person can be practically imperceptible to another. For example, it was likened to running a box fan on high by many reviewers. What they didn't mention is that they meant the old metal ones that grandma was always warning you not to stick your tongue in, NOT any fan meant for residential use manufactured within the last 40 years! I bought this air purifier for two reasons: to remove cigarette smoke, and to make the air more pleasant to breathe near a large rat cage that doesn't get cleaned nearly as often as it should. I ALWAYS kept an oscillating fan, running on low, to circulate the air near that cage so I didn't think it would be much different noise-wise than that. Unfortunately, this air purifier is almost as loud on low as that table fan is when set to high.

THE BLUE LIGHT
And while I'm complaining, I may as well mention that the blue light that everyone is complaining about is SO much brighter than any human would think possible. I can't imagine why they did that, I mean, it is REALLY disturbing! I can't take any pictures or video of how truly offending it is because one of the very first things I did was cover it. Well, I attempted to cover it. It isn't just one light, it's a circle of evil blue laser light that is emitted ALL around the dial, which makes it practically impossible to cover without hindering the function of the dial. Masking tape does NOTHING to lessen the sheer determination of this light, even with several layers. As ugly as super thick, silver duct tape is, I would certainly go that route if I had any. With limited options at my disposal, I chose to use about 30 brown paper sack essential oil label stickers, layered, of course. I can still see the light, oh yes, even THROUGH the thick, brown paper, but at least it's low enough now that it doesn't light up the ceiling in a dark room anymore. (Yes, it seriously does!)

FUNCTION
At first, I really didn't think it was doing much. The first day it arrived I happened to have several people over and they were ALL smoking so I fired it up and hoped it did its job. It didn't seem much better to me, as it was REALLY smoky in here and, as I mentioned, it's WAY too loud to watch tv or hear any music or have a conversation with it on high so I kept it on medium or low most of the time. The next day was okay but again, I wasn't sure if it was working or not, maybe a little better than it would have been without it, I don't know. Either way, I thought it helped a bit with the rat cage smell and with flu season upon us, I thought I may as well let it run and clean some air. It's also super dusty in here, no matter how often I dust (not that I do, I'm just saying, it gets REALLY dusty either way). Even so, I'm afraid I didn't have that amazing experience of checking the filter and finding it full, either. In fact, it was surprisingly clean. It had SOME dust on it but after running practically constantly for a full month right in the high-traffic center of the living room/dining room/kitchen, having two huge rats, a constantly shedding dog, and one or more smokers, not a lot going on there. BUT, I turned it off the other day. Yes. I did it. I don't know why I did it but I won't do it again! Not two minutes after I turned it off the whole living room started to smell like rat pee! EWWW!! I mean, BAD! So, being the responsible adult I am *cough cough*, I cleaned the cage. Ah, all better. Then I smoked a cigarette. The first in a month without the purifier on, mind you. And it stunk up the whole apartment in a way that makes me wonder how I could stand to smoke inside before I got the air purifier! It was like I had thrown a party in the 70s, such that I could literally see the smoke hanging in the air, as I had so many times before. I had forgotten about that, in one short month I had forgotten about that smoke hanging in the air and having to open windows in the freezing cold to try to get some fresh air circulating. I really should have known how hard it was working, I did have other clues, like when I go to use the bathroom, it's always smoky in there while the air in the main living area smells fine. When I go to bed, I can smell smoke stronger in there even though I don't smoke anywhere but one spot in the dining room, furthest from the other rooms. So the filter isn't full, I can live with that. It's clearly doing what I bought it for. Who knows, maybe my HEPA filter vacuum is doing its job, too?

title: Live up to its hype
text:
I am not going to repeat what others have said but will highlight a few important points:

1. One thing to keep in mind that while the cooking time with this is much shorter than regular cooking methods, you need to factor in the time it takes to boil the water and create enough steam to reach the right pressure. For better results, you want it to sit a little after cooking to get better results, which also takes some time. So it is not really "instant" but it does make many cooking jobs much faster.

2. I am Chinese and my wife is Japanese so we have dedicated cookwares to make rice, and we know how a pot of good rice looks and tastes like. If you don't have these, I can tell you the rice made by the Instant Pot is as good if not better than what we usually get. You add rice and water to the pot in a 1:1 ratio (eg., 1 cup each), select "Rice" and the actual cooking time is 10 min. You could manually release the pressure immediately or let it sit for 5-10 min, depending on whether you like the rice to have some texture or softer.

3. While you can use it to steam, but the food, whether it is vegetable or sausage, can be soggy. For vegetables they also turn yellow. So while Instant pot can steam (and of course it can), a dedicated steamer may work better for some of the food.

4. I personally think this is best for making stew and soup that usually takes hours and this can cut down the cooking time to be around 30 min. Since you can also sauté in it, you do not need to sauté in another device and then transfer it to the pot for making soup, as two steps can be combined in the same device.

title: A few problems, but fair replacement policies
text:
I bought a Sun's Tea tumbler in July 2012 and after the first washing the bottom glass split away in a perfect circle. As I remember it, they sent me a replacement that was missing the seal in the lid, which they again replaced. Finally, I was happy with the product, and I handwashed it to ensure it wouldn't break again. In December 2012 I bought a second one of these tumblers as a backup since I use it a lot. Just this last week I had left my tumbler somewhere, so I finally got out my trusty replacement from its packaging. First, the filter just flops out and doesn't snap in place like it should, and then after one hand washing, I just tried to make tea in it again, and the glass on the bottom is cracked. Nothing was done to it to cause this to happen. I'd say after FOUR problems with two orders, that is unacceptable.
UPDATE July 30, 2015: Although my replacement tumbler was in storage and unused longer than the standard guarantee period, when I finally used it and it cracked the company did send me another replacement. I have increased my rating because this company does seem to make an effort to correct problems in a timely way even if there are some quality issues. Another observation is that from what I have seen you have to pay a decent amount more money to get a tumbler with tea strainer of much better quality.

title: How to Get the Crock Pot WeMo Slow Cooker Connected to your WiFI and Cell Phone.
text: I haven't actually cooked in it yet and I'll update this post after I try it out several times. This will be a new experience for me because I have never used a slow cooker, but the advantages of having a meal ready for the whole family at the end of the day has convinced me to try. I'm posting this info NOW to help everyone else who might be having trouble getting the cooker to be recognized by their cell phone. Like a lot of folks I had a fit with it at first, but thanks to D. Diesness's instructions and some determined experimenting, I finally got it figured out. Here goes. First, before you start, write down your home internet password and have it handy. Next download the WE-MO App to your cell phone, tablet, or whatever. My cell phone uses Android so I downloaded the program from Google Apps. Finding the app on line and downloading it takes all of a minute or so. Next, the trick is to RESET the cooker to its factory original settings. I had to do this several times. Slide your fingers down the edge of the right side of the black control panel on the front of the cooker and you'll find a button near the bottom right. Unplug the cooker from the wall. Now, press and hold the reset button down WHILE plugging it back in. This will reset it. Once the WiFi icon on the front of your cooker stops blinking orange and then green, and finally goes to a steady green light (which will take a couple of minutes every time you have to reset it) your cell phone will recognize the cooker and add it to it's list of WI-FI connections. What really confused me was what to do next. Here's the next critical part, open your cell phone's "Settings" Menu, and hit the WiFi tab, then scroll down your cell phone's list of available Wi-Fi Connections to the one that says "WeMo.SlowCooker".  Tap on the entry for the cooker and see it if gives you the option to select the word "Connect". If you have that option, choose it. If you don't, you'll have to do another factory reset. I had to do this several times. Once you are able to hit the word connect, close or minimize the WiFi selection screen and open the WeMo App. The app will almost immediately recognize the cooker and tell you to start setting up the programming by hitting "Start". First it will ask you to take a photo of the cooker and even re-name it if you like. Then it will ask for your email address so enter that, from there follow the directions, a couple of screens later it will show a list of available WIFI networks (yours, your neighbors, etc. just like your cell phone would show). Pick yours. Then it will ask you to type in your network password and save it. It will then go through the process of verifying the network and once it completes that process which can take several minutes, it will tell you that you can now access your cooker. The thing that threw me off for a number of tries was that I was afraid, I was re-setting my cell phone network to the wrong network by telling the cooker to connect to my WiFi. However, once the WeMo program recognizes the cooker, then your cell phone setting will return to its normal WiFi connection. Having done this, all you have to do to get the cooker ready to use remotely is to open the WeMo Tab on your cell phone and go to the picture of your cooker. The WeMo app will detect the cooker if it's plugged in and tell you if it is turned on or off, etc.and let you change heat and time settings, start, stop, etc.. Hope this helps!

title: Easy to use and amazing results until...
text:
Update: The last couple of times I've used this the cooling function hasn't worked. The yogurt was kind of lukewarm and after cooling in the fridge it didn't taste like much of anything. I made a batch with my non-electric, thermal yogurt maker and it was great, so it's not the starter. Too bad, because I liked being able to set it and forget it. So I've downgraded it to 3 stars.

I had my doubts about making good yogurt without heating the milk, but I wanted to give it a try. I used whole organic milk and followed the directions for Plain Yogurt Variation #2 exactly. I set it for 8 hours, but checked after 6 to see if it was done yet. It wasn't, so I let it go the full 8 hours. Then I let it sit for 12 hours in the cool mode and this morning I opened it to find the thickest, creamiest yogurt I've ever made. I'll never go back to all that fuss, and I know I'll make yogurt much more frequently.
Those who have not had success may need to try a different starter culture - I'm using the heirloom yogurt I made with Cultures for Health Bulgarian starter culture.
Be sure to read all the Tips and Hints and follow the directions exactly. With the right starter and the right milk, you will have wonderful results.

title: Not ready for prime time -- App comes up very short - creating a frustrating customer experience.
text:
As a vacuum, this is fine. As a smart vacuum, it has a long way to go. Purchased early May and have let it run for a month. The software doesn't seem to be able to map our house. For reference, it is a 2100 sq. foot floor plan. Every day, it goes through the same routine:
The robot starts a cleaning cycle - then runs out of battery. It returns to the charger, recharges and then starts again brand new!!??! I have no idea why it does not start from where it left off.

Additionally, the manual says that when it is first developing the map, it will move along the walls to map the space. My robot has never done this - it only starts cleaning, back and forth, in the room the charger is in.

Finally, the app is slightly misleading in so much as they advertise you can create spot cleaning zones or schedules or create barriers where you do not want the robot to go. In actuality, however, the app determines the "rooms or sections" of your house. Meaning if you have an open floor plan and it decides that your kitchen + dining area + family room are 1 section, you can never only clean the kitchen. You have to use the determined sections that the app made.

If they can fix the software, this would be an easy 5-star experience.

title: Not too bad... Can be amazing with some upgrades.
text:
I was skeptical when I first saw this, but I live in NYC and the 6 inch footprint seemed very appealing in our tiny apartment. I've had it for less than a week, and I'd have to say I'm pretty satisfied with it.

I think this machine would be a winner if Delonghi would only include a non-pressurised basket and a real steaming wand. I see other people online modifying their machines with great result. I can't wait to try out the upgrades.

PROS:

* Footprint - So tiny! Only 6 inches wide!
* Espresso - Produces thick crema
* Pressurised basket - More forgiving of grind size. It even produces thick crema from a spice grinder!
* Pannarello wand - The foam produced by the wand is consistently and shockingly good for almost no effort. No special training or technique required. You can definitely make latte art with it if you really try.

CONS:

* Lightweight - Need to take special care not to knock the machine over, especially when tightening the portafilter.
* Clearance between filter and tray - You can remove the tray for extra room, but if you don't, the clearance is pretty small. Only fits short cups or shot glasses.
* Pressurised basket - Extracts less flavor than a standard non-pressurised basket. The basket also pops out of the portafilter a lot when knocking out the puck.
* Pannarello wand - Nearly impossible to make amazing foam. Frustrating for people who know how to steam latte art quality milk, or prefer different density of foam.
* Single boiler - Only one boiler means it's a bit more trouble to make a cup of espresso AND steam milk. However, to be fair, double boilers are non-existent in this price range.

UPGRADES:

* Breville 50 mm portafilter (BES820XL/204)
* Breville 50 mm single wall filters
* Silvia v1/v2 steaming wand

Bought this for my Breville Smart Oven Air. I wasn't sure which size to buy, but the larger size 12x10x1 fits my Breville perfectly.

Pros:
- The sheet and rack set have a beautiful shiny silver mirror finish.
- It's dishwasher-safe!
- Very sturdy stainless steel
- No chemical coating
- Rust-resistant
- No warping

Cons:
- It says food releases easily but I think it still requires a bit of work

Pro Tip: Try to clean the pan immediately after using the pan and as soon as it's cool enough to handle. This really helps with preventing the food from getting stuck and becoming really hard to get off.

title: Good deal for this package of cast iron essentials
text:
This package came with many useful items!
The four scrapers are very durable and helped clean my grooved grilling cast iron well.
The rubber handle is snug and works very well for that hot iron.
The chainmail works pretty well. Almost to well, because you may over scrub your pan if used to rough. The chainmail has not rusted, but storing the sponge inside may leave that sponge a little wet and may become unsanitary. So I suggest removing the sponge when finish using it in the chainmail.
I have not used the two hangers that help dry the chainmail/sponge (because i have a place to hang my chainmail already), so I cannot give a helpful opinion.
Finally the weakest item in the box is the towel. The towel leaves lint on the pans while drying. Which is not good when seasoning the pans. I mainly use it for a second holder while handling my heavier pans.
Overall very good package for the price. I would recommend it for the deal.

I have to say that the replacement had no issues of the original filter and I have been fairly happy about it, once I was confident enough to try it following the first experience.

I'd give the good filter and customer service 5 stars but given the quality control issues that I originally had, I'm removing 2 stars.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (Dec/22/2019):
Horrible smell. This makes my Coway the biggest pollutant in the apartment.

title: Customer service not very helpful.
text:
The product when it works is great. It does have issues getting hung up on furniture or becoming stuck sometimes. I just moved the troublesome items out of the way so the vacuum can run without problems.
My real issue came up, when I started having problems with the vacuum not docking. The vacuum had trouble docking itself and would misalign. It then would not charge or run. I also started having issues with it not connecting to my WiFi and for a few days it would just randomly lose connection.
When I got thru to customer service, I was told that the connection issues were due to their main servers being down (at least 3 days). Since I was not notified (I'm sure other customers were not notified), I spent quite a bit of time trying to troubleshoot something I would not be able to fix.
As for the docking problem, the service rep had me clean, wipe, dust and blow out vents. He then wanted me to do a hard shut down. It was very difficult following the directions and unhooking and hooking the battery was next to impossible for me. I have arthritis and trying to stick my fingers into a tight space inside the vacuum to remove a tiny piece of plastic was very difficult. I am not sure where my call was connected to, but the connection was garbled, with quite a bit of static and it was very difficult to follow the directions.
Very poor technical help. Hoping all the troubleshooting I did will fix the vacuum. Purchase with caution.

title: wonderful curtain liners
text:
I'm not sure why there is a problem with measurement description, it clearly states total 54" two pieces 27".. Anyway I love these liners, used them in our RV for large front windows.. You need to make a little effort to make them work, however that isn't difficult.. I used pins to attach them to curtains [rv curtains are on rail, so you can't use curtain hooks] made a small over lap on each curtain connection & used velcro buttons to close that gap.. they block the light wonderfully, when your on the road or campground there are endless lights that make sleeping hard.. These turned out super for both blocking light and helping to keep sun out so rv was cooler and cold out to keep rv warm [dependent on weather]..
I'm sure if the same effort was made to place these on house curtains it would work there also... I'll add that comment when we get home and I put them up..
Oh and for other RV'ers we also used them on the sun roof panel [in shower] and over ceiling vent so light doesn't come in through there. I cut them to size and velcro buttons to attach them [that way you can remove as needed.. very easy...
so the long story is i love these curtains and they do the job beautifully....

title: Great audio video rack for the price but requires some modifications to handle heavy equipment on the bottom shelf.
text:
I recently purchased this from a different seller. Amazon didn't have it in stock when I was looking to order it.

I have two amps that weigh approximately 70lbs a piece and a processor that weighs approximately 30lbs. I wanted to install them all on the bottom rack. The middle and bottom shelves are only rated for 50lbs. The reason the bottom shelf is rated so low is there is no support in the middle. I find the 50lb rating to be too high in the stock form forget about going over that. I solved this by getting a piece of 2"x2" pine at the local hardware store. Keep in mind that a 2"x2" is actually 1.5" x 1.5". Unfortunately that is still a bit too thick to work. I shaved about 1/8 of inch off on one side using a table saw. I then painted it black. I used double sided tape to hold it to the center metal support under the bottom shelf. I also used carpet sliders on all parts that touch the ground since I am using this on carpet. I removed the front leveling screws and used carpet sliders there as well.
With the cut down 2x2 supporting the middle metal bar the lower rack is rock solid. It can now support the weight I need it to. I don't see a way to increase the middle rack capacity but doing what I described above will greatly increase the bottom shelf's capacity. I am surprised the manufacturer didn't do something similar with the stock design. In stock form the lower shelf bends with minimal weight. Not ideal for an audio video rack this wide.
I will try to post some pictures when I have a chance but it is fairly self explanatory. The metal bar in the middle underneath the bottom shelf needs to be supported if you want to put anything heavy on that shelf. The top shelf is designed to hold a heavy TV and it appears to be able to handle the weight. I am not installing a TV on the top shelf but I can tell that it can handle much more weight than the middle and bottom shelves.

Overall this is a great bargain for a three component wide audio video rack. I have searched and searched and was surprised how few three component wide racks there are. Not only that but I need one that was fairly low to the ground. This one fit all the criteria I needed but it couldn't handle the weight I needed it to in stock form. It just needs some simple modifications to be able to handle much more weight.

Update: I decided to install my center channel speaker on the second shelf instead of the top. It weighs ~30lbs. I also have an Oppo 95 Blu-ray player, Toshiba HD-XA2 HD DVD player, cable box, headphone amp, Wii, and a sling box all on that shelf. Needless to say it was bowing and needed to be modified. The easiest solution was to get a 1" dowel to add support between the middle and bottom shelf. I cut it to length, installed felt pads on both ends, and then painted it black. Now the center shelf is supported properly but only because I had already reinforced the bottom shelf.

With the modifications I have done this rack is doing the job I need it to do. I am still shocked the manufacturer didn't design it to handle more weight but I imagine most people are not using the way I am. In stock form even the 50lb weight rating is a joke. It bows with only a slight push. With my fairly simple and inexpensive modifications this rack is rock solid and a bargain.

I posted a few pictures to help explain.

title: Wow - this is amazing!
text:
I enjoy coffee, espresso, and drinks like cappucino. I'm definitely not an expert or a snob when it comes to these types of drinks. For some background, I have experimented with brewing at home using a french press, one of those cone brewers, and another pod brewing system (the Senseo from years ago). Yeah, a french press does a good job and is pretty easy to use, but not easy enough apparently because it's never caught on in my home. Something like the Nespresso appeals to me because it seems almost completely effortless to use (place pod in machine and push button).

My purchase came with the Vertuoline Evoluo machine, a milk frother, and some pods for sampling (8 coffee pods, and 4 espresso pods).

The Nespresso Vertuoline Evoluo brews with special Vertuoline pods -- there are Original Line pods (these are older and don't work with this machine), and the newer Vertuoline pods. When I was first researching which pods to buy, some places online don't seem to clearly indicate if they are the Original Pods or the Vertuoline pods, so that's something to keep in mind if you're shopping for them.

The main Nespresso machine is very simple. You fill the reservoir with water, place the pod in the machine and push 1 button. It scans the pod to know how to brew it (coffeee vs espresso), and within about 90 seconds your beverage is brewed. When you open the machine again (to put a new pod in) the used pod automatically falls in to a bin on the side of the machine for disposal later.

My first test was with one of the included coffee samples, and honestly, I was completely shocked at how good it was. Such a smooth, velvety texture... really delicious. Quite frankly I felt like I must have been doing something wrong when brewing my own coffee previously, because compared to that this is very clearly a far superior beverage than what I am used to. Again, I'm not a coffee snob, but as far as I'm concerned this produces superior coffee than what I am used to, even stuff I have gotten from coffee shops and restaurants, and I'm very pleased with it.

The milk frother is quite easy to use as well. Pour in some milk up to the fill line and push a button, less than 90 seconds later it's done. Very easy. I used it to make Cappucino with one of the sample espresso pods and it turned out great. The only just flat out negative thing I can say about this entire package is the milk frother could be easier to clean and have a better design. It's not hard to clean, just compared to the Nespresso machine which requires basically zero effort, the frother does require a little effort (rinsing out, washing with soap and water after each use). The whisk portion of the frother is very small and attaches magnetically (fairly weakly) and seems like it could fall off easily and be easy to lose. The frother is still a very nice machine and works well despite this concern.

Pros:
- Looks nice, was worried it would look like cheap plastic based on photos I saw online, but it looks very nice in person
- Nearly effortless to use and maintain the Nespresso machine
- Brews excellent coffee and espresso
- Temperature is just right

Cons:
- I'm used to drinking a little more coffee at a time and wish that it brewed larger cups. It fills my coffee cup (albeit a fairly large one, 14-16oz I think) a little more than half way. I guess I'll have to get used to "European" style. The old Senseo machine only brewed like 4 ounces of coffee so this is a step up from that I guess! UPDATE - I discovered that you can customize the brewing amount. It explains it in the instruction manual. My fault for not reading it...but you can fairly easily adjust how much it will brew.
- Milk frother whisks seem like they could be easy to lose
- Pods aren't available hardly anywhere. Online stores like Amazon have them listed, but all from 3rd party sellers with high markups. Nespresso's own web site seems to be the best place to get them but they have a minimum order of 50 at a time. You'll be looking at about a $50 bill every time you want to order coffee. I can't find them at any brick & mortar stores.
- Not a ton of variety with the pods that are available. It's all good for me, but compared to something like Keurig the selection seems pretty limited.

Overall, despite the cons listed above, I'm ecstatic with the purchase and would get one again in a heartbeat.
