title: Disappointed
text:
I was super excited to get this clock, which made my disappointment so much worse. It is absolutely beautiful, but that’s where it stops. Here are all the cons:
-The light is WAY too bright, even on the dimmest setting
-The system sounds are WAY too loud and can’t be muted—no idea why it has to make a noise every time you click a button. This means I have to have it set BEFORE my baby goes down for the night because if I forget, the just the loud process of setting the alarm wakes her up...
-The “sound control” is not volume control. It’s a function that allows the display to turn off until a sound or tap turns it on. I’ve found that a tap doesn’t work, I have to physically lift the clock and bring it back down on the nightstand for it to turn on. And when my baby wakes up crying at night, the super bright display turns on and now I have both a crying baby and a flashlight-level light shining in the room. It’s so bright when it comes on that your eyes have to actually adjust to it.
-The controls are not common sense. There are only 3 buttons for the many functions needed. None are intuitive...like holding down the “down” button for three seconds before the sound (or was it light?) control to pop up.
-The weekday/weekend alarm option applies to all alarms simultaneously. So you can’t set a weekend alarm and a weekday alarm. It’s just that you can set weekday alarms that don’t go off on the weekend.
-the plug has another blinding red light
The date display is very weird: the year is huge and center and the month and day are tiny and in the bottom corner...like I’m more likely to forget what year it is???
-Regarless of how many alarms you have set, only one alarm light turns on. So you can’t tell from the alarm interface whether that’s just one alarm or all three. I would have liked a dot per set alarm.

This clock looks nice, but that’s where the buck stops. I absolutely hate it and wish I had saved the money.

Please don’t buy it!!

title: I have been looking for good cookware since living on my own as a young ...
text: The big question here, should I spend $500+ on this cookware, and why? Short answer is yes. Yes you should. But why should you buy this cookware set? After all, there're other brands that cost drastically less. And if you ever saw this cookware in person, you might laugh at the price tag, and scoff at the obscurity that a pan should cost this much. I know I did. I have been looking for good cookware since living on my own as a young adult. And I did what every young adult does, I bought a cheap $30 Teflon cookware set. It was a great 1st set, and there is nothing wrong with a starter set. But I'd get a few months of service out of them before the Teflon started chipping away, and i'd have to replace my cookware yearly, only to repeat this process all over again. Since then we've tried other types of cookware. From ceramic to cast iron, and other types of stainless cookware, and the only thing that worked was Cast Iron. And I love my cast iron set, but anyone who has cooked on cast iron will tell you, it gets heavy after awhile. I eventually stumbled onto All-Clad. I spent months, struggling with my apprehension, trying to decide if I should "Invest" into these pots and pans. Seeing them on sale, I finally put myself out of my misery, and purchased this set. Once the pans arrived in the mail, I rushed home to see if I've squandered my money. I washed the pans and immediately began testing. I tested the pan in the most brutal fashion I could think of, the fried egg test. The egg sizzled, and popped in the pan. When it was time to flip, I braced myself for the struggle I would inevitably face, trying to un-stick this stubborn egg from my pan. Instead, the egg moved effortlessly. I was in disbelief, laughing to myself about what just happened. So I cook another egg just to be sure it wasn't beginners luck. The egg never stuck to the pan, and I flipped the egg over without a spatula. I still didn't believe it, so I cooked a pancake, then oatmeal, a sandwich, stir fry, mash potato's.... and fast forward to today... I couldn't imagine life without these pans now. They can handle the simplest of tasks, and they perform these tasks flawlessly. Do you want a pan that heats up fast? These will work. You want even heating? No Problem. You want non-stick? Got you covered. Are they well built? Yes. Is this worth spending over $500? Easily. What is my favorite thing about these pans? Watching a cooking show, and seeing these exact pans in the show. Doesn't matter if its on TV, the internet, or cook books. You'll see these pans in the background, and smile. If this is your first time using Stainless Steel Cookware, do yourself a favor and watch a few Youtube video's on the subject. "How to cook with Stainless Steel." It'll save you from writing a bad review on this product. Anyways, hope this helps someone.

title: TERRIBLE DRM, TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE.
text:
TERRIBLE DRM, TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE.

Shame on Keurig. We picked up this model to replace our Tassimo. I have a Keurig at my office, and liked the system much more than our Tassimo. My wife also picked up some "Brewed by Keurig - works in all Keurig Brewers" pods afterwards. We immediately got the oops screen. I called the number on listed, and spoke with a rep (on a land line). The connection was crystal clear, and the rep took me through the process of setting up a keurig account online. She informed me that I would get a free box of K Cup pods. When I asked her what we are to do with the two boxes of pods that don't work (we put them in our storage drawers), she got very quiet. Then, "Mr. Benz? Are you there?" Nothing changed with the quality of our connection - it was crystal clear and I could hear her breathing. She was pretending that our connection was bad to avoid telling me "sorry sir, you are SOL - the boxes are opened and you can't return them now." "I can plainly hear you, and I don't believe that we have a bad connection - this is ridiculous," I informed her. For the sake of her standpoint she kept saying "are you there?", then thanked me for calling keurig and hung up on me.

I don't really blame her for this - she probably gets this all day long owing to her company's idiotic policy of introducing DRM to their coffee pods.

A quick google search showed me that all I have to do is cut out the top of a used 2.0 pod and tape it to the reader of the machine for it to brew any coffee pod out there. This is an extremely easy fix, of which I am glad. This begs the question however, concerning the knuckleheads running the company. How many people have been burned by an idiotic policy of introducing DRM to coffee? They have completely alienated their customers. I sincerely hope there is a worthy competing product out there to buy when we get rid of this unit.

While I would have been happy to buy their official pods, now I will be going out of my way to buy non-keurig 2.0 licensed pods going forward. I'm voting with my dollars against idiotic company policies.

title: A nice, and heavy, set of steak knives
text:
One of the great mysteries is what makes a "great knife" - regardless if it is a chef's knife, steak knife, or a hunting blade. I can't say that I am absolute expert when it comes to the finer aesthetic details, but I can help when it comes to the metal that is used.

18/8 stainless is what people in the steel industry call 304 (at least in the USA). It contains 18% chromium (where as a rule of thumb anything over 12% is considered stainless) and 8% nickel, it is non-magnetic, and definitely stainless. However , in the world of stainless steels it is rather low end (and in my opinion the germans are not necessarily superior... my preference would be the stuff made in the good ol' USA). Another issue is that it is relatively soft and doesn't hold a great edge.

18/10 (Which is what this set is) - Contains 18% chromium and 10% nickel. The increased nickel buys you a bit more strength (so theoretically it should hold a better edge) and it makes it a bit more resistant to certain acids. However, it become a bit more susceptible to stress corrosion cracking (Which for a typical knife is a non-issue). Again, the Germans really don't have any particular advantage in the production of 316 stainless steel.

410, 416, 420, 440 stainless - I am going to group them all together - these are marginally stainless steel blades (Wash them and dry them after use... never let them rest metal-on-metal with other grades of steel especially in the presence of salt). They are magnetic and will stick to a magnet. The advantage is that they can hold a much better edge since these grades of stainless steel can be made much harder than both 18/8 and 18/10 (and it is not even close). Again, in the world of stainless steel these are all low-end and inexpensive grades.

The exotics - 154CM ( a high end grade), Tool steels (A2, D6, and etc) and the CPM grades ... most (but not all) are not stainless although they will have varying degrees of resistance to rust. The primarily advantage is that these grades can be made both very sharp and tough (think swords). Some of these grades are quite exotic and can be very expensive. While the exotic grades can make a lot of sense for a high end set of chef knives I am not sure why you would want them in steak knives.... well.... unless you ear A LOT of flippin' steak.

Soooooo..... back to the Black Pakka Wood steak knife set.... when it says that it uses "18/10 German made blade" I yawn and am thoroughly unimpressed. However, the knives are very heavy and feel very substantial in your hand- definitely not flimsy. They do seem very well built even if they are not a metallurgical wonder.

The knives seem well balanced. The have a nice sharp tip that transitions into a serrated edge....I can confirm 100% that it will cut grilled chicken with minimal effort.

The set also comes with a nice (not super great) storage case. The knives essentially fit into slits into the wood for storage. Again, it is nice but it certainly will not impress the Queen of England.

Final Verdict - A nice set of knives - they definitely have the weight and look that shouts "I was not bought at a dollar store" . My personal preference would probably be a set made out of the 400 series stainless steels like either a 440 or 420, but that is probably a bit of overkill.

title: Terrific Product, Thoughtfully Designed, Easy to Assemble.
text: I love my new workbench.  It comes delivered in a heavy box, so best to have the delivery guy bring into the garage or area where you're going to actually assemble.  They advise having 2 people to assemble, but I did it myself at age 63.  The key is laying out all the pieces first on the cardboard from the box or a blanket/towel (to avoid scratches) and to use leverage for the heaviest piece - the wood table top.  The instructions are clear, and all the pieces are labeled as what part they are and the labels include arrows to indicate "top", and "front" or "back" which of course you need to pay attention to to avoid re-work, but the labels are exquisitely clear.  The assembly really was a breeze and I did it myself in a "relaxed" 3.5 hours while listening to music in my garage.  Everything fit and they give you the right amount of hardware with a separate package of extra screws and bolts.  They give you a screwdriver and a wonderfully designed wrench for the bolts.  It's hard to describe but one step requires using the wrench to tighten bolts on the supports for the pegboard and there's these really thoughtfully designed cutouts in the grooves of the supports so you can use the angled wrench in complete circles to make bolting this piece really easy.  Just great engineering with the convenience of the customer in mind.  I'm using this with a Trinity Tool Chest I got at Costco and the height of the table and chest match virtually perfectly. As you can tell I was really impressed with the thoughtfulness in design, ease in assembly, and the usability of this product.  Highly recommended.

title: foldability/portability is an advantage
text:
The PVC material is very thick. The bag is really waterproof. I placed ice and water in it and it didn't leak.

It's a wine ice bag with handles. The handles indicate you're meant to carry it - carry it to a friend's house as a gift? carry it to the park? It's an ice bag so you're supposed to fill it with ice to cool the wine. You can either bring the ice bag folded, with wine bottle and bag of ice separate or carry the wine bottle and ice in the ice bag. Your drive or walk, to wherever you're going, must necessarily be short otherwise the ice will melt and you'll be carrying a bag of sloshing water. That's very awkward.

I actually thought at first that I'll use the ice bag with gel packs, instead of real ice, so I wouldn't have that melting ice/sloshing water problem. I tried but there's not enough room to put gel packs on either side of the wine bottle unless I'm able to find really small/thin gel packs. To be fair, the ice bag is not advertised to be used with gel packs.

I suppose, the advantage of this ice bag, as a wine cooler, is that it's foldable. But if you're going to bring this along as a wine cooler (to e.g., a park), you'll need a separate real cooler (insulated) to keep the ice in. Then, once you're at the park, you can put the ice and wine in the ice bag. But what would be the point of that if you already have the real insulated cooler with you? Well, the ice bag would make it convenient to have the wine bottle out and staying cool instead of stashed away in the real insulated cooler. :) Is that way overthinking the issue? I'm just trying to find the advantage of having this with us while listening to a concert at Millennium Park in Chicago. I'm imagining the logistics of having to stop at a store to get a bag of ice, carry the bag of ice to the park,... (Keep in mind that when you're in downtown Chicago, it's much more practical to take the bus/train or a taxi/Uber than to bring your car and park it for hours.) At the end of the concert, we throw out the melted ice, dump the empty wine bottle in a recycling bin and just carry the now folded ice bag home. Now, that is more practical than carrying a real bulky ice bucket.

See photos:
photo 1- wine bottle with real nicely packed ice around it
photo 2 - my failed attempt to use ice gel packs

I think these reusable ice cubes (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0000CFPNN/ref=olp_product_details?ie=UTF8&me=) may be small enough for the ice bag.

title: Worst bookshelf ever!
text: Worst bookshelf ever! My package arrived with multiple issues. Unfortunately they were all not discovered until things were almost unpacked and assembly had begun. Originally it seemed that the defects were so small they could be overlooked but it turned out different. The box was already torn up and it was too heavy and would be too much trouble to repack and send it back at that point. At first we noticed that the holes in the pieces looked like a dull drill bit was used which caused damage to the ebony finish around each one. There was a huge scrape on one of the shelves which exposed the pressed wood. This damage was not due to shipping since the piece was packed in the middle of other similar ones which had no damage and they were all covered in the same packing material. There was a large bubble in the laminate of one of the shelves. Finally, the drill holes on the side of several "I" panels were completely missing. This, of course, caused additional visible damage as the screws were secured. The quality control of this product was not a focus and this defective unit was shipped. One of the most difficult and time consuming bookcases to assemble. Never from this company again due to their design. This is the only furniture kit piece I have purchased that required 2 people to assemble, which is normally a simple task. Enclosed are some photos during unpacking and construction. Very disappointed and frustrated.

title: A step backwards from Keurig 1.0 in functionality!
text:
Every once in a while I come across a purchase that I really regret, this one is it out of all my purchases for the 2015 Christmas season.
When Keurig only had single serving machines in the past, it was a great idea and worked great for work place, but not really a time or money saver for families with multiple drinkers. With Keurig 2.0, the carafe concept seems to solve that problem (especially when using refillable baskets), but after 1 month use, it's definitely not ready for prime time.
The biggest problem is capacity, the most it can brew at one time is "4-5 cups", or about 25oz. For people who drink coffee from mugs, this makes 1.5 mugs of coffee, not enough for 2, but too much for one. So this really is not any more convenient for family use.
The second problem is the user interface, it really needs to go back to the drawing board. Below are the problems:
1. It defaults to 3-4 cups every time. You can change it, but you have to change it EVERY SINGLE time, why not let users determine the default like Keurig 1.0?
2. The preset is lost the moment the carafe or any part of the coffee maker is disturbed, and you have to go through the whole reset all over again. Keurig 1.0 has the preset in memory, but not Keurig 2.0.
3. You can not access the menu until after it preheats! This is truly ludicrous. If I want to set the pre-brew time at night for the next morning's brew,you have to wait about a minute for the machine to preheat, then to access the menu for preset (because it can't save any presets!). Or, if you accidentally touched something on the machine, it loses it's preset, you now have to wait for it to preheat and then re-enter the setting. This is a huge waste of energy and time.

Keurig: If you are listening, put in a ROM memory so it can store presets!!!! Or just take the firmware from Keurig 1.0 and put it into this!

title: Not necessarily better than the previous generation....
text:
I always eagerly await new simplehuman sensor pumps, because I have them all over my house. Currently, I have the previous generation, [[ASIN:B00GHWOVBY simplehuman 8 oz. Sensor Pump with Soap Sample, White]], and the six I have in my house have been great for almost 2.5 years at this point.

This new model is 9oz, whereas mine are 8oz, but the first impression is that, wow - this is significantly larger than my 8oz model. It's quite wide and imposing, though - on the plus side - build quality is significantly improved. No longer is there a flap lid that feels like it is going to break every time you open it - now it's a fully removable, and weighty - lid. For such a large device, though, it's surprising it only holds one additional ounce of soap. If you turn the unit over, you can view up the see-through bottom how little space in the pump is actually used for the soap container - about half. The rest is a plastic funnel (likely hiding the battery) for pouring soap in. Why it needs a funnel is beyond me...

Also to note is the color looks more like brushed nickel than brushed stainless steel. Definitely a coppery tinge to it. Think of it as "brushed stainless steel with nickel" (that's the best description I can give it).

The charging cable is slightly peculiar. It's not peculiar in that it's now magnetic. It's just that the contacts are fully exposed. simplehuman says this sensor has an IP67 rating (so you can rinse it off), but it remains to be seen how well those contacts hold up. It's quite possible to have magnetic charging without exposed contacts, so perhaps we'll see that in the next model.

New for this model, too, is the ability to place your hands in different places along the front side's sensor to determine how much soap comes out. This is a good idea in theory. In reality, though, it's pretty hard to put your hand underneath at exactly the right place for the exact amount of soap you want, and it leaves me missing my button-adjustable models like the previous generation. To get a tiny amount of soap, you need to place your hand quite far up the body of the pump, very close to the dispensing opening. On several occasions, I've almost knocked the thing over or touched the dispensing head. Neither of these things is good...

And the last downgrade over the previous generation is that you can no longer see how much soap you have in the dispenser. I really like with my previous generation simplehuman that I can, at a glance, see how much soap is remaining through the back. Prepare to be surprised with this model when all of a sudden no soap comes out in X number of weeks/months. You can, however, lift the pump up and stair up the plastic bottom to sort-of figure it out, but... yeah... no. I can't see a reason there wasn't a see-through slit cut into the lower portion of the back of this pump to show you how much soap is remaining. Maybe the next model.

Overall, this isn't a bad pump. It works similarly to the last-generation model, with some "improvements" (depending on how you look at things). But really the only positive thing I can say for absolute certainty is that it definitely FEELS more premium. I just wish its function matched that feel.

3.5 out of 5. OK.

title: Above-Average Drip Coffee Maker
text:
This is a nice “above-average” drip coffee maker. It’s very easy to set using the controls on the front top portion of the machine. I like that it has a reusable gold tone filter. It has a water filter you can use, if desired. . . but. . . I have a separate water filter I use for all of my drinking /cooking, so this extra filter is not necessary for me. The heating pad keeps the coffee nice and hot. Like with most drip coffee makers, it has an “anti-drip” system, meaning you can pull the pot out before it has brewed completely. .. but. . . this really drives me crazy when people do this. . .. because. . . when the coffee first comes out, it’s very strong. At the end of the brewing cycle the coffee that comes out is weak. So if you take a cup of coffee out of the pot before it has finished brewing, then that cup will be too strong, and the rest of the pot will be weak.

This coffee maker has a very “streamlined” look to it. Overall I like it just fine. I don’t think there is anything super special about it. Even though it’s Made in China, it’s still affordable at the current seventy-dollar price.

title: GOOD, but other reviews seem to exagerate a bit.
text:
I got this because I am on the slim fast diet which has two meal replacement shakes a day. And you make those by mixing the powder with fat free milk. And my second shake is usually while I am out of the house. I live in LA so the weather hit triple digits regularly through august and September and I didn't want the milk to spoil.

First things first, it does keep things cold, however I would say that there was some definite exageration about HOW long and HOW cold things are kept. If i just make my shake and put it in the bottle at normal refrigeration temperature it will stay cool for about 4 hours which is all I really need while I am indoors the whole time. If I put some ice in the shake it will stay cold for about 6-8 hours with the ice fully melted by the 8th hours.

Still it does exactly what I need and if you are using this to keep drinks like water or juice cold it will do a great job especially with some ice.

I recommend leaving the empty, clean bottle in the freezer or refrigerator with the lid off the night before so the metal gets cold on the inside and that will give you quite a few hours extra in cooled insulation.

Oh and a quick note, that matte finish does scrape off fairly easily, and my bottle is only ever on my desk, in my fridge, in my car's cup holder or in my purse.

title: Cotton Candy Dreams!
text:
Ive decided since there are not enough reviews to make one for this cotton candy machine.

First off I was also one of those people that owned one of those 30-40 dollar cotton candy machines and yes they are more for novelty than anything else. I love cotton candy and always buy it when i see it as a fair. So for me, paying 3-8 dollars for a little cotton candy I would much rather own this and be the fun uncle and eat it whenever i want for 240.

Lets start about when I got it. First off mine came warped on a leg. It was smashed in so check your machine when you get it. I will not deduct stars for this because its mostly likely cause was shipping. Besides that it came well packaged and i fixed mine and kept it

The machine itself is VERY well built. But i expected that for the cost. It was very simple to use and had well enough instructions. If its heated up correctly its more like 3 seconds for cotton candy so be ready.

It makes a ton of cotton candy and fast. I used the gold medal stuff 3 for 25 which was an amazing deal. You can make a cone within 20 seconds and you could feed an army fast!

It comes with spare belts, spare fuse, and a wonderful floss scooper!

Cleanup is so easy as you put it over the sink and i have a spray attachment on my sink so you just melt the candy away.

I made about 8 cones and shoved them in tuperware for later! Yum!

All in all for the price i give this a 5/5! Its a wonderful deal and if you want more than a thimble of cotton candy from the 30 dollar machine, this one can satisfy!

Enjoy!

title: Well-made Dispenser
text:
Had to get a replacement bathroom soap dispenser. The one I had had a stainless steel top that rusted. This plastic pump is not as elegant but at least it will never rust.

This came in two pieces: the body and the spout. You line up the two holes in the pump and insert the spout. Priming the pump took quite a bit of work - so much that I thought it was broken. But once the soap got going it's worked well. The pump motion is smooth, and it dispenses quite a bit of product. (If it's too much for you, don't depress the pump as far.) The container holds a lot of product. The opening at the top is an okay size; not the smallest I've seen, but not the largest. If your hand isn't steady enough, try using a funnel. The tube that extends into the container is precisely cut so it goes straight down, rather than curving as you see in some other.

Only drawbacks are minor. Because the spout is not secure, it can twist a bit. But that easily fixed. The other issue that arises is also related to the fact the spout is simply inserted. Product leaks a bit on the inside and outside, and some product remains in the spout. I use clear soap, so it's difficult to see, but I imagine if you use soap or lotion that is orange, blue, white, or whatever color, the leakage and remainder in the spout will be quite evident. If that doesn't bother you, consider this well-made dispenser.

Since the pan is light weight, I was able to lift the pan and flip crepe a few times or use a metal spatula to do the job (yes, you can! No more worries about non-stick coating, as there is none!).

Hope Amazon would carry De Buyer Blue Steel Saute Pan soon...

title: 3rd world build quality. Beware of the FAKE 5 Star reviews. Don’t believe them.
text: This machine worked as promised for 3 days then broke. Now, it just recirculates the air within the room. This machine has 3rd world build quality. Nothing about this machine was engineered, it was built out of piece-meal parts, which is why it looks decidedly unsleek. They bolted a fan on to a cheap refrigerator. Then they developed a case to fit around their Frankenstein-esque creation, that’s why everything is blocky; parts sticking out everywhere. They drain pan is at the bottom and requires you to tip it over a ledge, again, the product of poor engineering. If you return it within 30 days, Amazon will take it back and pay the shipping. If you return it after 30 days, you have to pay shipping and return it to manufacturer in ORIGINAL PACKAGING. They clearly paid a company to write fake reviews. Ask yourself why a company you’ve never heard of has triple the reviews of Honeywell or LG?!?! Also, note all the paid Amazon sponsorship. Their strategy was, build an AC as cheap as possible, with slightly better specs than trusted companies, then price it similarly. Even the “Verified purchase” reviews can be faked. There are Chinese companies will pay people to buy the machine, write a review, then the product back to Amazon. Don’t be fooled.

title: Expensive, but so worth it. Don't bother with the plastic covered wire ones if you can afford these.
text: We purchased 5 of these; 3 small, 1 medium and this large one. We wanted to move our spices, which were clear over there in the pantry, closer to the stove and countertop. This set completely took up one shelf of the upper cabinet, but so worth it. I was worried that I'd be giving up that "precious near the stove, and well within reach space" with things that would be a nightmare to install and difficult to use. My concerns were completely unfounded. I installed them myself in no time at all - maybe an hour and a half for all 5, but I was taking my time to make sure I did it right. They *slide smoothly* and they slide *all the way out*. The *rubber bands are perfect*. They hold everything in, but don't make it hard to get them out. When placing them, nudge them away from the side with the hinges. Otherwise, if the door isn't open all the way, the one near the hinge will hit the door and, if you're in a hurry, it'll leave a mark. (It's on the inside, so who cares.) Also, this hasn't happened with these, but rather with a similar one we have for our pots and pans. That one has some real heft to it and the corresponding cabinet door doesn't _like_ to open all the way. If you can afford them, get them. Then you won't have to replace your cheaper ,plastic covered, hang on the inside of the cabinet door type when you realize how much you hate them, even though they work great and do help with the problem of the stuff in the back of the cupboard rotting because you can't get to it.

title: Best cup warmer ever!
text:
This cup warmer is the best thing for our tea drinking habit! We used to fix large cups of tea for my husband and I and then end up finishing off a cold cup of tea, having to reheat the same cup of tea multiple times in the microwave, or dumping cold tea down the drain and fixing another hot cup of tea. Now...we can have up to a 16 oz. cup, filled with tea and it NEVER gets cold! Or any cup up to 3 7/8" in diameter.....wich is actually a big cup! We have used a cup on this warmer that is 3 7/8" in diameter and the contents of the cup stayed piping hot. My husband has used a very tall narrow cup on this warmer and it stayed piping hot the entire time.

The warmer does NOT have an auto shut-off or an in-line switch on the cord. The power switch is on the front side of the warmer and takes very little pressure to turn on and off. Do NOT put your fingers (or any other part of your skin) on the red warming plate once it is turned on. It warms up quite quickly and takes several minutes to cool off once the power is turned off as well. PLEASE USE COMMON SENSE WHILE USING THIS PRODUCT! When the fluid level is low in the cup, the fluid becomes more than hot enough to burn the inside of your mouth.....sip carefully!

As you see in the pictures, I am using a different/larger cup that is thicker than the cup that comes with the warmer. This cup still stays piping hot. My plate needs to be wiped clean, but you can see that when it is on, there is a red light that is emitted from around the power button on the front. The picture of the bottom shows that there are rubber feet that are slightly lower than the cup warming device so that air can circulate underneath it. Do not block the vent on the bottom side. If you smell burning rubber then it is advised that you smell the underside to be sure there isn't an electrical short causing the smell of burning wire insulation coming from inside of it. The power cord is 6' 4" (or 64") long and also comes with a small velcro cord tie on it. That way, if the cord is too long, just tie the excess off to keep your area nice, neat, and orderly. I have had half a cup of tea (the cup in the picture) and the temperature is 130 degrees Fahrenheit.

Several people have complained about a foul odor when they first used this warming plate. Yes, it was there. I would say that it lasted several hours but it was nothing bad enough to make us turn either of our cup warmers off or to stop using them. One review stated that this odor caused his/her drink to taste the same as the odor. We did not find this to be true with ours. I would think that this person may actually inhale lightly when sipping his/her drink which can make anything taste funny.

I would recommend this cup warmer to anyone who enjoys a hot drink every time they pick up their cup. The plate wipes off easily with a damp rag. NEVER submerge the product in water!

All in all, this is the BEST cup warmer I have ever seen or owned!

title: YES! these DO keep their seal in the freezer!
text:
These, work perfectly if you remember to do a few simple things:
1. Wrap moist food lightly in plastic wrap, cling wrap or press N seal. If freezing, freeze liquids like sauces in flat containers (like lock n lock), remove when frozen and wrap, or place into a regular zip bag with the zipper cut off, then put into the foodsaver bag. This enables you to reuse the foodsaver bag later.
2. Press some of the air out of the bag. Press the zip strip firmly on a hard surface two or three times. Use the back of a butter knife or spoon to ensure the bag is tightly sealed.
3. Place the sealer firmly over the vacuum hole. Start the vacuum process and twist/wiggle the sealer a tiny bit to ensure a good seal. For added security, place a small piece of freezer tape over the hole.

The manufacturer said these bags were "not recommended" for the freezer because they "might" not hold the seal. I tested this... THEY DO HOLD, if you seal them correctly. I make portions of meats and cheese for sandwiches, fruit, vegetables, and other items and wanted to be able to remove a portion and reseal the bag and return it to the freezer. These re-sealable bags are perfect for that.

Remember though, for use in freezer or refrigerator, you must blanch vegetables before sealing. Especially broccoli which gives off gasses when sealed fresh, Read the manual ( I know, I usually don't either) but this manual has important information and no one wants to take a chance and either waste food or worse, get sick. To freeze fruits, wash, dry, peel, slice and freeze on cookie sheets first. Place in zipper bag then into the foodsaver bag. Take out what you need and reseal. For long term storage use the regular foodsaver bags or rolls.

Obviously these are terrific for non freezer and non refrigerator storage too. All your pantry items will stay fresh seemingly forever.
Like me, you will wonder how you ever lived without this system and these bags.

text:
I love having these popsicle molds! I was looking for an option that would allow me to use my own popsicle sticks, as opposed to the ones with the plastic drip guards (drip guards may be convenient, but just don't feel super chic....).

We read some complaints about people having difficulty removing their frozen pops. When it's time to remove the pops, we just place the mold in a pan filled with warm water for a couple of minutes, and they slide out pretty easily. For cleaning, we don't place them in the dishwasher – just let them soak in warm soapy water for a bit, and scrub out any stubborn bits with a bottle brush.

Overall, these work perfectly for my needs, and my husband and I have had fun creating a ton of different flavors. title: Nothing near non-stick results
text:
The first time I used my All-Clad Stainless Steel 10" Frying Pan (I bought the 10 piece $700 set through Amazon), I can't get it clean. I tried to follow instructions and turned down the heat on my electric burner from the usual 5+ to 4 and cooked 5 eggs with 4 ice cubes and a cover. The eggs steamed over with soft yokes in about the same time as in the past using my cheap non-stick 10" skillet. However, I cannot get this pan even close to clean using plastic scrubbing pad or brush or scouring sponge (harsh soaps and no metal cleaning devices). I have the Bar Keepers Friend Cleanser and Polish ordered but not received. My experience with the 3 Qt pan is very similar except not as severe from using it to fry hash-brown potatoes with vegetable oil in the bottom. In both cases as mentioned I turned down the heat.

This set was a Christmas gift for my wife because she loves to cook as well and we have a 20 yr-old Teflon coated set that works great but not as pretty or highly recommended. title: Large and in charge, but do wash with caution.
text:
The di Oro silicone spatulas are by far the largest cooking utensils I own. I honestly giggled when I opened the box because of their enormous size. The long turner spatula was a big as my hand and the standard turner spatula was bigger than my palm. Granted, my hands are on the smaller size, but the spatulas’ surface areas are laughable. The large size, though, is completely advantageous when lifting and/or turning many large ingredients. For instance, you can use the round spatula to glide under an entire pancake to flip it. You can also slide under a fish fillet and transfer it from pan to plate without part of the fish hanging off and possibly breaking.

The spatulas are heat-resistant up to 600 degrees Fahrenheit. This makes them great tools when lifting proteins and other items from a dish straight out of the oven. I have limited counter space when cooking so I usually leave my cooking utensils on a holder in the middle of my electric stove. The spatulas’ heat resistance prevents any melting or discoloration while around hot electric burners.

Silicone is chemically stable so it won’t react with food and liquids nor will it release vapors over its lifetime of use. This BPA-free material makes the spatulas safe to use in any kitchen. They are also nonstick so you can use them with any pans you own without causing damage. Food will not stick so it’s easy to maneuver your ingredients when cooking. Please advise that when certain items are extremely oily, they can slip off the surface of the spatula. I think this issue is common with most nonstick utensils, but with caution, you shouldn’t have any problems with food flying away.

The handle has a matted texture so it is easy to maintain a strong grip even when your hands are wet. There is also an indentation on each handle for your thumb to support your grip. The body of the spatula is made of stainless steel which increases the strength and durability of the product while providing flexibility.

The spatulas are dishwasher safe and their nonstick quality makes them even easier to clean. However, there are gaps present on the handle where the silicone meets stainless steel. Whether you wash by hand or a dishwasher, water can get trapped in these gaps if they are not dried properly. This can lead to the growth of mold, yeast, and bacteria. I highly recommend you dry these spatulas with the handles up so that any water trapped in the handle drips down. (And please do the same with similar items.)

These spatulas are made of quality materials. The only negative aspect of this product is the attachment of the handles. I would still recommend this set to anyone, especially at a $24.99 price point. Just keep in mind that you need to dry these properly to avoid any growths.

Please Note: I purchased this spatula set at a discounted price for an impartial evaluation as written in the product review above.

title: Easy to use, perfect results!
text:
Prior to this purchase, I hadn't used a deep fryer in about 30 years. I wanted to make fish and chips, clam cakes and dough boys (fried dough) for my family and then for a summer party later on. Though I was a bit apprehensive, I purchased two units for this purpose. Well, I found the Secura 4.2L/17 Cup, 1700-Watt Stainless Steal Deep Fryer to be an excellent product. It was easy to use, easy to clean, and the cooking results were perfect every time! I am really happy to post this review. What I found to be the best characteristics are as follows: 1) The Baskets - I can fry two different foods in smaller quantities using the two small baskets or make a larger quantity of fries, etc in the single basket. Being able to wash the stainless steal baskets in the top of the dishwasher makes them easy to clean too. 2) Cover -The filter in the top of the cover, really works to control the smell of frying. The large handle makes the cover easy to remove and replace as needed. 3) Controls - Easy to see, easy to set, and having to use the timer provides some security that you won't leave the unit on accidentally. 4) Though other fryers have built in filtering/draining systems, I honestly found that pouring the used oil back in the bottle simple to do. The part that holds the oil is light weight and lifts off the unit easily. I then pour the oil through a strainer over a funnel back into the bottle. It's a snap! 5) RESULTS - every thing I have made in these fryers has cooked perfectly.
I really love this fryer and highly recommend it.

title: Good juicer w/great customer service and some small part reliability issues
text:
The features I like the best are:
1) The vertical system auto feeds most thick veggies like carrots, cucumbers, sliced beets & celery and anything you have to slice up to go through the vertical chute.
2) It has plenty of power as I've never stalled it the 20 mos. I've used it. One time it plugged and I just reversed it a few times to clear it.
3) Just the right amount of pulp gets through so you don't have to use the pulp screen on top of the supplied pitcher. The pulp is very fine and mostly stays in suspension in the juice.
4) The juice cap is very convenient allowing you to easily remove the pitcher of juice and put the pulp pitcher under the juice spout for rinsing.
5) Great customer service as I requested replacement of some small parts to be replaced under warranty.
Areas of improvement are:
1) The little tabs that hold the juice cap to the spout break easily If you accidentally bump the cap, when open, hard enough to knock it off the spout.
2) There's a little rubber plug in the bottom of the bowl that you remove each time you clean it that has a little strap used to retain the plug which breaks after repeated removals. Then you have to use a needle nose pliers to remove the plug.
3) Clean up: The biggest issue with all juicers is the time it takes to clean up after each use. The professional reviewers say this unit is one of the fastest to clean up. I don't have experience with other juicers and have to rely on their relative ratings; however, they all have a screen to clean which takes me from 7 to 10 minutes just for that part to remove the pulp with the included brush. I think the times the referenced reviewers give is to just rinse of the loose pulp from the parts. I wash/scrap the pulp off all the parts and then wash them in hot soapy water manually with a dish rag.
Other: The size/capacity of the bowl is not important in selecting a juicer as juice comes right through the screens and runs out the juice spout into your container and doesn't fill up the juicer bowl at all. I Juice 2/3 # of carrots, 1 cucumber, 1/2 med. size beet, 2 stalks of celery, 1 large clove of garlic, 1" of ginger, & 1/2 lemon and get about 500 ml of juice.

title: Some quality issues but get one that works and they rock... (Gotta love the return program)
text:
My first one smelled and overheated right out of the box, but after returning and replacing it my 2nd is working great 6 months on...

So I already have all 3 of the smaller sizes and I was thrilled when I saw this one come out. Well I naturally ordered it asap. And it came super fast so I immediately planned a dinner with the new awesome big crockpot... MY BAD... Thank goodness I was home that day... It smelled when started up and it was a little odd but I assumed it was just a protective coating burning off (You know like they have on engines) well after 30 minutes I came back to it and it still stunk but was running so I left it be. Then about 2 hours later I come back to a smelly cold crock pot. So I unplugged and replugged it and it started back up, then it really stunk and shut off again... Well Long story short we ended up ordering pizza...

I returned it and got a new one, this one works flawlessly... I made sure to fill the dish with water and test it for 8 hours on high though before ever cooking in it... The new one never stunk and the housing never feels too hot (it does get warm not so hot you can't touch it) .

So I ended up saying 4 stars because after the dud the 2nd one works like a champ and we use it weekly... TEST, TEST, TEST before cooking in it is my advice and return it for a another one if it fails the tests. Once you get a good one it will work great...

Just my thoughts,

AK

title: Modern Neutral Fabric, Classic Lines, Updated Mid-Century Design, and Comfortable for the Whole Family!
text: I bought the sofa in the Ceni collection by Bryght.  Since I can't figure out a way to review it on Bryght's website, and the couch isn't listed on Amazon, I figured this was the next best place to share my review.  My wife and 2 (soon to be 3) kids absolutely love this couch!  We paid $1049 for the couch (no tax and free shipping) and we couldn't be happier.  It's not the comfiest couch in the world but it's certainly not the most uncomfortable either, we think it sits right in the middle.  The cushions that rest next to the arm rest are the perfect touch and with out them the couch would not be nearly as comfortable.  Our whole family, not to mention our dog and cat can all fit comfortably on the couch.  I'm about 5ft7in and can lay down fully extended.  If some one is taller than me you can remove the 2 armrest cushions for extra added length.  The depth is great and it is very ergonomically designed to get cozy in many positions.  The fabric seems to be of very nice quality and the build of the couch seems to be something comparable to furniture at IKEA, not a knock to the quality, but just saying it's a pretty affordable couch so it feels like what I paid for it.  It also has 2 legs that sit hidden in the middle of the couch for extra strength and support, nice touch.  I would recommend this couch to someone who is looking for a modern neutral tone/fabric, classic lines, updated mid-century design (w/out being to obvious and trendy), adult look, and comfortable enough for the whole family to enjoy!  5 stars.

title: Great way to move some air around
text:
This is my third Dyson fan, and so far, it's proving to be one of my favorites.

Construction quality is first-rate with high quality parts and terrific finish. It's bigger than many fans, but there's something solid and reassuring about the size and shape. My oldest Dyson is in my home gym...it's several years old now, and it still works exactly like new.

You can position the fan to adjust the airflow in a few ways. Of course, it oscillates back and forth to spread air over a wide pattern. You can also tilt it forward or back, making it pretty easy to get the air where you want it.

At low speeds, the fan is fairly quieter - I'd say, it's quieter than a similar conventional fan. As you crank it up, it does get louder - but I only find it too loud when set on the top speed.

The heat is an interesting idea, but in my opinion, not strong enough to dramatically raise the temperature of a room. Still, if you want some airflow on a chilly day, it's just the thing for that.

Definitely one of the cooler luxury items I own...worth a look if you like the style.

title: 30 months later and still happy with the bed.
text:
When originally ordering this mattress I was disappointed (to say the least) that so many people decided to post rave reviews after only one week of use. There is no way to truly judge the quality of a mattress after just one week (unless you absolutely hate it). The bed arrived with no smells that I could detect, as some reviewers have mentioned. However, I ordered mine in the winter and perhaps ordering in the summer can cause the bed to develop an odor during shipping. After 7 months of use, there has been no loss of quality in the mattress. It still has the same soft upper layer with a firm underlying support as when it was originally unwrapped. I had a sleep number bed before this and have been using the bottom portion of that bed to support this mattress (it is basically a plastic box) and have had no issues. I expect this to last several more years, and will post an update at the 1 year mark.

Update: The bed is still comfortable and has no noticeable deformation or change after 2 and a half years of ownership. This bed has been moved to my guest room, which is where I sleep the 6 months of the year I am on night shift, so it does not get nightly use throughout the year any longer. I would estimate that it has gotten about 19 months of nightly use in the roughly 30 months I've owned it. Still a worthwhile bed in my opinion, and has been given a stamp of approval from my guests who have used it as well.

I spoke to a repsentive at Nespresso and he stated the most important things to do to protect the frother was: 1, clean after each use with a soft cloth, 2, do not use any metal tools to get out the whipped milk. title: Top starter gaming racing chair
text:
I consider this the best starter racing style gaming chair you can get. They are all about the same size, so if you're on the fence and want to try it out before dumping a lot of money on a chair, I think this is a 5 star chair for that.

Overall I think these are also a bit better than the Amazon Basics mid-back or high back chairs, and I consider leather, even PU leather, much better to sit on than the mesh chairs that are popular. The problem with PU is it will always peel, there's no way around that, and it's only going to really last a few years. Mesh will last a bit longer maybe but isn't really that comfortable.

The super expensive office chairs that I've had at work I don't think are at all worth it. But even if you think they are, they are just a lot more expensive.

This chair is easy to put together, it takes about 20-30 minutes max and everything is easy to tighten with the included allen wrench. The covers you have to screw in, and I might recommend a regular screwdriver, especially for the deeper holes. There is no hole on the seat cushion for those cover screws, but you don't really need any since the screws are shallow and will screw into the brackets anyway.

The chair does smell. Some of it is probably polyurethane and some of it is probably the off-gassing. I'm sure it will go away after a bit, but be prepared for that. Some of the surfaces are also a little dusty, but I used a simple multi-purpose cleaner spray and it came right off.

Chair tilts a little backwards, but when you sit on it, it feels straight so I guess that's just how it's supposed to be. The back rest has a tilt/recline feature, which you activate with a lever on the right side almost exactly like a car seat does.

The included lumbar and neck pillows are filled with some cheap cushion material and covered also in PU leather. The higher end chairs will give you velour covered memory foam. You can also buy those for $30-50 if you really want to as well.

I would say if you like this style of chair, the next real upgrades are real grain leather and Napa leather options. That will set you back $500+ and $700+ and you can really only get them from Noble Chairs or Secretlab. I plan to do this for the Napa at some point, albeit they are out of stock, and chances are the price will get closer to $1k. I am not fully sure if those will last longer either, you might just be better off buying this chair every few years instead.

As I wrote above, PU chairs are all pretty much the same. The material really doesn't change. They all seemingly use a nylon base, PU leather, steel frame and foam for the cushions. This chair says it uses a shaping sponge, while the others say they use cold cured foam. The cold cured foam maybe is a step above, and the velour with memory foam pillows probably are too, but I'm not sure that it's worth the $300+ most of the gaming racing chairs charge. I seriously think once you start going above this price point at $100-120 or so, the next upgrade has got to be in the upholstery, and nothing else really will matter as much.

Overall I'd give this chair a solid 3 or 4, but for the right person it's a 5. That's the problem with the rating system, I don't know exactly what you personally are looking for. An inexpensive chair that will last a couple of years or more and is in this style, it's a 5 easily. If you're looking for really high quality, and it's just a step for you, maybe it's a 3 or 4. But at this price point I can't justify anything below 5 stars, so I give it a 5, and I urge people that want to try this style out to seriously consider grabbing this one first, if they can't test out a higher priced chair for awhile and don't feel comfortable just dropping a higher price amount without testing something.

Edit 1 Week: Smell was really terrible for the first 2-3 days, but then faded and is fine/gone now. Might not be a bad idea to let this air out a few days somewhere.

The arms got wobbly and I had to re-tighten the bolts. I had to do this two times. Not sure if this will be a continuing issue or not.

I'm still undecided whether I will stick with this or go for a better leather version. I really don't want to get another PU version, so for that I'll probably stick with this. But if I see a good deal on the real leather and napa leather options I'm leaning towards getting that, and giving this one to someone else as a gift.

title: Beautiful well crafted walnut silverware tray
text:
[[VIDEOID:d7a952e1e8488f954c6e7eb8e596bb27]] [[VIDEOID:48d20cfb8c34ad5122167d5d52bc03fa]] This walnut silverware tray is very beautiful and made of solid wood that's joined together so smoothly that I couldn't feel any rough areas anywhere. I measured the tray to be 14" high x 10" across, with an outer height of 1 3/4" and the inner compartment height at 1 1/2".

There are 5 total compartments, and each of the four main compartment measures 2 1/2" across by 1 1/2" high (inner aspect), and the fifth compartment measures 2 3/4" across by 1 1/2" high. I own a silverware setting for 12 and the tray was able to accommodate all of my silverware in the main compartments and then my serving pieces fit into the fifth compartment.

My kitchen drawer's inner dimensions were 15" across x 20" deep and as you can see in the short video I made, the tray fit into it with ample room to spare. The silverware tray has four rubber disks on the bottom that keeps the tray from sliding around when I open and close the drawer as well.

The back of the tray is made of slats that have been glued together, but the workmanship of the one I received to sample was so good that I wouldn't have known that by looking at the grain or tone. One join up in the fifth compartment showed a very slight amount of light through when I examined it so I was able to determine that it was glued rather than solid, but the imperfection is so small that it doesn't show at all when the tray isn't held up to the light so I'm not deducting a star. Overall the workmanship is excellent and this piece should look gorgeous and last for years to come. It's a shame to hide it away in a drawer!

I purchased this item at a reduced cost for evaluation and review purposes.

The issue ofcourse was getting myself to spend $50 for 100 new hangers. I finally took the dive and made the switch. Omg what the hell took me so long? My closet looks amazing and these hangers look fantastic! I should add that I went with this particular brand because before I buy anything online I read the reviews. Although there are cheaper versions out, there were a few things (or complaints) that I took note of and that I didn't want to deal with: shedding (so many reviews spoke of small fiber hairs shedding all over their clothes and closet, some even included pictures) I don't have time for that headache and these do not do that at all, no swivel (another main complaint of other brands was the fact that the hangers were fixed to hang one way) I was hanging roughly 100 pieces of clothing and did not want to worry about putting the clothes on the right way. With the swivel I was able turn it the right way no matter how I hung the  clothes. Easy peasy! Lastly, breakage. I didn't want to deal with spending so much money on hangers only for them to break since I'd have a few heavy jackets to hang (another noted complaint of other brands was the hangers breaking). After hanging all my clothes I have not broken one. These are beautiful and very sturdy, lightweight and has created so much more room in my closet! Make the jump! I am highly satisfied and these hangers were worth every penny!

title: Terrific For Small Families
text:
I've had this slow cooker for almost a year, but waited to review it until I had some experience with it. I've cooked small roasts (about 2.5 pounds), a single chicken breast (for ginger-orange chicken), a single pork tenderloin and various soups and stews. It does very well at all of them. One thing I had to learn is that it takes a little longer to cook food than it does in my longtime pal, the 6qt Hamilton Beach Stay or Go, but this is not a bad thing. The purpose of a slow cooker is to gently cook food, after all. Low is stated as 200F, High at 212F. I think these are optimistic, as on High it doesn't really boil, but shows what most people would call a high simmer, with small bubbles appearing frequently. My Hamilton Beach, on the other hand, easily reaches a medium boil on High. The Cuisinart is also slower to reach maximum temperature, despite it's smaller size.

I only cook soup on High, and again it takes about 1 hour longer than my HB. Chuck roast (2.5 pounds) cooks in 7 hours on Low. A chicken breast reaches 165F in a little over an hour. Pork tenderloin is done (145F) in about 2.5-3 hours. One benefit to these lower temperatures compared to my HB is that lean meats more gently. My chicken breast is succulent, and instead of shredding into dry strings, it comes apart in chunks, or can be easily sliced. Pork tenderloin (I cut one in half and lay it end to end), is moist, tender, done to medium, and is moist and tender.

This is the first programmable slow cooker I've owned, and Ilove that I can program it to switch to Warm when cook time is up, so it requires less personal attention than my analog HB, with it's High, Low, and Warm dial. I've lately begin using it to thaw meat. It's thick insulated crock is perfect for this. I fill it about 2/3rds with warm water, drop in 1 pound of ground beef in a Ziplock bag and an hour or so later, the beef is thawed but still chilled, and bright pink all over.

All things considered, this is an outstanding slow cooker for a family of 2-4 people who don't want a mountain of leftovers.

title: Not heavy duty but they get the job done - and there's a LOT of them!
text:
First of all, you should be aware that these ship from China so they are gonna take awhile to get to you. Mine took about 17 days to arrive. I was in no hurry to receive them so that worked out fine for me.

For the price, you get a LOT of cupcake liners. You can make a whole lot of cupcakes before you run out of these. They actually come in two separate, clear, storage containers. The storage container is basic and cheap but it does the job, although the lid is a bit tricky to get back on.

These aren't heavy duty or anything, so don't have expectations of a high-end, high-quality paper on these liners. They are pretty thin. But, they do the job in that they are cupcake liners and they are decorative. And, after all, you are gonna throw them away so it isn't like you need card stock, right?

My only issue with these is that the way they are stacked, and because the paper is thin, it is VERY tricky to get them separated and, in trying to do so, I've ruined more than one - not that it tore but the thin paper crumpled up so it would no longer be attractive for serving. But, I think I'm getting the hang of it a little more.

And, the gold is actually a nice gold, not overly shiny and cheesy looking but only semi-shiny (satiny) and lustrous.

Overall though, you get a lot of liner for your money. If you want super heavy duty liners you'll be paying a lot more than this for 176 liners! These are gonna last me a long while, I'm sure.

Please note: I did receive this item at a discount or for free in exchange for my honest review of this product. And, my honest opinion is what you got. I don't get any incentive to leave a positive review. I don't get penalized for a negative review. I receive the discount (and then have to purchase the item) PRIOR to leaving a review (Obviously!) so there is nothing being held over my head (such as a demand for a high review) in order to receive such discount. I am sure there are many reviewers out there who give false positive reviews out of some perceived compulsion because they received a discount, but I am not one of them.

title: Happy plunging
text: Miracle product. Was dealing with a slow draining shower drain for weeks. Had tried the popular home remedies (plastic snake tool, baking soda and vinegar, Dawn dish soap) to no avail. I was starting to look into enzyme drain cleaners but they had such mixed reviews. I had hesitated on these drain plungers for the same reason. Finally bit the bullet on this one and my only regret is that I hadn't done it sooner. I had my doubts when I took it out the package because it was made of a flimsy plastic material. And it took a bit of trial and error to get my drain unclogged, but really only because I didn't have a good seal on the overflow drain. Make sure you do that not just to make the plunging effective but also because all sorts of gross gunk sprays out of it. Once I stuffed that overflow tightly, it only took a couple plunges for my shower drain to start running freely again. It helps to run the water a bit before you start plunging. Stamp it all the way down and then pull it up really quickly (like ripping off a bandaid). I'm very happy that I don't have to wash my feet and ankles twice every time I shower now.

title: The board is sturdy and the width seems like it would be a ...
text:
I researched ironing boards for three days before deciding on this one based on reviews on amazon and other sites as well. I received this ironing board last week and set it up today for the first time to do my ironing. The board is sturdy and the width seems like it would be a good surface to iron on. The pad and cover that came with it are more than adequate for ironing. It was easy to set up. However, it is not stable. This board wobbled so badly that I am afraid to use it. I tried it on different floor surfaces just to make sure it was not my floor. It is not. I did not see any instructions to help me mitigate uneven leg length. I like the looks of this ironing board but sadly it will have to go back. I intend to try another one like this and if that too is unstable, I'll be starting my research all over again. Disappointed.

Update 10.5.2015

My replacement board arrived and is stable. The higher adjustment is good for my back. The wide board s nice except that it's a bit too wide for some of my kids' clothes. I did get a sleeve press so that helps. My only issue is that the cover that comes with the board is not slick and fabric clings to it rather than sliding easily as you adjust the garment to iron in another area. This is annoying enough that I am in the market for a more slippery cover. I'm having to waste too much time to put down my iron, pick up the garment with both hands and adjust it's placement of the ironing board. In the past, I could just drag the garment into position with one hand. Bummer as covers for this size ironing board are not exactly cheap. Will be great for large items such as tablecloths or large clothes which my family doesn't own so I expect that I will be using my old narrower board as our clothes fit on it better. I like the board but would not buy again.

title: Stress-free, flawless waffles every time!
text:
WooOOoOOOO! I have not had a "stress-free" waffle in close to a decade, no kidding! I'd tried to buy this very waffle maker back then, and oddly enough kept getting shipped a crepe maker. So I gave up. Well, in all the years between, I've tried two top-of-the-line waffle makers: All-Clad and Breville. Neither model would let me extricate the waffle without a HUGE mess. Because those models are designed with a submerged waffle bed, I had to dig and pry and gouge and completely rip my waffle to shreds getting it up and out of the machine. The stress from years of totally unsuccessful waffle-making prompted me to DONATE my machines - both of them.

Then, I shopped at Amazon and found - to my amazement - the same wonderful waffle maker I'd had years ago (and was trying to replace, but kept getting the crepe maker?). This time I got the genuine article, and have rediscovered my LOVE for waffles. First time, every time, the waffles lift effortlessly off the griddle. How is that possible? Because of the waffle maker's superior design: the waffle sits UP on top of the griddle, with the lid making the deep imprint for Belgian waffle. When you lift the lid, you have about half an inch of waffle to grab hold of and lift off the griddle. I now get 4 perfect squares of waffle each and every time I put batter in the machine. EVERY TIME. It takes about 5-6 min to get 4 squares baked, an audible beeper signals when the griddle is hot and when the waffle is done (per your preference).

It may sound silly to say that making waffles cause stress, but seriously, hubs & I invented cuss words for the two previous models we'd owned. Now we can look forward to having waffles on a regular basis. Being vegan, there are many healthy, butter-free recipes to try. Healthy & delicious! I'm thrilled with this CucinaPro waffle maker.

title: Vornado 783 Full Size Whole Room Air Circulator
text:
The fan is pretty cool. New concept/design that can be appreciated.
Pros:
- Air output is definitely better than a standard floor fan

Cons:
- Even though it says it has multiple heights, it's not telescoping. You take off the extension, and now the fan be close to the floor. Or you add the extension and now the fan is somewhat tall. Also, the extension is secured with screws, so it's not something you can do on the fly like a standard telescoping fan
- The noise this puts out. I don't mind the noise, it's why we bought it mostly apart from the hot summer nights. But Level 1 is not loud enough, and Level 2 is too loud. Level 3 is just ridiculous. Don't expect to have a conversation within 7-8 feet of this fan when it's on High. HOWEVER, the air output at Level 3 is awesome!!
- No oscillation. I knew this when I bought it, but it's kind of a standard feature that all floor fans should have. I understand the technology in this fan should cancel out the need, but back to that Level 3 thing. If you are putting this in a decent size room 13x13 or bigger, it will need to be on Level 3 to try to get that effect of bouncing off the walls. On level 2 or lower, if I'm across the room I don't feel anything.

title: ... a few complaints about this and it sounds mostly like people don't realize what they are buying
text:
I've read a few complaints about this and it sounds mostly like people don't realize what they are buying. First this isn't a non stick surface, it's cast iron. If you've never cooked on cast iron clean up/care is a little different then you might be prepared for. For starters it's iron, it will rust very fast so don't leave water on it for any period of time, cover it as soon as it's cooled and don't even think about using it in the rain. On the plus side you can't really ruin cast iron. If it does rust some scrubbing should do the trick. When you are done with it scrub it good while it's still hot, scrub everything off with something rough like steel wool or a wire brush, wipe it down with paper towels, and put a thin layer of grease, oil, or if you feel like spending money buy some special cast iron conditioner.

I think the pre-seasoning kind of sucks. So I'd save up a good amount of grease from cooking (or again by the cast iron conditioner) before you use it the first time. Set the heat on low and just keep applying thin layers to it as you heat it up, don't put so much on it starts to pool but don't let any spots dry out either. It's a hassle but if you do this for a hour or two nothing will stick to it for years to come. As an alternative when you use it for the first time you could just a lot of nice thick cut bacon and get the same result.

The only reason I'm not giving this 5 stars is the defuser plates don't do much, you clearly get very hot spots right under the burners while the edges aren't even hot enough to cook on.

title: I am so in love with this cupcake holder
text:
I am so in love with this cupcake holder. I was pleasantly surprised to see how well it was made. I have spent a long time searching for the right holder and most are very flimsy and the tops to secure well. That is not the case with this one. The tiered pieces and the cover are a heavier duty plastic. It also assembles very quickly. The tiered pieces have a twist-lock set-up so that they are super secured once you put them together and they easily come apart for smaller storage. The top was also very easy to use. It uses a basic sliding motion to extend to the full height required for all three tiers. The third tier screw into the base which has the locks and the top slips over and you just pop the metal clasp and you're ready to go. It felt very secure when I was carrying it by the handles, it didn't feel like the bottom would fall out. I was also surprised that with all three tiers filled, the cover cleanly went over without smudging any frosting. The only note I would have is that the little divots where the cupcakes sit are for large sized ones only. If you put mini cupcakes in there they would definitely move around or fall over. You would have to use extra care if that is what you're transporting.

The item shipped with plenty of filling to ensure that the items would make it in one piece. It arrived on time, even with expedited shipping. I would definitely order from this vendor again.

title: A Decent Looking Bed, A Few Disappointments
text:
I really like the looks of this bed if you squint a little and look at it from a ways off. I have owned a couple of very nice wrought iron beds and really liked the looks but they were higher quality than this one. I got a couple disappointments when I put it together. The biggest of which is that my rigid box spring could not fit the bed lengthwise. I ended up having to shift box springs around to get one that would fit the bed.

Set up was quick and easy. I'm not sure why this is called a snap bed, or why the video advertisement says the pieces snap into place. There is nothing that snaps, but it is an easy construction. 8 screws with the needed allen wrench included is nice. The pieces fit together fine, and while this is not the sturdiest bed I've owned, it is as good as most inexpensive head and foot boards that attach to a bed frame.

The finish is a painted on fake brushed nickel. There were two voids in the paint on mine and the threat that it can be scratched off. The welds are large and rough, perhaps that was a look they were going for, but they are amateurish enough to look less elegant. All in all, it's an OK bed, just not as good as I would have hoped from the photos and video.

title: Useless, Disappointed, Should not have purchased
text:
I live in a ranch, all hardwood floors except 1-5x9 area rug, 1 cat. I am 100% dissatisfied with this purchase. Why? I did not expect this unit to keep my house spotless but I did expect it to be able to help lessen my cleaning during the week. It does NOT. I have to pre-sweep and post sweep and sweep during its run time. It is totally useless. If you have a cat, have hardwood floors, you understand that cat litter is a problem. It does not have the ability to pick up cat litter unless you pre-sweep to localize the dirt, then as roomba runs over these little piles, the spinning brush will scatter the litter, if you're lucky and the brush misses the pile, it DOES NOT have enough suction to pick up 99% of the litter, so keep sweeping into little piles throughout its run time. Then when it's battery dies break out a regular vacuum and just go over everything. This unit DOES NOT have any kind of intelligence, it'll go to one area and keep going back to this area over and over and over. If your home has any normal home funishings, ie wood, this thing will smash, and I honestly mean SMASH, into everything dark, ie wood, or glass without mercy for itself or your funishings. The sensors are useless except on white or tan colored items. This was a TOTAL WASTE OF MONEY.
All these great reviews...I don't understand, either I got a lemon or these people don't have a cat, don't have hardwood floors or live where they don't mind doing all the extra work. For the money I spent on this, it should be able to pick up cat litter without all the extra work, it should NOT smash into every piece of furniture I own and it shouldn't be as STUPID as much as it is.
Honestly, don't buy it if your home is anything near my interior setup, you will be disappointed.

text:

I used Paris Grey Annie Sloan chalk paint on a soft white bedroom wall - it was so so easy - and fast - to bring texture, depth, beauty, and romance to the bedroom. I wanted a subtle look so I used a fairly dry sponge roller over the stamp, then I pressed the stamp itself to the wall. The Original Wall Stamp is very forgiving: my "mistakes" become part of the charm of the finished look.

I have plans to use this stamp over some ugly tile in the bathroom of a rental property to bring that room back to life at very low cost and effort. And today I ordered another design from the Original Stamp Company; I figured you can't have too much of a good thing to add to my up-cycling supplies.

title: Great protection from accidents!
text:
Excellent protection! We have a cat who has decided to show his displeasure with us by urinating on our bed, usually in the wee hours of the morning. We have a waterproof mattress cover, but that entails washing the comforter, all the sheets and the mattress cover. So I thought I would try this to see how it would work out. I purchased a lightweight down comforter to place inside and an inexpensive duvet cover to go over it. We had our first accident this morning and it worked perfectly! I could tell there was an issue from the weight on my foot, so I slowly got out of bed and felt the top duvet cover and it was damp. I don't know how long it had been like that, but the cat was no where to be seen so it wasn't immediate. We carefully stripped off the top duvet and then mopped up the remaining liquid on the Floppy Ears duvet. I think the only flaw in this design is that it is not really absorbent, so the liquid pools up on it and can spill off if you aren't careful. But nothing spilled off and I was able to relatively easily untie the internal comforter without making a mess and remove it. This was the first time we haven't needed to fully strip the bed and do two loads of laundry!

As far as the breathability goes, it really isn't that great - but it is hard to comment just on this because I had a second duvet cover and a light down comforter inside. My regular duvet cover didn't have anywhere to tie in the corners, so this slipped around a lot inside - this was our first use so I am going to remedy that after washing. I think we will try just the Floppy Ears duvet inside the regular duvet for the next try since it is summer. In the winter we will need more warmth from the comforter. My husband was a little daunted by the complexities of untying and unzipping, but it is so much easier than washing everything (and getting wet ourselves!) - he just needs to actually use the products himself once and he won't have any issues.

The zipper opening was very large and easily allowed me to place the comforter inside without much difficulty. The ties are long and easy to use, very convenient that there are ties on both the inside and outside.

I highly recommend this if you have pets or little ones that tend to have accidents on your beds. A great upgrade would be to improve the absorbency of it.

title: Pleasantly surprised! Improved taste of water from old pipes.
text:
I work in a historical building in DC with less than stellar plumbing and the hard-lined water cooler I have to fill my bottle from is an improvement over the tap but still has that slightly tangy dingy metallic aftertaste. Within a minute or so of putting this little filter bag into a 40oz bottle, the metallic taste is totally gone. Not sure how to explain that doesn't sound hinky but I'm very pleased with the product and will purchase again when this one wears out. So far have used the same filter bag in about ten refills of the 40oz bottle and it still seems to be very effective at neutralizing the unpleasant qualities of the water at work. Had a slight powdery residue before first use but I do not rinse it prior to use and noticed no grit or anything in the water.

Update: After using this product for the past several months, I have a couple things to say:

This is the third time I am buying this product - I find it continually and impressively effective at improveing the taste ( and thus am assuming the quality) of the water I drink at work and home.

With regularly use (for me, thats about 2 fills of a 40 ounce bottle, 4-5 days per week) the filter is very effective for about two to three weeks and gradually you will notice the water taste improvement lessen over the third and fourth week. Therefore I use about 1 filter per month, 2 if my husband uses one as well.

And lastly, I haven't had to remove or dry the filter between uses. I occasionally set it aside to wash the hydroflask bottle but then put it right back in with water and have noticed no scent or tatse to suggest that it might spoil, mildew or mold. Being mineral based this makes sense but just an additional observation.

text:
I purchased this specifically to use as a "sea salt shaker" and it works very well. My new kitchen colors are "cobalt blue" so this piece works in very well with my cobalt blue cannisters and other cobalt blue items in the kitchen. My standard salt shakers hardly shake out any sea salt, but it comes out of the top of this shaker very easily. In fact, the only problem is that I have to avoid "shaking" the salt out, because it pours out of this shaker too easily. Still, it has been my best solution so far for using sea salt instead of regular iodized salt, and I love that I finally have a way to cook easily with sea salt in my new kitchen.

The only caveat I have about these "new" Mosser glass items is that the tops do not set well on any of them.
