title: Surprisingly comfortable, structurally sound.
text:
I bought this as a temporary bed when I moved into a new apartment. I didn't want a cheap "camping-type" air mattress, I wanted something a little higher-end that would last. Honestly? This is surprisingly comfortable and for the price you can't go wrong. I love how it has a built-in inflation system, it took less than 3 minutes to fully inflate. And if it's too firm for you, you can turn a dial to let out as much air as you like.

Now, after I got my cat, I realized that it had a slow leak . . . somewhere. I'm sure the leak was from my cat's nails, because I had been sleeping on the mattress for two months and had no issues. I wasn't able to actually find the leak, but it was a super slow one and I never woke up in the middle of the night on the floor or anything. Maybe in a much squishier bed than I started with earlier in the evening, but it's structurally sound enough that it kept its shape even without as much air in it.

A few weeks after the slow leak, I got a real bed, and deflating this mattress was a snap. Should I have guests in the future, I'll definitely use it, slow leak and all. As I said, it's not that big of a deal.

Overall, if you're looking for a high-quality, surprisingly comfortable air mattress, for a great price, I highly recommend this one.

All of them said that it could take months for Panasonic to respond to warranty part requests and would refuse to let the shops use parts that were not specifically sent from Panasonic as requested.  According to two of the shops, we could bring our microwave in, but should be prepared to be without it for at least 6 months.  At this point, we went to Target and bought a new one. Now to the Bissell: I bought one of these after being disgusted with the RD's performance. I was AMAZED. Attached is a picture of what the RD left behind just a few weeks ago.
You will use a fraction of the water. I did my whole living room traffic pattern on one tank with the Bissel and it wasn't even full. It took me 4 fills with the RD.
You will be able to walk on the carpet in stocking feet immediately after using if you follow the instructions.
Cleaning the unit is super easy. There is a YouTube video of how to service your machine each time. If you have PETS you must do this every time. I vacuumed 4 times with my Dyson Animal and I still had this machine pull gobs of hair out of the carpet.
BOTH bottles come out so you can clean and dry them every single time.
It is QUIET. The cats didn't even leave the room. After using the RD the cats avoided the carpet for over a day due to the wetness. They walked on and laid on the carpet right after I was done with the Bissell.
The cord is detachable so if you have a HUGE house you can swap out the cord for a 100 footter!

text:
This model is working well with my current household of a dog and cat who love to shed! I think the results are on par with the heavy carpet cleaners you rent from the grocery store or big box, and in the long run I have already paid for this vs. rental. A few tricks I would suggest

1. The top water container seems to leak a bit when you start out if it is filled to the mark, I now tend to underfill it a bit. Of course it is leaking on the carpet you are cleaning, so it's not the end of the world. And it stops once some of the water has been used.

2. Maintenance goes a long way! Take the extra few minutes after your cleaning to clean the brushes and the components. There is a special cleaning tool that is actually helpful for getting the hair/wet dust out of the front structure. It took me a while to figure out how to remove the front part and I still struggle with it. Also, clean the brush area, simply spin slowly and so much crud will fall out!

I have been using the Anti-AllergenPlus cleaner by Hoover rather than the Bissell brand. I am scent sensitive and didn't want to take a chance with a scented product. I use way less than recommended. As someone else noted, just using hot water has amazing results. I also spot clean for stubborn stains using Mrs. Meyers carpet cleaner, or the Nature's Miracle pet enzymes (original formula) when appropriate.

I have to say that this has been a very comfortable solution for me personally. I have sciatica and other spinal issues and this bed is a joy for me. I assume my guests will all love it, as well.

Although the long-term durability of the bed can't be judged yet, assuming it holds together without leaks a good long time (making it worth the investment / price I paid) so far, I am quite happy with the ease of setup, quality of construction, and sleeping comfort.

text:

After holding scraps of my lunch all afternoon at room temperature I want to be sure my bento box is as clean as possible. On page 3 of the instruction box at the top of the page it clearly states: "Your Bentgo is -completely- dishwasher safe" but at the bottom of the -same- page it states "It is not recommended to microwave or dishwash the Bentgo top lid or divider lid." So which is it, guys? I can tell you, with a warped lid that does not seal, you'd better heed the warning.

And say you do bring lunch to work and want to warm it up. The natural thing would be to loosen the lid but use it to contain splatters in the microwave. Nope. Bring along a roll of saran wrap to work? Cover your food with a paper towel? Seriously?

So this is another case of a product much more concerned about looking pretty than being functional. And the instruction book? Well, that's just a case of the company putting a spin on the design failure. I contacted the company with this problem with no success.

title: I was extremely eager to get this as I do love my cup of joe in the morning and the ...
text:
I got my Contigo Autoseal west loop stainless steel mug today! I was extremely eager to get this as I do love my cup of joe in the morning and the countless of starbucks mugs (that are not worth the money...) have all been thrown out. I also got the tea infuser that you have to buy separately. As soon as I got the mug, I took off all the wrappings, glanced over the instructions, stuck the tea infuser in, poured in some hot water and began my test. Here are my first impressions:

Pros: The mug is definitely great quality. The weight and feel of the mug definitely seems premium. I have two small children in the house, so being able to lock the opening is a great bonus and I'm sure will come in quite handy in the future. I love how it is easy to clean off as well. It's just a all around great travel mug!

Cons: Here are a few things for you to consider before buying this to make sure it is not a deal breaker for you! Finger prints... Because it is stainless steal, the mug itself is a fingerprint magnet. I got the black mug, hoping that the fingerprints would be less visible; it's still visible... This is not a deal breaker for me but it could be for you, hense the critic. The bigger critic for me, that almost made me return the mug, is the opening. I love my coffee hot. This mug does an exceptional job keeping it hot for the duration of the day. Unfortunately, the opening on the lid is shallow, which makes it hard for me to control the flow of the liquid. It might just be me, but this causes me to burn my lip and tongue constantly using this mug... I find myself having to open the lid and cool down the coffee/tea before being able to drink from it. Lots of anxiety tilting this thing to drink...

Overall, a great mug! If the could deepen the opening a little to give better control, I think this would have been the perfect mug for me.

title: My first week with the humidifier...
text: As the reviews were a little over the place, wanted to add my 2 cents.  Long review, more a first hand experience. I think it's very important to match experience with setting, so I'm using this is in a larger house (5bedrooms) that is more of an open floor plan, and high ceilings in a good part of the house (18').  That said, the house was very dry when I started the humidifier: 22%.  Based on some reviews I expected that within a couple of hours it would be tropical humidity.  I put the system in the center of the house (area with high ceiling), and on maximum.  I had to refill every few hours, it took a good 5 or 6 hours to get to about 27%.  The fan is pretty loud on high, so at night I lowered it to low, and refilled before going to bed.  By morning both tanks were empty and humidity was at about 30%.  After a good 24 hours, it was 33%. Since then I've kept the humidity setting to just a bit higher than the first level and fan on low, and it has kept humidity about 33-34%.  I refill at least a couple of times a day.  I forgot to refill last night, by morning it was 26%.  On the noise level. When I first turned on the fan, I did hear a VERY annoying vibration, low hum at the lowest fan speed as some reviews have mentioned.  I almost decided right then and there, that I would return it.  But after using it for a day, by evening that noise was pretty much gone. Also every couple of days, I flip the filter upside down, seems the top of the filter sometime gets a bit yellow and dry, and by turning it, makes it, I feel, wet more evenly.  I wish there was a way to see the level of water in the tanks (you can only see the last 3", which on a system like that doesn't last long for my setting)

title: Replacing the old wooden clothing rack.....
text:
I am a 32y/o female. I have used drying racks for a long time to stop my clothes from shrinking. Primarily just shirts. I dry my pants in the dryer. I had been using a wooden rack for years and I was just over it. The rack was a good size but the white paint from the rack just littered the floor. No sooner than I cleaned it up I would look over and more white paint littering the floor. I decided that I wanted to try a metal rack so I bought this.

I was a little worried when I saw all the parts in the box. However, it really was very easy to assemble. No tools. The rack bars just snap into place. I had it up and together probably in about 10 minutes. It has anti skid tips on the bottom which I like. I don't want it to slide but I also don't need something to tear up my floor.

I am happy with this rack. It is attractive and sturdy enough to hold my clothes and even my rugs when I run them through the washer.
The only change I would really make if I could is to make it wider. My wooden rack was wider and I miss that. However, I am a large woman so for most people this rack would be plenty wide

title: I liked the size
text:
OK. I almost never review products here, but this was such a bizarre situation, decided I would warn others.

I purchased this for my husband as a gift. I researched a ton prior. This unit was well reviewed by a few sous vide chefs. I liked the size, as we do not plan on using it often, so wanted something easy to store. It arrived, and we used it for our first successful long cook with our Anova. Super easy, great seal, fast, easy to clean and store. At the time, seemed like a wise purchase.

A few months later, I went to use it again and it was dead. I placed it on the charger overnight, suspicious as no light came on the cradle, but hopeful. The next day, nothing.

So I contacted Waring. I received a lovely reply, saying I could mail the unit back for replacement, but unless the unit is charged monthly, it loses the ability to recharge and dies permanently. Thus I needed to charge my new unit once a month to have it work. I replied that I had somewhere I could store it plugged in permanently, but the rep replied that would also kill the battery. It needed to be charged monthly.

I am a fairly organized person and have monthly tasks -- dog's heart worm pills, cleaning the light switches, etc. But adding charing the pistol vac is not something I want to do. We own this now, so will see how long I can keep it up. But until they fix this issue, unless you have a Martha Stewart type calendar and staff, perhaps best to avoid purchasing.

I have worked in the metal stamping industry for 30 years and know a little about burrs and sharp edges. My suggestion is to tumble these plates either part-on-part in a rotary tumbler or use a vibratory deburring tub with a little ceramic media to knock down the potentially harmful sharp edges. If it weren't for the sharp edges, I'd give it 5 stars.

title: Simple, yet elegant.
text:
I have the chaise part of the futon, and I figured, why not get the futon itself?

First of all, this futon is stunning. Everyone that comes over loves the couch and thinks it looks amazing. It has a very simple, yet elegant look.

The assembly took less than five minutes. It was pretty simple and it's hard to mess it up.

There is one major qualm I have about this futon, however. When I extend it into "bed mode", if you lay completely on the "back" side, the futon almost "tips" over. What I'm getting at here is that the futon balance when it's in "bed mode" is off.

I think the way to improve this is to have screw on legs for the back of the couch that will prevent it from tipping over. Like imagine a big tube with a screw head on the tip, and you can screw it in tool-less. It would be a simple addition and I don't think it would add too much cost to the futon. This is the only thing that prevented the futon from getting 5 stars. Other than that, I love it!

USAGE UPDATE: After 9 months of NORMAL use, the futon has started to falter. I have not used this futon for sleeping and I don't have guests over too often. I have no idea how this happened and I have no idea how to fix it. It seems like the foam has collapsed on one side, and over-expanded on the other. I am disappointed that it broke down after 9 months. I have withdrawn my 4 star rating and have changed it to a 2 star rating. I have uploaded a picture of the problem.

title: All around it's a nicely designed, easy to use, alternative to slaving over the hot stove
text: If JJ Abrams stopped making movies like Star Wars, Star Trek and Mission Impossible and went into designing really cool and smart kitchen appliances, the GCR 1700 would be right up his alley. It looks like the love child of R2D2 and BB8 and works as smoothly as the plot of The Force Awakens. Ok enough with the homage to JJ & SW, let's just say when I first came across this during one of my Amazon appliance "surfs" I felt a "stir" in the force. because this seemed to solve a lot of problems that have been keeping me out of the kitchen. First it's pretty much self contained--a real all in one cooking device which for our family makes way more sense  than a stove does. Everything happens inside the domed lid, so no spattering, spills etc...next it's all pre programmed, so there's no guessing with dials, timers and settings, the Gourmia people set this up so it does it all at the proverbial  push of a button; grilling, baking (my mini corn muffins were a hit) ,  steaming, pan frying, roasting--it' all there and ready to go. Though what really makes it a game changer as far as I'm concerned, is it's "robo" ness in the stir, sauté and "anything that needs to be kept moving while cooking" department. One you put in the ingredients, it's not just hands free but also worry free, the stirring paddles "cover" everything so between the non stick surface and the smart paddles doing their thing there's no worries about scorching--just be sure to rinse all the parts and cooking surfaces really well before your first trip into robo cook land as we learned the hard way a few years ago what happens when you don't rinse non stick cookware before "the first time". All around it's a nicely designed, easy to use, alternative to slaving over the hot stove, and the fact that it looks like a natural for the Millenium Falcon doesn't hurt!

title: They came out great! You really wouldn't know that they were window ...
text:
I bought 3 of the "Old English" design and was able to cover 4 small windows with them. They came out great! You really wouldn't know that they were window films unless you got right up close and examined them. They really look like in the company's professional photos.

I have attached my "before and after" pics of 2 rooms so you can see how much of the unattractive view behind my house is blocked out while still allowing light into these rooms. I had narrowed my design choices down to this one and a floral one but I am really glad I ultimately chose this one because it really does look like a legit frosted window and it goes well mith my decor.

They were quite easy to put up. The measuring and cutting of the film sheet took longer than the actual installation. I followed the directions and they worked like a charm. The film is very substantial feeling, not at all flimsy to handle. It is easy enough to manage it without it folding over onto itself while you're trying to get it up onto the window. If you get it on wrong, you can easily lift it up and re-do since there's no actual adhesive on it, just a cling effect to keep it on.

One piece of advice I would give is if you cut the sheet, put the factory cut side on the bottom of your window and your scissors-cut side at the top where there's less chance for anyone to see it. Most of us don't have a super long straight-edge ruler and a table that you'd want to use a sharp knife on, so most likely you'll be using scissors like me. Since your cut line won't be perfect, put it at the top. I ended up finding this out the hard way when I saw a gap of light coming through at the bottom of my film. I just peeled it up and re-did it. Now I have the nice even edge lined up with my window at the bottom.

I am very happy with this product so far and would definitely recommend it!

title: Legitimate natural wood and rattan stools that look nice, but are not constructed very well.
text:
We bought six of these stools, and have three young children using them daily in a breakfast nook. After a few months of daily use, unfortunately they have become a bit loose and rickety due to all the construction joints loosening up a bit. They still look nice- and the top woven rattan material is holding up just fine- and the wood finish is surprisingly durable for the price and cleans nicely. I may spend 20 minutes and just tighten up all the screws and maybe throw a few strategically placed brad nails in the joints to tighten everything up a bit.

If the manufacturer would have used larger corner blocks on the inside of the top seat when putting this together, it would be a stronger stool and would likely not be as loose now. But honestly, for the price we paid for a two-pack of genuine wood stools with a genuine rattan top (not plastic woven strands like many others I have seen), it is worth the 20 minutes it will take me to improve these. Just keep that in mind when purchasing- there is a reason they are so affordable- fortunately for me, it's not because they skimped on material quality, just on construction quality.

I tried flipping it over to the soft side that did not help. Then the to layers came apart on me. I could now pull it apart no problem. The glue or whatever they used to hold the 2 sections just came apart. I can live with that but I could not live with the lost support it had when I first got it.. So this mattress is really only good for about 3 months.. I am a 6 foot 2 man and weigh 220 pounds. This is about the 5th foam type bed I have tried. If you do not have any back problems and do not mind a soft feeling bed you might like this. If you need something firm for support do not buy ANY of these type mattress. My opinion is these companys are really pushing these type beds because of profits! They make a lot of money on these in savings on shipping and convinance. Not having to pay a delivery service to set up a real bed... I am going to be using this bed as packing material to ship items. Because not only has the 2 sections come apart the foam is now very easy to tear with your hands. Will make for good packing stuff for shipping that is all this bed is worth after 3 months. This is my opinion only that I am sharing. You may have a great expieriance with this. for me it was a waist of money.

title: Love it!
text:
I am sold on these, but... Forget about the window kit. Be a pro and install these through the wall. It only takes a 5" hole. Unless you are renting. For homeowners, just prep each room you intend on using these. Get one of those really long 1/2" drill bits that can do masonry and wood. One drill through and hammer the rest once you get the hole. These are more efficient through the wall. Less loss. Plus they look nicer this way. I bought 2 of these and prepped 3 areas. Family room, living room, and master bedroom. Now I can move one and plug in to the other real easy.
We just went through our first heat wave, temps in the 90's. With 2 running, they lowered the inside temp about a degree an hour and more importantly made us comfortable. Ok, it is not like an ice cold central air, but I guess if you buy enough of these it will be. The reason to buy these portable AC's is for efficiency. I can run 1 or 2 of these steady for a fraction of the cost of a central AC. In my Family Room, I went through the fireplace, works good since mine is sealed off a long time ago and I installed an electric fireplace in front back then.
For those of you with a broken central AC and you like to conserve, you may consider doing this, rather than spending $5500 on a new AC, and then spending an extra $200 a month just to use it.
Btw Before deciding on these, I was planning on doing 3 mini split AC installs. This would have taken me a month to install and would have been very difficult and cost $4500 total or more. I got basically the same result here with just a few hours work to make these portable AC's look better, with a fraction of cost.

title: Experiments and Research on Safety: UV/Lead/Mercury
text:
I am very paranoid as an expecting father -- that is why I got this in the first place. It shocked me that the manual said the cord has lead and the uv bulb has mercury. I do not care much about lead cause it is everywhere and it does not volatile. However mercury really scares me -- if the bulb was leaking mercury vapor -- that is going to be worse than any bad air -- it will destroy the nerves of ur family.

I had to figure out the following questions:
1. how do I know if the bulb is working .. the blue decoration light WILL light up even if you remove the UV bulb!!!!!
2. How do I know of the bulb is leaking mercury .... how much mercury does it have in the bulb?

I emailed the guardian customer support and they give me the following answers:
1. there is less than 5mg mercury in the bulb --- which if turned to vapor is still way too much in one room.
2. if the bulb is broken,it would not light up, cause it requires vacuum in the bulb.

I also emailed AWAIR customer service, cause I have an AWAIR air monitor, and they said mercury vapor cannot be detected.

So the only way to all the questions seem to be to figure out if the UV bulb is lighting up -- if it is, then the bulb is sealed and assuming no leaks were happening.

So I emailed em again -- they said in order to check if the UV bulb is lighting up, I need to remove the back frame and the filter, and disable two safety locks (top and bottom), and light the UV light to see if it is working -- as said in other reviews.

This is a bad idea cause you are not supposed to look into UV lights... I end up did all they suggested but used an camera instead of looking into it. Finally I was able to see the glow blue light inside the UV unit from video taped. After seeing that, I realize you can actually see the uv light from the top of the back, behind the very top of the filter, with both filer and back frame on -- so whoever wants to verify it, there is no need to remove anything. Notice that the uv light is a different tone comparing to the blue decoration light in the front, it was lighter blue. Still it is a very stupid idea to have a blue decoration light on the unit. If I had not did the test without the frame and filter, I would not know the blue glow was from the UV light, not the decoration light.

Overall it was not easy to find peace of mind and assurance of safety. Containing mercury in a air purifier is also fundamentally flawed IMO.

text:
I just received this today, and I think I'm really going to like it. It is more than large enough for my normal-sized sewing machine. The smaller cases did not have wheels, and I already have one of those that came with my machine. The extra space should allow plenty of room for accessories and projects. I was a bit concerned because one or more reviews mentioned it didn't have enough padding. I would give it four stars if it had thicker padding; however, if you analyze the bag, the outside pockets on the front and either side are also padded, so that gives you an extra layer in addition to the padding in the bag. I will probably cover a piece of 1/2" foam in black nylon, and stick it behind the machine since the back doesn't offer as much protection.

There are plenty of outside pockets which are padded, two inside zippered pockets are attached to the back with velcro and can be removed. They are not padded. There is also a zippered mesh pocket on the inside of the top, but it is only about half the size of the top. I'm not sure why they didn't make that the entire width of the top. The front and back handles have a vinyl grip that fastens around both handles, much like some luggage. They seem sturdy enough. The telescoping handle is easy to pull up and retract. The color is darker than it appears in the photo, although not dark by any means. I was glad to see that, as I was concerned about it showing dirt or marks easily if too light in color. The wheels appear to roll easily.

Since I haven't used it yet, I will be sure to update this review if there are any changes after I've used it a few times.

title: Comparison of Taylor 5925N and CDN FG80  Thermometers
text:
I bought four refrigerator/freezer thermometers to measure my kitchen and garage refrigerator/freezers. I bought two each of the Taylor 5925 and the CDN FG80 models. It wasn’t clear to me from the reviews why I should prefer one over the other.

The thermometers are nearly identical in size and construction. The CDN FG80 covers a slightly wider temperature range 80° F on the high end vs 74° F for the Taylor, and -40° F vs. -28° F on the low end. Unless you are measuring something colder or warmer than the usual freezer or refrigerator, this is an advantage for the Taylor thermometer, since the markings for the interesting temperature range are correspondingly larger. The Taylor range is -34 C to + 30 C. The CDN range is -50 C to + 34 C.

Accuracy seemed not to be a factor. I compared all four units at room temperature and in the refrigerator, and they all agreed to within a degree or so. I did the ice water test with a sample of each model. A mixture of ice and water that has reached equilibrium will be at 0 C or 32 F. I put the thermometers (one at a time) in a plastic zip lock bag, and immersed the bulb end in ice water for 15 minutes. They both read 34 F. This may be due to experimental error, since the entire thermometer was not immersed, and there was some air in the bag. This was a big improvement over my old dial-and-pointer thermometer which I threw away after it was off by over 10 degrees F in the same test.

There is a narrow viewing angle at which the red temperature line is greatly magnified and easy to read. This seemed about the same on both models. I liked the brightly colored temperature zones on the Taylor 5925N.

They both have metal clips on the back. The Taylor also has suction cups which can fit on the clips. The CDN clips are tight against the back of the thermometer. I had to bend them out with pliers to hang on a wire basket in one case, and to make it stand upright on a flat surface in the other case. I don’t see how you could ever mount the CDN without bending those or using something else to attach it. I considered attaching it with wire ties. The clips on the Taylor are more useful. In one case, it clipped onto the front edge of a wire shelf. In the other case, I used the suction cups.

When I bought these, the Taylor was about a dollar less. The Taylor 5925N would be my pick for a freezer/refrigerator thermometer.

title: Effective slicer, but be careful!
text:
I’ve been trying out all sorts of different slicing / julienne tools to see which one I like best. I’ve now used a benriner, julienne peeler, spiralizer (hand crank version), a spiral slicer (pencil sharpen version), food processor blades and now this mandoline.

Of all the types, I find this mandoline and the benriner to be the most versatile. They are both very similar in form. The benriner is just a Japanese brand of mandoline that a cooking teacher of mine had recommended. I find changing plates is a little easier with a mandoline than the benriner but the benriner has a more compact form if space is an issue.

The mandoline and benriner also seem to be the most dangerous to use. I’ve sliced my finger quite a few times on the benriner due to slippage, and this feels similar. I bought metal mesh gloves to use with my benriner and I would definitely recommend doing the same with this mandoline. The hand guard is a must-use if you don’t have one, or else I’d grip as high up the vegetable as you can.

I like that the mandoline has a stand that lets you prop it at an angle. With the benriner I had to slant it against a bowl. The handle grip for this mandolin was comfortable to hold and the rubber feet are a nice touch. In terms of sharpness, the mandolin seemed decent. I had to apply a bit of pressure but my onion sliced fairly effortlessly.

In terms of price, this product seems to be competitive with other slicers of the same type. You’re not paying for extra packaging or anything as this product comes in a non-descript white box and the product comes in bubble wrap. I wish there were instructions included but you do get them via a separate email. Most of the slicer is made of plastic so it’s not as sturdy as say a de Buyer mandolin with a lot more metal parts, but then again you’re not paying $150. I actually don’t think it’s worth paying a lot for these types of tools because the blades don’t stay that sharp for long (I replaced my benriner about once a year) and you WANT your blades to be as sharp as possible while slicing! Between this design and the OXO design I like that the OXO lets you pick the cutting type and then turn a dial to adjust the thickness, but this might be simpler in terms of picking the right attachment to get the thickness and width. The 4 blade holder is nice for safety, but the blades don’t lock in and can slide out if held upside down.

Of the other types of vegetable prep tools, I found the spiral sharpeners the easiest to use. You stick your vegetables in, twist like you’re sharpening a pencil and out comes noodles. It only has two types of slicers though so it’s not as versatile as the mandolin and cleanup is a bit of a pain as the food gets caught in the middle.

Spiralizers (hand crank) and food processors are the fastest for me, but the most cleanup and the bulkiest, while julienne peelers are the most labour intensive but handiest for irregular shapes.

Overall I think this is a great tool at a decent price. There are some minor areas of improvement (like having the extra blades lock into the holder) and having the labels on the blades larger (they are so tiny I missed them initially). I received a review sample of this product for my opinion, but would buy this again when the blades get dull.

title: The ultimate travel air purifier
text:
I own two IQAir Health Mate Pros, which are the most effective air cleaners available, but a little bulky for trying to take on an airplane. When this came out, I had to give it a try. Happy to say that I've traveled with it three times, just packed in a bag, and it has given me blissful sleep on the pillows, sheets, and mattresses where I was staying.

You need to set this up close to your head. It's not meant to clean the room, but to produce a zone of clean air around your head. On the highest of the three settings, it's audible, but that's about all. On the two lower settings the sound is barely noticeable.

The quirks: (it wouldn't be IQAir without quirks) First, you plug the cord into the side of the unit and into the wall. You may need an extension cord in some hotel rooms, to run the power from the outlet to your face. The cord is reasonably long, but for some hotel rooms may just not be long enough. So bring an extension cord.

The stand is actually cool. But, when you attach the disc-shaped unit to the stand, it doesn't really CLICK into place. Rather, it SLIPS into place. Result: If you try to pick up and move the unit, the stand may fall off. It'd be nice if it had some kind of positive attachment to the lozenge.

I have no idea, obviously, how long the filter will last. I do know that I'm really glad to have this, and believe it will open up a world of travel that I thought I had lost.

Edit: After a few months of ownership, I decided to try using this in my bedroom, every night, to help me sleep. The good news is that it works as well at home as it did in a hotel room. The bad news is that the filters don't last long at all. I run it on the highest speed, 3, for about 8 hours each night, and after about a month I'm starting to clog up and wake up coughing. Nor is it a slow decline. Rather, one night I'm fine, one night I struggle, and then it's hopeless. Too bad. But if you look at the filters you can see that they are rather small, without much surface area, and so it's no surprise that they fill up quickly.

Once again, others whose allergies are somewhat less savage than mine may get more out of each filter. But this will be my travel filter rather than every day. I will not reduce the rating, because this was an unknown rather than an expectation, and this will still be the ultimate travel air purifier. But if you use it for travel, you may want to track the number of hours use, and when you get near to 250, swap it out if you're about to go on the road.

Edit #2: The really interestingly-shaped filter sits inside this thing wrapped around the top and the back side, which I realized might cause problems with filter longevity. Why? Because dust can settle out of the air directly onto the filter, by traveling down. Unlike the big tall house-sized units that I also reviewed. So I started putting a plastic bag over the unit when not in use.

Good news! Doing this about doubles the filter life for me. Going from one month to two months per filter is definitely worth it, given that all I do is put a trash bag over the thing. It still costs me about a dollar a night, but my sleep is so much better that it's worth it.

Edit #3: After about a year of use I noticed that filter life was starting to tank. When you change a filter, you'll notice a second, smaller lift-off cover that has a little curved piece of styrofoam under it. This is the muffler, to reduce the already miniscule amount of sound the unit produces. Trying to clean this made it worse, but removing it entirely resolved the problem, and the unit is barely louder. So you may want to consider ditching this. It doesn't seem to be a replacement part, but I plan to go to the hardware store, buy matching foam, and cut out a replacement. I'll let you know.

title: A no brainer if you've got a Baratza and do any manual brew
text:
This device is an obvious choice for any brew method. (Except espresso) It seems like all modern coffee recipes describe dosages in grams, so if you want to grind fresh beans right before brewing, and you want the correct dosage, and you don't want to waste beans, having the grinder shut off at the correct dosage is a no-brainer.

Frankly, I'm not sure how you would use a Baratza Encore with a full hopper without this thing and get a correct dosage. The Virtuoso and above all have timers so there you have a guide- this you would have to weigh your beans before hand or just guess.

I love that I have three presets- one is set to 17g for Aeropress, another is at 21g for V60, and another is at 42g for Chemex. If you're already spending over $100 on your grinder you might as well just get this as well.

Obviously, if your primary coffee of choice is espresso and you're grinding directly into your portafilter, this thing isn't as necessary. But, for all other methods it really helps you reduce the number of variables you're working with so you can get an accurate pour, an accurate grind, accurate temp without having to worry about getting an accurate dose.

title: Decent Build - For the Price
text:
I bought this set when it went on sale during the Amazon Summer Sale. We have a breakfast bar at our kitchen and we've been dying to find a nice pair of stools to compliment the design.

After doing some research online and generally being unimpressed with the local selection (Target, IKEA, etc), we decided we would go against our normal precautions and buy a set online. Were we satisfied with our decision? Yes and no.

Let's begin with the good:
+ Price
+ Design (The design is basic, but effective.)
+ Height
+ Quality (More to come on this)

And then the bad:
- Quality

So how can Quality be both good and bad? Well, the overall quality is nice - the materials are great, stitching is fantastic, and the leather feels like leather. The bad part is the actual stand. It supports an adult just fine, but its a little more "wobbly" that I would have expected and it can make you think twice about sitting on them for the first time.

Overall though, wobbliness aside, we are impressed with the stools and we got them at a great price.

text:

Easy to assemble

Cons

I herniated two discs in my back at the same time (L4-L5 and L5-S1) and let me tell you this: It sucks. I would not recommend it to anyone. I immediately realized how bad my old chair was on my back, so I ordered a gamer chair with a hard lumbar pillow thinking "hey, this will work. It's designed for gamers. Gamers sit ALL THE TIME. I just need it for watching Hulu at night with my wife and playing games a few hours on off days." Nope. The chair wobbled and soon tilted and now is almost as bad as the chair I replaced. I saw this chair and after reading mostly positive but still somewhat mixed reviews I went for it. I'm glad I did.

First let's talk Assembly.
This chair is easy to assemble. Like, really easy. I have assembled many computer chairs and desks in my life. This chair is the easiest I have ever assembled. The instructions are clean and concise (Although let's be honest, you could probably figure out how to assemble a chair on your own) and each step has its own page, making it really easy to keep up with where you are in the process. Each step has a full size picture too. The design of the chair is brilliant in that when you put the arms on the base, they make cups for the back to sit in. Also, PRO TIP: AFTER YOU UNBOX EXERYTHING DON'T IMMEDIATELY THROW THE BOX AWAY. Close it back up and use the box as a table to assemble the chair. When the seat of the chair is on the box, it keeps it at a comfortable working height and allows enough room on each side to easily and quickly attach the arm rests. AND if you have a drill with the right size bit, use that for assembly set on medium torque. Saves time and ensures you don't over tighten if you are heavy handed like me.
TOTAL ASSEMBLY TIME: <15 MINUTES

Now, let's talk about Design.
The Design is simple and straight forward. No "slope the back to 180 degrees and invert to form a gravity table. Then transform it into a picnic basket with wheels and go to the park with the jet engine attachment". It is just a chair, plain and simple. I like the way the arms are designed because it prevents the possibility of the chair to "sag" or "bend" with use as I see with a lot of chairs that have the L-Shaped support from base to back. The two-bolts-in-back-two-in-base on each side design has seen the most success for me in the long term. Hopefully this will hold true with this chair. The lumbar pad is firm and the adjustment knob is easy to use and fine tune to the exact pressure desired. Perfect for someone with back problems. The base is stable and the casters snap in firmly but easily. The chair raises and lowers easily and is insanely comfortable. PLEASE NOTE: This chair truly is designed for big and tall people. If you aren't big and tall, maybe look elsewhere because at the lowest setting, my feet JUST sit flat on the ground. If I were any shorter, my legs would be dangling. Of course, I guess you could just get a footrest, but either way take note.

Now comfort.
So far the chair is insanely comfortable. The extra padding at the front keeps my legs from falling asleep and the lumbar pillow not only prevents an extra onset of additional back pain but also seems to be alleviating some of the pain. I honestly cannot remember the last time I could sit down without feeling excruciating sciatic pain. Here's a Haiku telling you just how I feel.

Happy tears streaming
my face, now a waterfall
I blossom like spring

The arm rests are a comfortable height. My head actually hits the head rest, though I usually don't have my head that far back. The width is comfortable and it feels stable and sturdy.

Overall
I am so far very pleased. As time goes on I will update if anything changes. Otherwise, As it stands now, you should definitely get this chair if you have back pain. Oh, I didn't even mention yet, THIS CHAIR IS SO AFFORDABLE! I almost projectile vomited all over my screen when I searched "Best office chairs for herniated disc". THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS! What?! for a chair?! But then Amazon had my back (HAHAHA GET IT?!) And I put down the hammer as my piggy bank's eyes went from terror and disbelief to relief and shock, still amazed that I could have ever thought to smash him to pieces for the delicious money inside. Seriously though, if you're still reading this then you obviously are really interested in the chair. Just get this chair.

title: Good machine, customer service not quite so much
text:
Works quite well and is easy to clean and use. Easily portable. Reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is twofold: first, it is quite noisy, especially if you lift it off the carpet. Scares my dog, and he is the reason I bought it.

Second, customer service was not good at all. When I first used it, it worked great for spraying, but I could not get it to suction the water back up. Tried everything, no go. Checked all directions, including the trouble shooting guide. Called customer service and spoke to a nice young man named Adam, whose English was marginal. He insisted that we go through every single step of his troubleshooting guide, none of which was relevant, even though I had told him from the start there was no suction. He finally gave up and referred me to a local store. I called the store before going there, they could not make any suggestions and was told I would have to leave it there. The whole problem was that there was suction at the end of the hose, but not when I attached either tool.

I finally watched the video suggested in the manual, and although not mentioning it specifically, it gave me a clue when the demonstrator indicated you could take off the plastic caps on the tools for cleaning. AHA! I had taken them off when I first set up the machine, thinking they were there for protection in shipping or something similar. No, you must leave them on for the suction to work. A simple thing, and now I feel stupid, but you would think the company would mention this in the manual or in the trouble shooting steps in the manual or on Adam's list!

text: Overall this is a very nice product for a good price. It is aesthetically pleasing, easy to clean, substantial in weight, and makes good French press coffee. (I do wash it by hand, not in the dishwasher, so I can't speak to that.) Why not 5 stars? I've had it 13 months now, and it has held up, doesn't get grounds into the coffee, and looks as good as new, except for the following: The only design flaw is in the top of the handle / press mechanism, which is actually plastic, though it looks like metal. Instead of making it of metal and screwing it into the press mechanism, the manufacturer simply glued about a 3" semi-disk onto a <.5" base which is continually used when you execute the press, putting forth a lot of pressure. Predictably, this top semi-disk snapped off, and when I superglued it back, it promptly snapped again. The press is still usable, but that part being gone certainly takes away from the aesthetic beauty of the press. Hope they correct this with future designs.

I bought a couple of these fans last summer and they worked well for us (and still work) so I bought 2 more these for this summer so that I would have them in all the bedrooms and living spaces. These have helped us stay cooler and kept us from dying of heat stroke or something like that. ;-)  This fan has an adjustable height and is made from plastic. It looks rather nice for a fan. I have them in both black and white. It also features oscillation for wide-area cooling.  It has 5 Speeds/Levels of Quiet Control including "White Noise". It also has an auto shut off feature with a 1, 2, 4, & 8 hour option.  It also comes with a remote control that allows you to control the fan without getting up. Anyways, I have 5 of these fans in total. While 2 of them are new the other 3 that I have ran all summer pretty much nonstop and are still working this summer. So with that said, I am very very happy with my purchase and I would recommend these if you are in the market for a fan.

title: No Hardware, Damaged, & Weak Shelves
text: I don't know if I'll be editing this review down or not? At this moment, I am giving it 3 stars. The bookcase isn't even put together yet. The box arrived so beat up one of the major pieces looked like it had been chewed on by a small dog. The worst part was broken "hardware bag" inside. Gapping box holes allowed 80% of the hardware needed to put this together to fall out, what was left that was plastic was broken from the weight. There are big phone numbers listed both on the box and on the included paperwork saying is there are missing or damaged parts or if there isn't any hardware then call the number. Wow... does this happen a lot? It makes you wonder when that's the first printed thing you see! I called the number and French is the language, then Spanish, then English. The entire call was excellent customer service but we have to wait 5-7 business days for shipping, no cost to us for a U.S. mailing and it's coming from Mexico. Otherwise it would have come from Canada. They are replacing all that's damaged and missing. What will happen next? Time will tell. Last but not least was my last shock. The paperwork says each shelf can only support 15 lbs! So if you needed something really strong and dependable I'm not so sure this is it? If I had known 15 lbs per shelf was it I would have kept on looking. Too late now.

title: Organized Space Option
text: Purchased because I like that the "hangers" are black & I have a black chalkboard door to hang on the backside.  It doesn't show much but it is thicker than a metal hanger when considering your clearance to close at the top of your door jam.  The baskets are nice size and they seem to hold weight nicely.  I put several cans in them but it looked as if the rack was bowing in middle.  I switched items around and it seems better.  I need to either screw the bottom to the door or figure out something to keep it from swinging when I open the door.  Otherwise, it freed a lot of space and helped me organize my pantry so I know what I have!

title: Bought these for sporting events for times that they take ...

title: Nonstick flakes off while exterior is still beautiful!
text:
I love that it kept my beverages warm, the top was easy to clean and came apart, the exterior color has lasted for years! I always hand washed it all as we live in an old farm house with no dish washer. It's been dropped countless times and never chipped or leaked.
However, my issue is the non stick interior flaked off and I ended up drinking pieces of it. I wish it was a durable as the exterior. I don't feel safe infesting a coating of any type.
Please make this color with slick steel.
I only put 2 stars because I feel the flaking of the coating is a health issue not just function or aesthetic.

title: Sparks fly!
text: After doing as much research as possible, and because I have had Russell Hobbs products in the past, I chose this toaster when my old one died.  Sadly, I discovered after about a week's use, that when you press the "pop up early" button, a significant spark flies from inside the toaster...and now I am noticing that occasionally this happens even when a regular toasting is being done and the toast pops up.  Caution advised.
